7.8.d: इन्धे राजा समर्यो नमोभिर्यस्य परतीकमाहुतं घर्तेन | नरो हव्येभिरीळते सबाध आग्निरग्र उषसामशोचि ||
7.8.e: THE King whose face is decked with oil is kindled with homage offered by his faithful servant.  The men, the priests adore him with oblations. Agni hath shone forth when the dawn is breaking.

7.8.d: अयमु षय सुमहानवेदि होता मन्द्रो मनुषो यज्वो अग्निः | वि भा अकः सस्र्जानः पर्थिव्यां कर्ष्णपविरोषधीभिर्ववक्षे ||
7.8.e: Yea, he hath been acknowledged as most mighty, the joyous Priest of men, the youthful Agni.  He, spreading o’er the earth, made light around him, and grew among the plants with blackened fellies..

7.8.d: कया नो अग्ने वि वसः सुव्र्क्तिं कामु सवधां रणवः शस्यमानः | कदा भवेम पतयह सुदत्र रायो वन्तारो दुष्टरस्य साधोः ||
7.8.e: How dost thou decorate our hymn, O Agni? What power dost thou exert when thou art lauded?  When, Bounteous God, may we be lords of riches, winners of precious wealth which none may conquer?

7.8.d: पर-परायमग्निर्भरतस्य शर्ण्वे वि यत सूर्यो न रोचतेब्र्हद भाः | अभि यः पूरुं पर्तनासु तस्थौ दयुतानो दैव्यो अतिथिः शुशोच ||
7.8.e: Far famed is this the Bhārata's own Agni he shineth like the Sun with lofty splendour.  He who hath vanquished Pūru in the battle, the heavenly guest hath glowed in full refulgence.

7.8.d: असन्नित तवे आहवनानि भूरि भुवो विश्वेभिः सुमना अनीकैः | सतुतश्चिदग्ने शर्ण्विषे गर्णानः सवयं वर्धस्व तन्वं सुजात ||
7.8.e: Full many oblations are in thee collected: with all thine aspects thou hast waxen gracious.  Thou art already famed as praised and lauded, yet still, O nobly born, increase thy body.

7.8.d: इदं वचः शतसाः संसहस्रमुदग्नये जनिषीष्ट दविबर्हाः | शं यत सतोत्र्भ्य आपये भवाति दयुमदमीवचातनं रक्षोहा ||
7.8.e: Be this my song, that winneth countless treasure, engendered with redoubled force for Agni,  That, splendid, chasing sickness, slaying demons, it may delight our friend and bless the singers.
We, the Vasisthas, now implore thee, Agni, O Son of Strength, the Lord of wealth and riches.  Thou hast brought food to singers and to nobles. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.9.d: अबोधि जार उषसामुपस्थाद धोता मन्द्रः कवितमः पावकः | दधाति केतुमुभयस्य जन्तोर्हव्या देवेषु दरविणं सुक्र्त्सु ||
7.9.e: ROUSED from their bosom is the Dawns' beloved, the joyous Priest, most sapient, Purifier.  He gives a signal both to Gods and mortals, to Gods oblations, riches to the pious.

7.9.d: स सुक्रतुर्यो वि दुरः पणीनां पुनानो अर्कं पुरुभोजसं नः | होता मन्द्रो विशां दमूनास्तिरस्तमो दद्र्शे राम्याणाम ||
7.9.e: Most wise is he who, forcing doors of Paṇis, brought the bright Sun to us who feedeth many.  The cheerful Priest, men's Friend and home-companion, through still night's darkness he is made apparent.

7.9.d: अमूरः कविरदितिर्विवस्वान सुसंसन मित्रो अतिथिः शिवोनः | चित्रभानुरुषसां भात्यग्रे.अपां गर्भः परस्वा विवेश ||
7.9.e: Wise, ne.'er deceived, uncircumscribed, refulgent, our gracious guest, a Friend with good attendants,  Shines forth with wondrous light before the Mornings; the young plants hath he entered, Child of Waters.

7.9.d: ईळेन्यो वो मनुषो युगेषु समनगा अशुचज्जातवेदाः | सुसन्द्र्शा भानुना यो विभाति परति गावः समिधानं बुधन्त ||
7.9.e: Seeking our gatherings, he, your Jātavedas, hath shone adorable through human ages,  Who gleams refulgent with his lovely lustre: the kine have waked to meet him when enkindled.

7.9.d: अग्ने याहि दूत्यं मा रिषण्यो देवानछा बरह्मक्र्ता गणेन | सरस्वतीं मरुतो अश्विनापो यक्षि देवान रत्नधेयायविश्वान ||
7.9.e: Go on thy message to the Gods, and fail not, O Agni, with their band who pray and worship.  Bring all the Gods that they may give us riches, Sarasvatī, the Maruts, Aśvins, Waters.

7.9.d: तवामग्ने समिधानो वसिष्ठो जरूथं हन यक्षि राये पुरन्धिम | पुरुणीथा जातवेदो जरस्व यूयं पात ... ||
7.9.e: Vasiṣṭha, when enkindling thee, O Agni, hath slain jarutha. Give us wealth in plenty.  Sing praise in choral song, O Jātavedas. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.10.d: उषो न जारः पर्थु पाजो अश्रेद दविद्युतद दीद्यच्छोशुचानः | वर्षा हरिः शुचिरा भाति भासा धियो हिन्वान उशतीरजीगः ||
7.10.e: HE hath sent forth, bright, radiant, and refulgent, like the Dawn's Lover, his far-spreading lustre.  Pure in his splendour shines the golden Hero: our longing thoughts hath he aroused and wakened.

7.10.d: सवर्ण वस्तोरुषसामरोचि यज्ञं तन्वाना उशिजो न मन्म | अग्निर्जन्मानि देव आ वि विद्वान दरवद दूतो देवयावा वनिष्ठः ||
7.10.e: He, like the Sun, hath shone while Morn is breaking, and priests who weave the sacrifice sing praises,  Agni, the God, who knows their generations and visits Gods, most bounteous, rapid envoy.

7.10.d: अछा गिरो मतयो देवयन्तीरग्निं यन्ति दरविणं भिक्षमाणाः | सुसन्द्र्शं सुप्रतीकं सवञ्चं हव्यवाहमरतिम्मानुषाणाम ||
7.10.e: Our songs and holy hymns go forth to Agni, seeking the God and asking him for riches,  Him fair to see, of goodly aspect, mighty, men's messenger who carries their oblations.

7.10.d: इन्द्रं नो अग्ने वसुभिः सजोषा रुद्रं रुद्रेभिरा वहा बर्हन्तम | आदित्येभिरदितिं विश्वजन्यां बर्हस्पतिं रक्वभिर्विश्ववारम ||
7.10.e: joined with the Vasus, Agni, bring thou Indra bring hither mighty Rudra with the Rudras,  Aditi good to all men with Ādityas, Bṛhaspati All-bounteous, with the Singers.

7.10.d: मन्द्रं होतारमुशिजो यविष्ठमग्निं विश ईळते अध्वरेषु | स हि कषपावानभवद रयीणामतन्द्रो दूतो यजथाय देवान ||
7.10.e: Men eagerly implore at sacrifices Agni, Most Youthful God, the joyous Herald.  For he is Lord and Ruler over riches, and for Gods’ worship an unwearied envoy.

7.11.d: महानस्यध्वरस्य परकेतो न रते तवदम्र्ता मादयन्ते | आ विश्वेभिः सरथं याहि देवैर्न्यग्ने होता परथमः सदेह ||
7.11.e: GREAT art thou, Agni, sacrifice's Herald: not without thee are deathless Gods made joyful.  Come hither with all Deities about thee here take thy seat, the first, as Priest, O Agni.

7.11.d: तवामीळते अजिरं दूत्याय हविष्मन्तः सदमिन मानुषासः | यस्य देवैरासदो बर्हिरग्ने.अहान्यस्मै सुदिना भवन्ति ||
7.11.e: Men with oblations evermore entreat thee, the swift, to undertake an envoy's duty.  He on whose sacred grass with Gods thou sittest, to him, O Agni, are the days propitious.

7.11.d: तरिश्चिदक्तोः पर चिकितुर्वसूनि तवे अन्तर्दाशुषे मर्त्याय | मनुष्वदग्न इह यक्षि देवान भवा नो दूतो अधिशस्तिपावा ||
7.11.e: Three times a day in thee are shown the treasures sent for the mortal who presents oblation.  Bring the Gods hither like a man, O Agni: be thou our envoy, guarding us from curses.

7.11.d: अग्निरीशे बर्हतो अध्वरस्याग्निर्विश्वस्य हविषः कर्तस्य | करतुं हयस्य वसवो जुषन्ताथा देवा दधिरे हव्यवाहम ||
7.11.e: Lord of the lofty sacrifice is Agni, Agni is Lord of every gift presented.  The Vasus were contented with his wisdom, so the Gods made him their oblationbearer.

7.11.d: आग्ने वह हविरद्याय देवानिन्द्रज्येष्ठास इह मादयन्ताम | इमं यज्ञं दिवि देवेषु धेहि यूयं पात ... ||
7.11.e: O Agni, bring the Gods to taste our presents: with Indra leading, here let them be joyful.  Convey this sacrifice to Gods in heaven. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.12.d: अगन्म महा नमसा यविष्ठं यो दीदाय समिद्धः सवे दुरोणे | चित्रभानुं रोदसी अन्तरुर्वी सवाहुतं विश्वतः परत्यञ्चम ||
7.12.e: WE with great reverence have approached The Youngest who hath shone forth well-kindled in his dwelling,  With wondrous light between wide earth and heaven, well-worshipped, looking forth in all directions.

7.12.d: स मह्ना विश्वा दुरितानि साह्वानग्निः षटवे दम आ जातवेदाः | स नो रक्षिषद दुरितादवद्यादस्मान गर्णत उत नो मघोनः ||
7.12.e: Through his great might o’ercoming all misfortunes, praised in the house is Agni Jātavedas.  May he protect us from disgrace and trouble, both us who laud him and our noble patrons.

7.12.d: तवं वरुण उत मित्रो अग्ने तवां वर्धन्ति मतिभिर्वसिष्ठाः | तवे वसु सुषणनानि सन्तु यूयं पात ... ||
7.12.e: O Agni, thou art Varuṇa and Mitra: Vasisthas with their holy hymns exalt thee.  With thee be most abundant gain of treasure. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.13.d: पराग्नये विश्वशुचे धियन्धे.असुरघ्ने मन्म धीतिं भरध्वम | भरे हविर्न बर्हिषि परीणानो वैश्वानराय यतये मतीनाम ||
7.13.e: BRING song and hymn to Agni, Asura-slayer, enlightener of all and thought-bestower.  Like an oblation on the grass, to please him, I bring this to Vaiśvānara, hymn-inspirer.

7.13.d: तवमग्ने शोचिषा शोशुचान आ रोदसी अप्र्णा जायमानः | तवं देवानभिशस्तेरमुञ्चो वैस्वानर जातवेदो महित्वा ||
7.13.e: Thou with thy flame, O Agni, brightly glowing, hast at thy birth filled full the earth and heaven.  TIOU with thy might, Vaiśvānara Jātavedas, settest the Gods free frodi the curse that bound them.

7.13.d: जातो यदग्ने भुवना वयख्यः पशून न गोपा इर्यः परिज्मा | वैश्वानर बरह्मणे विन्द गातुं यूयं पात ... ||
7.13.e: Agni, when, born thou lookedst on all creatures, like a brisk herdsman moving round his cattle.  The path to prayer, Vaiśvānara, thou foundest. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.14.d: समिधा जातवेदसे देवाय देवहूतिभिः | हविर्भिः शुक्रशोचिषे नमस्विनो वयं दाशेमाग्नये ||
7.14.e: WITH reverence and with offered gifts serve we the God whose flame is bright:  Let us bring Jātavedas fuel, and adore Agni when we invoke the Gods.

7.14.d: वयं ते अग्ने समिधा विधेम वयं दाशेम सुष्टुती यजत्र | वयं घर्तेनाध्वरस्य होतर्वयं देव हविषा भद्रशोचे ||
7.14.e: Agni, may we perform thy rites with fuel, and honour thee, O Holy one, with praises:  Honour thee, Priest of sacrifice! with butter, thee, God of blessed light! with our oblation.

7.14.d: आ नो देवेभिरुप देवहूतिमग्ने याहि वषट्क्र्तिं जुषाणः | तुभ्यं देवाय दाशतः सयाम यूयं पात ... ||
7.14.e: Come, Agni, with the Gods to our invoking, come, pleased, to offerings sanctified with Vaṣaṭ.  May we be his who pays thee, God, due honour. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.15.d: उपसद्याय मीळ्हुष आस्ये जुहुता हविः | यो नो नेदिष्ठमाप्यम ||
7.15.e: OFFER oblations in his mouth, the bounteous God's whom we must serve.  His who is nearest kin to us:

7.15.d: यः पञ्च चर्षणीरभि निषसाद दमे-दमे | कविर्ग्र्हपतिर्युवा ||
7.15.e: Who for the Fivefold People's take hath seated him in every home  Wise, Youthful, Master of the house.

7.15.d: स नो वेदो अमात्यमग्नी रक्षतु विश्वतः | उतास्मान पात्वंहसः ||
7.15.e: On all sides may that Agni guard our household folk and property;  May he deliver us from woe.

7.15.d: नवं नु सतोममग्नये दिवः शयेनाय जीजनम | वस्वः कुविद वनाति नः ||
7.15.e: I have begotten this new hymn for Agni, Falcon of the sky:  Will he not give us of his wealth?

7.15.d: सपार्हा यस्य शरियो दर्शे रयिर्वीरवतो यथा | अग्रे यज्ञस्य शोचतः ||
7.15.e: Whose lories when he glows in front of sacrite are fair to see,  Like wealth of one with hero sons.

7.15.d: सेमां वेतु वषट्क्र्तिमग्निर्जुषत नो गिरः | यजिष्ठो हव्यवाहनः ||
7.15.e: May he enjoy this hallowed gift, Agni accept our songs, who bears  Oblations, best of worshippers.

7.15.d: नि तवा नक्ष्य विश्पते दयुमन्तं देव धीमहि | सुवीरमग्न आहुत ||
7.15.e: Lord of the house, whom men must seek, we set thee down, O Worshipped Onel  Bright, rich in heroes, Agni! God

7.15.d: कषप उस्रश्च दीदिहि सवग्नयस्त्वया वयम | सुवीरस्त्वमस्मयुः ||
7.15.e: Shine forth at night and morn: through thee with fires are we provided well.  Thou, rich in heroes, art our Friend.

7.15.d: उप तवा सातये नरो विप्रासो यन्ति धीतिभिः | उपाक्षरासहस्रिणी ||
7.15.e: The men come near thee for their gain, the singers with their songs of praise:  Speech, thousandfold, comes near to thee.

7.15.d: अग्नी रक्षांसि सेधति शुक्रशोचिरमर्त्यः | शुचिः पावक ईड्यः ||
7.15.e: Bright, Purifier, meet for praise, Immortal with refulgent glow,  Agni drives Rākṣasas away.

7.15.d: स नो राधांस्या भरेशानः सहसो यहो | भगश्च दातुवार्यम ||
7.15.e: As such, bring us abundant wealth, young Child of Strength, for this thou canst  May Bhaga give us what is choice.

7.15.d: तवमग्ने वीरवद यशो देवश्च सविता भगः | दितिश्चदाति वार्यम ||
7.15.e: Thou, Agni, givest hero fame: Bhaga and Savitar the God,  And Did give us what is good.

7.15.d: अग्ने रक्षा णो अंहसः परति षम देव रीषतः | तपिष्ठैरजरो दह ||
7.15.e: Agni, preserve us from distress: consume our enemies, O God,  Eternal, with the hottest flames.

7.15.d: अधा मही न आयस्यनाध्र्ष्टो नर्पीतये | पूर्भवा शतभुजिः ||
7.15.e: And, irresistible, be thou a mighty iron fort to us,  With hundred walls for man's defence.

7.15.d: तवं नः पाह्यंहसो दोषावस्तरघायतः | दिवा नक्तमदाभ्य ||
7.15.e: Do thou preserve us, eve and morn, from sorrow, from the wicked men,  Infallible! by day and night.

7.16.d: एना वो अग्निं नमसोर्जो नपातमा हुवे | परियं चेतिष्ठमरतिं सवध्वरं विश्वस्य दूतमम्र्तम ||
7.16.e: WITH this my reverent hymn I call Agni for you, the Son of Strength,  Dear, wisest envoy, served with noble sacrifice, immortal messenger of all.

7.16.d: स योजते अरुषा विश्वभोजसा स दुद्रवत सवाहुतः | सुब्रह्मा यज्ञः सुशमी वसूनां देवं राधो जनानाम ||
7.16.e: His two red horses, all-supporting, let him yoke: let him, well-worshipped, urge them fast.  Then hath the sacrifice good prayers and happy end, and heavenly gift of wealth to men.

7.16.d: उदस्य शोचिरस्थादाजुह्वानस्य मीळ्हुषः | उद धूमासोरुषासो दिविस्प्र्शः समग्निमिन्धते नरः ||
7.16.e: The flame of him the Bountiful, the Much-invoked, hath mounted up,  And his red-coloured smoke-clouds reach and touch the sky: the men are kindling Agni well.

7.16.d: तं तवा दूतं कर्ण्महे यशस्तमं देवाना वीतये वह | विश्वा सूनो सहसो मर्तभोजना रास्व तद यत तवेमहे ||
7.16.e: Thee, thee Most Glorious One we make our messenger. Bring the Gods hither to the feast.  Give us, O Son of Strength, all food that fcedeth man: give that for which we pray to thee.

7.16.d: तवमग्ने गर्हपतिस्त्वं होता नो अध्वरे | तवं पोता विश्ववार परचेता यक्षि वेषि च वार्यम ||
7.16.e: Thou, Agni, art the homestead's Lord, our Herald at the sacrifice.  Lord of all boons, thou art the Cleanser and a Sage. Pay worship, and enjoy the good.

7.16.d: कर्धि रत्नं यजमानाय सुक्रतो तवं हि रत्नधा असि | आन रते शिशीहि विश्वं रत्विजं सुशंसो यश्च दक्षते ||
7.16.e: Give riches to the sacrificer, O Most Wise, for thou art he who granteth wealth.  Inspire with zeal each priest at this our solemn rite; all who are skilled in singing praise.

7.16.d: तवे अग्ने सवाहुत परियासः सन्तु सूरयः | यन्तारो ये मघवानो जनानामूर्वान दयन्त गोनाम ||
7.16.e: O Agni who art worshipped well, dear let our princes he to thee,  Our wealthy patrons who are governors of men, who part, as gifts, their stalls of kine.

7.16.d: येषामिळा घर्तहस्ता दुरोण आनपि पराता निषीदति | तांस्त्रायस्व सहस्य दरुहो निदो यछा नः शर्म दीर्घश्रुत ||
7.16.e: They in whose home, her hand bearing the sacred oil, Iḷā sits down well-satisfied-  Guard them, Victorious God, from slander and from harm. give us a refuge famed afar.

7.16.d: स मन्द्रया च जिह्वया वह्निरासा विदुष्टरः | अग्ने रयिं मघवद्भ्यो न आ वह हव्यदातिं च सूदय ||
7.16.e: Do thou, a Priest with pleasant tongue, most wise, and very near to us,  Agni, bring riches hither to our liberal chiefs, and speed the oflering of our gifts.

7.16.d: ये राधांसि ददत्यश्व्या मघा कामेन शरवसो महः | तानंहसः पिप्र्हि पर्त्र्भिष टवं शतं पूर्भिर्यविष्ठ्य ||
7.16.e: They who bestow as bounty plenteous wealth of steeds, moved by desire of great renown-  Do thou with saving help preserve them from distress, Most Youthful! with a hundred forts.

7.16.d: देवो वो दरविणोदाः पूर्णां विवष्ट्यासिचम | उद वा सिञ्चध्वमुप वा पर्णध्वमादिद वो देव ओहते ||
7.16.e: The God who gives your wealth demands a full libation poured to him.  Pour ye it forth, then fill the vessel full again: then doth the God pay heed to you.

7.16.d: तं होतारमध्वरस्य परचेतसं वह्निं देवा अक्र्ण्वत | दधाति रत्नं विधते सुवीर्यमग्निर्जनाय दाशुषे ||
7.16.e: Him have the Gods appointed Priest of sacrifice, oblation-bearer, passing wise.  Agni gives wealth and valour to the worshipper, to folk who offer up their gifts.

7.17.d: अग्ने भव सुषमिधा समिद्ध उत बर्हिरुर्विया वि सत्र्णीताम ||
7.17.e: AGNI, be kindled well with proper fuel, and let the grass be scattered wide about thee.

7.17.d: उत दवार उशतीर्वि शरयन्तामुत देवानुशत आ वहेह ||
7.17.e: Let the impatient Portals be thrown open bring thou the Gods impatient to come hither.

7.17.d: अग्ने वीहि हविषा वक्षि देवान सवध्वरा कर्णुहि जातवेदः ||
7.17.e: Taste, Agni: serve the Gods with our oblation. Offer good sacrifices, Jātavedas!

7.17.d: सवध्वरा करति जातवेदा यक्षद देवानम्र्तान पिप्रयच्च ||
7.17.e: Let Jātavedas pay fair sacrifices, worship andgratify the Gods Immortal.

7.17.d: वंस्व विश्वा वार्याणि परचेतः सत्या भवन्त्वाशिषो नोद्य ||
7.17.e: Wise God, win for us things that are all-goodly, and let the prayers, we pray today be fruitful.

7.17.d: तवामु ते दधिरे हव्यवाहं देवासो अग्न ऊर्ज आ नपातम ||
7.17.e: Thee, even thee, the Son of Strength, O Agni, those Gods have made the bearer of oblations.

7.17.d: ते ते देवाय दाशतः सयाम महो नो रत्ना वि दध इयानः ||
7.17.e: To thee the God may we perform our worship: do thou, besought, grant us abundant riches.

7.18.d: तवे ह यत पितरश्चिन न इन्द्र विश्वा वामा जरितारो असन्वन | तवे गावः सुदुघास्त्वे हयश्वास्त्वं वसु देवयतेवनिष्ठः ||
7.18.e: ALL is with thee, O Indra, all the treasures which erst our fathers won who sang thy praises.  With thee are milch-kine good to milk, and horses: best winner thou of riches for the pious.

7.18.d: राजेव हि जनिभिः कषेष्येवाव दयुभिरभि विदुष कविः सन | पिशा गिरो मघवन गोभिरश्वैस्त्वायतः शिशीहिराये अस्मान ||
7.18.e: For like a King among his wives thou dwellest: with glories, as a Sage, surround and help us.  Make us, thy servants, strong for wealth, and honour our songs wirth kine and steeds and decoration.

7.18.d: इमा उ तवा पस्प्र्धानासो अत्र मन्द्रा गिरो देवयन्तीरुप सथुः | अर्वाची ते पथ्या राय एतु सयाम ते सुमताविन्द्र शर्मन ||
7.18.e: Here these our holy hymns with joy and gladness in pious emulation have approached thee.  Hitherward come thy path that leads to riches: may we find shelter in thy favour, Indra.

7.18.d: धेनुं न तवा सूयवसे दुदुक्षन्नुप बरह्माणि सस्र्जे वसिष्ठः | तवामिन मे गोपतिं विश्व आहा न इन्द्रः सुमतिं गन्त्वछ ||
7.18.e: Vasiṣṭha hath poured forth his prayers, desiring to milk thee like a cow in goodly pasture.  All these my people call thee Lord of cattle: may Indra. come unto the prayer we offer.

7.18.d: अर्णांसि चित पप्रथाना सुदास इन्द्रो गाधान्यक्र्णोत सुपारा | शर्धन्तं शिम्युमुचथस्य नव्यः शापं सिन्धूनामक्र्णोदशस्तीः ||
7.18.e: What though the floods spread widely, Indra made them shallow and easy for Sudās to traverse.  He, worthy of our praises, caused the Simyu, foe of our hymn, to curse the rivers' fury.

7.18.d: पुरोळा इत तुर्वशो यक्षुरासीद राये मत्स्यासो निशिता अपीव | शरुष्टिं चक्रुर्भ्र्गवो दरुह्यवश्च सखा सखायमतरद विषूचोः ||
7.18.e: Eager for spoil was Turvaśa Purodas, fain to win wealth, like fishes urged by hunger.  The Bhṛgus and the Druhyus quickly listened: friend rescued friend mid the two distant peoples.

7.18.d: आ पक्थासो भलानसो भनन्तालिनासो विषाणिनः शिवासः | आ यो.अनयत सधमा आर्यस्य गव्या तर्त्सुभ्यो अजगन युधा नर्न ||
7.18.e: Together came the Pakthas, the Bhalanas, the Alinas, the Sivas, the Visanins.  Yet to the Trtsus came the Ārya's Comrade, through love of spoil and heroes' war, to lead them.

7.18.d: दुराध्यो अदितिं सरेवयन्तो.अचेतसो वि जग्र्भ्रे परुष्णीम | मह्नाविव्यक पर्थिवीं पत्यमानः पशुष कविरशयच्चायमानः ||
7.18.e: Fools, in their folly fain to waste her waters, they parted inexhaustible Paruṣṇī.  Lord of the Earth, he with his might repressed them: still lay the herd and the affrighted herdsman.

7.18.d: ईयुरर्थं न नयर्थं परुष्णीमाशुश्चनेदभिपित्वं जगाम | सुदास इन्द्रः सुतुकानमित्रानरन्धयन मानुषे वध्रिवाचः ||
7.18.e: As to their goal they sped to their destruetion: they sought Paruṣṇī; e’en the swift returned not.  Indra abandoned, to Sudās the manly, the swiftly flying foes, unmanly babblers.

7.18.d: ईयुर्गावो न यवसादगोपा यथाक्र्तमभि मित्रं चितासः | पर्श्निगावः पर्श्निनिप्रेषितासः शरुष्टिं चक्रुर्नियुतो रन्तयश्च ||
7.18.e: They went like kine unherded from the pasture, each clinging to a friend as chance directed.  They who drive spotted steeds, sent down by Pṛśni, gave ear, the Warriors and the harnessed horses.

7.18.d: एकं च यो विंशतिं च शरवस्या वैकर्णयोर्जनान राजा नयस्तः | दस्मो न सद्मन नि शिशाति बर्हिः शूरः सर्गमक्र्णोदिन्द्र एषाम ||
7.18.e: The King who scattered one-and-twenty people of both Vaikarna tribes through lust of glory-  As the skilled priest clips grass within the chamber, so hath the Hero Indra, wrought their downfall.

7.18.d: अध शरुतं कवषं वर्द्धमप्स्वनु दरुह्युं नि वर्णग वज्रबाहुः | वर्णाना अत्र सख्याय सख्यं तवायन्तो ये अमदन्ननु तवा ||
7.18.e: Thou, thunder-armed, o’erwhelmedst in the waters famed ancient Kavasa and then the Druhyu.  Others here claiming friendship to their friendship, devoted unto thee, in thee were joyful.

7.18.d: वि सद्यो विश्वा दरंहितान्येषामिन्द्रः पुरः सहसा सप्त दर्दः | वयानवस्य तर्त्सवे गयं भाग जेष्म पूरुं विदथे मर्ध्रवाचम ||
7.18.e: Indra at once with conquering might demolished all their strong places and their seven castles.  The goods of Anu's son he gave to Trtsu. May we in sacrifice conquer scorned Pūru.

7.18.d: नि गव्यवो.अनवो दरुह्यवश्च षष्टिः शता सुषुपुः षट सहस्रा | षष्टिर्वीरासो अधि षड दुवोयु विश्वेदिन्द्रस्य वीर्या कर्तानि ||
7.18.e: The Anavas and Druhyus, seeking booty, have slept, the sixty hundred, yea, six thousand,  And six-and-sixty heroes. For the pious were all these mighty exploits done by Indra.

7.18.d: इन्द्रेणैते तर्त्सवो वेविषाणा आपो न सर्ष्टा अधवन्त नीचीः | दुर्मित्रासः परकलविन मिमाना जहुर्विश्वानि भोजना सुदासे ||
7.18.e: These Trtsus under Indra's careful guidance came speeding like loosed waters rushing downward.  The foemen, measuring exceeding closely, abandoned to Sudās all their provisions.

7.18.d: अर्धं वीरस्य शर्तपामनिन्द्रं परा शर्धन्तं नुनुदे अभि कषाम | इन्द्रो मन्युं मन्युम्यो मिमाय भेजे पथो वर्तनिम्पत्यमानः ||
7.18.e: The hero's side who drank the dressed oblation, Indra's denier, far o’er earth he scattered.  Indra brought down the fierce destroyer's fury. He gave them various roads, the path's Controller.

7.18.d: आध्रेण चित तद वेकं चकार सिंह्यं चित पेत्वेना जघान | अव सरक्तीर्वेश्याव्र्श्चदिन्द्रः परायछद विश्वा भोजना सुदासे ||
7.18.e: E’en with the weak he wrought this matchless exploit: e’en with a goat he did to death a lion.  He pared the pillar's angles with a needle. Thus to Sudās Indra gave all provisions.

7.18.d: शश्वन्तो हि शत्रवो रारधुष टे भेदस्य चिच्छर्धतो विन्द रन्धिम | मर्तानेन सतुवतो यः कर्णोति तिग्मं तस्मिन नि जहि वज्रमिन्द्र ||
7.18.e: To thee have all thine enemies submitted: e’en the fierce Bheda hast thou made thy subject.  Cast down thy sharpened thunderbolt, O Indra, on him who harms the men who sing thy praises.

7.18.d: आवदिन्द्रं यमुना तर्त्सवश्च परात्र भेदं सर्वतातामुषायत | अजासश्च शिग्रवो यक्षवश्च बलिं शीर्षाणि जभ्रुरश्व्यानि ||
7.18.e: Yamuna and the Trtsus aided Indra. There he stripped Bheda bare of all his treasures.  The Ajas and the Sigrus and the Yaksus brought in to him as tribute heads of horses.

7.18.d: न त इन्द्र सुमतयो न रायः संचक्षे पूर्वा उषसो न नूत्नाः | देवकं चिन मान्यमानं जघन्थाव तमना बर्हतः शम्बरं भेत ||
7.18.e: Not to be scorned, but like Dawns past and recent, O Indra, are thy favours and thy riches.  Devaka, Mānyamana's son, thou slewest, and smotest Śambara from the lofty mountain.

7.18.d: पर ये गर्हादममदुस्त्वाया पराशरः शतयातुर्वसिष्ठः | न ते भोजस्य सख्यं मर्षन्ताधा सूरिभ्यः सुदिना वयुछान ||
7.18.e: They who, from home, have gladdened thee, thy servants Parasara, Vasiṣṭha, Satayatu,  Will not forget thy friendship, liberal Giver. So shall the days dawn prosperous for the princes.

7.18.d: दवे नप्तुर्देववतः शते गोर्द्वा रथा वधूमन्ता सुदासः | अर्हन्नग्ने पैजवनस्य दानं होतेव सद्म पर्येमि रेभन ||
7.18.e: Priest-like, with praise, I move around the altar, earning Paijavana's reward, O Agni,  Two hundred cows from Devavan's descendant, two chariots from Sudās with mares to draw them.

7.18.d: चत्वारो मा पैजवनस्य दानाः समद्दिष्टयः कर्शनिनो निरेके | रज्रासो मा पर्थिविष्ठाः सुदासस्तोकं तोकाय शरवसे वहन्ति ||
7.18.e: Gift of Paijavana, four horses bear me in foremost place, trained steeds with pearl to deck them.  Sudās's brown steeds, firmly-stepping, carry me and my son for progeny and glory.

7.18.d: यस्य शरवो रोदसी अन्तरुर्वी शीर्ष्णे-शीर्ष्णे विबभाजा विभक्ता | सप्तेदिन्द्रं न सरवतो गर्णन्ति नि युध्यामधिमशिशादभीके ||
7.18.e: Him whose fame spreads between wide earth and heaven, who, as dispenser, gives each chief his portion,  Seven flowing Rivers glorify like Indra. He slew Yudhyamadhi in close encounter.

7.18.d: इमं नरो मरुतः सश्चतानु दिवोदासं न पितरं सुदासः | अविष्टना पैजवनस्य केतं दूणाशं कषत्रमजरं दुवोयु ||
7.18.e: Attend on him O ye heroic Maruts as on Sudās's father Divodāsa.  Further Paijavana's desire with favour. Guard faithfully his lasting firm dominion.

7.19.d: यस्तिग्मश्र्ङगो वर्षभो न भीम एकः कर्ष्टीश्च्यावयति पर विश्वाः | यः शश्वतो अदाशुषो गयस्य परयन्तासिसुष्वितराय वेदः ||
7.19.e: HE like a bull with sharpened horns, terrific, singly excites and agitates all the people:  Thou givest him who largely pours libations his goods who pours not, for his own possession.

7.19.d: तवं ह तयदिन्द्र कुत्समावः शुश्रूषमाणस्तन्वा समर्ये | दासं यच्छुष्णं कुयवं नयस्मा अरन्धय आर्जुनेयाय शिक्षन ||
7.19.e: Thou, verily, Indra, gavest help to Kutsa, willingly giving car to him in battle,  When, aiding Ārjuneya, thou subduedst to him both Kuyava and the Dāsa Śuṣṇa.

7.19.d: तवं धर्ष्णो धर्षता वीतहव्यं परावो विश्वाभिरूतिभिः सुदासम | पर पौरुकुत्सिं तरसदस्युमावः कषेत्रसाता वर्त्रहत्येषु पूरुम ||
7.19.e: O Bold One, thou with all thine aids hast boldly holpen Sudās whose offerings were accepted,  Pūru in winning land and slaying foemen, and Trasadasyu son of Purukutsa.

7.19.d: तवं नर्भिर्न्र्मणो देववीतौ भूरीणि वर्त्रा हर्यश्व हंसि | तवं नि दस्युं चुमुरिं धुनिं चास्वापयो दभीतये सुहन्तु ||
7.19.e: At the Gods’ banquet, hero-souled! with Heroes, Lord of Bay Steeds, thou slewest many foemen.  Thou sentest in swift death to sleep the Dasyu, both Cumuri and Dhuni, for Dabhīti.

7.19.d: तव चयौत्नानि वज्रहस्त तानि नव यत पुरो नवतिं च सद्यः | निवेशने शततमाविवेषीरहञ्च वर्त्रं नमुचिमुताहन ||
7.19.e: These were thy mighty powers that, Thunder-wielder, thou swiftly crushedst nine-and-ninety castles:  Thou capturedst the hundredth in thine onslaught; thou slewest Namuci, thou slewest Vṛtra.

7.19.d: सना ता त इन्द्र भोजनानि रातहव्याय दाशुषे सुदासे | वर्ष्णे ते हरी वर्षणा युनज्मि वयन्तु बरह्माणि पुरुशाक वाजम ||
7.19.e: Old are the blessings, Indra, which thou gavest Sudās the worshipper who brought oblations.  For thee, the Strong, I yoke thy strong Bay Horses: may our prayers reach thee and win strength, Most Mighty!

7.19.d: मा ते अस्यां सहसावन परिष्टावघाय भूम हरिवः परादै | तरायस्व नो.अव्र्केभिर्वरूथैस्तव परियासः सूरिषु सयाम ||
7.19.e: Give us not up, Lord of Bay Horses, Victor, in this thine own assembly, to the wicked.  Deliver us with true and faithful succours: dear may we be to thee among the princes.

7.19.d: परियास इत ते मघवन्नभिष्टौ नरो मदेम शरणे सखायः | नि तुर्वशं नि याद्वं शिशीह्यतिथिग्वाय शंस्यं करिष्यन ||
7.19.e: May we men, Maghavan, the friends thou lovest, near thee be joyful under thy protection.  Fain to fulfil the wish of Atithigva humble. the pride of Turvaśa and Yadva.

7.19.d: सद्यश्चिन नु ते मघवन्नभिष्टौ नरः शंसन्त्युक्थशास उक्था | ये ते हवेभिर्वि पणीन्रदाशन्नस्मान वर्णीष्व युज्याय तस्मै ||
7.19.e: Swiftly, in truth, O Maghavan, about thee men skilled in hymning sing their songs and praises. '  Elect us also into their assembly who by their calls on thee despoiled the niggards.

7.19.d: एते सतोमा नरां नर्तम तुभ्यमस्मद्र्यञ्चो ददतो मघानि | तेषामिन्द्र वर्त्रहत्ये शिवो भूः सखा च शूरो.अविताच नर्णाम ||
7.19.e: Thine are these lauds, O manliest of heroes, lauds which revert to us and give us riches.  Favour these, Indra, when they fight with faemen, as Friend and Hero and the heroes' Helper.

7.19.d: नू इन्द्र शूर सतवमान ऊती बरह्मजूतस्तन्वा वाव्र्धस्व | उप नो वाजान मिमीह्युप सतीन यूयं पात ... ||
7.19.e: Now, lauded for thine aid, Heroic Indra, sped by our prayer, wax mighty in thy body.  Apportion to us strength and habitations. Ye Gods, protect us evermore with blessings.

7.20.d: उग्रो जज्ञे वीर्याय सवधावाञ्चक्रिरपो नर्यो यत करिष्यन | जग्मिर्युवा नर्षदनमवोभिस्त्राता न इन्द्र एनसो महश्चित ||
7.20.e: STRONG, Godly-natured, born for hero exploit, man's Friend, hedoth whatever deed he willeth.  Saving us e’en from great transgression, Indra, the Youthful, visiteth man's home with favour.

7.20.d: हन्त वर्त्रमिन्द्रः शूशुवानः परावीन नु वीरो जरितारमूती | कर्ता सुदासे अह वा उ लोकं दाता वसु मुहुरा दाशुषे भूत ||
7.20.e: Waxing greatness Indra slayeth Vṛtra: the Hero with his aid hath helped the singer.  He gave Sudās wide room and space, and often hath granted wealth to him who brought oblations.

7.20.d: युध्मो अनर्वा खजक्र्त समद्वा शूरः सत्राषाड जनुषेमषाळ्हः | वयास इन्द्रः पर्तनाः सवोजा अधा विश्वंशत्रूयन्तं जघान ||
7.20.e: Soldier unchecked, war-rousing, battling Hero, unconquered from of old, victorious ever,  Indra the very strong hath scattered armies; yea, he hath slain each foe who fought against him.

7.20.d: उभे चिदिन्द्र रोदसी महित्वा पप्राथ तविषीभिस्तुविष्मः | नि वज्रमिन्द्रो हरिवान मिमिक्षन समन्धसा मदेषु वाुवोच ||
7.20.e: Thou with thy greatness hast filled full, O Indra, even both the worlds with might, O thou Most Mighty.  Lord of Bays, Indra, brandishing his thunder, is gratified with Soma at the banquet.

7.20.d: वर्षा जजान वर्षणं रणाय तमु चिन नारी नर्यं ससूव | पर यः सेनानीरध नर्भ्यो अस्तीनः सत्वा गवेषणः स धर्ष्णुः ||
7.20.e: A Bull begat the Bull for joy of battle, and a strong Mother brought forth him the manly.  He who is Chief of men, their armies' Leader, is strong Hero, bold, and fain for booty.

7.20.d: नू चित स भरेषते जनो न रेषन मनो यो अस्य घोरमाविवासात | यज्ञैर्य इन्द्रे दधते दुवांसि कषयत स राय रतपा रतेजाः ||
7.20.e: The people falter not, nor suffer sorrow, who win themselves this God's terrific spirit.  He who with sacrifices worships Indra is lord of wealth, law-born and law's protector.

7.20.d: यदिन्द्र पूर्वो अपराय शिक्षन्नयज्ज्यायान कनीयसो देष्णम | अम्र्त इत पर्यासीत दूरमा चित्र चित्र्यं भरा रयिं नः ||
7.20.e: Whene’er the elder fain would help the younger the greater cometh to the lesser's present.  Shall the Immortal sit aloof' inactive? O Wondrous Indra, bring us wondrous riches.

7.20.d: यस्त इन्द्र परियो जनो ददाशदसन निरेके अद्रिवः सखा ते | वयं ते अस्यां सुमतौ चनिष्ठाः सयाम वरूथे अघ्नतो नर्पीतौ ||
7.20.e: Thy dear folk, Indra, who present oblations, are, in chief place, thy friends, O Thunder-wielder.  May we be best content in this thy favour, sheltered by One who slays not, but preserves us.

7.20.d: एष सतोमो अचिक्रदद वर्षा त उत सतामुर्मघवन्नक्रपिष्ट | रायस कामो जरितारं त आगन तवमङग शक्र वस्व आशको नः ||
7.20.e: To thee the mighty hymn hath clamoured loudly, and, Maghavan, the eloquent hath besought thee.  Desire of wealth hath come upon thy singer: help us then, gakra, to our share of riches.

7.20.d: स न इन्द्र तवयताया इषे धास्त्मना च ये मघवानो जुनन्ति | वस्वी षु ते जरित्रे अस्तु शक्तिर्यूयं पात ... ||
7.20.e: Place us by food which thou hast given, O Indra, us and the wealthy patrons who command us.  Let thy great power bring good to him who lauds thee. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.21.d: असावि देवं गोर्जीकमन्धो नयस्मिन्निन्द्रो जनुषेमुवोच | बोधामसि तवा हर्यश्व यज्ञैर्बोधा न सतोममन्धसो मदेषु ||
7.21.e: PRESSED is the juice divine with milk commingled: thereto hath Indra ever been accustomed.  We wake thee, Lord of Bays, with sacrifices: mark this our laud in the wild joy of Soma.

7.21.d: पर यन्ति यज्ञं विपयन्ति बर्हिः सोममादो विदथे दुध्रवाचः | नयु भरियन्ते यशसो गर्भादा दूर उपब्दो वर्षणोन्र्षाचः ||
7.21.e: On to the rite they move, the grass they scatter, these Soma-drinkers eloquent in synod.  Hither, for men to grasp, are brought the press-stones, far-thundering, famous, strong, that wait on heroes.

7.21.d: तवमिन्द्र सरवितवा अपस कः परिष्ठिता अहिना शूर पूर्वीः | तवद वावक्रे रथ्यो न धेना रेजन्ते विश्वा कर्त्रिमाणि भीषा ||
7.21.e: Indra, thou settest free the many waters that were encompassed, Hero, by the Dragon.  Down rolled, as if on chariots borne, the rivers: through fear of thee all things created tremble.

7.21.d: भीमो विवेषायुधेभिरेषामपांसि विश्वा नर्याणि विद्वान | इन्द्रः पुरो जर्ह्र्षाणो वि दूधोद वि वज्रहस्तो महिनाजघान ||
7.21.e: Skilled in all manly deeds the God terrific hath with his weapons mastered these opponents.  Indra in rapturous joy shook down their castles he slew them in his might, the Thunder-wielder.

7.21.d: न यातव इन्द्र जूजुवुर्नो न वन्दना शविष्ठ वेद्याभिः | स शर्धदर्यो विषुणस्य जन्तोर्मा शिश्नदेवा अपि गुरतं नः ||
7.21.e: No evil spirits have impelled us, Indra, nor fiends, O Mightiest God, with their devices.  Let our true God subdue the hostile rabble: let not the lewd approach our holy worship.

7.21.d: अभि करत्वेन्द्र भूरध जमन न ते विव्यं महिमानं रजांसि | सवेना हि वर्त्रं शवसा जघन्थ न शत्रुरन्तंविविदद युधा ते ||
7.21.e: Thou in thy strength surpassest Earth and Heaven: the regions comprehend not all thy greatness.  With thine own power and might thou slewest Vṛtra: no foe hath found the end of thee in battle.

7.21.d: देवाश्चित ते असुर्याय पूर्वे.अनु कषत्राय ममिरे सहांसि | इन्द्रो मघानि दयते विषह्येन्द्रं वाजस्य जोहुवन्त सातौ ||
7.21.e: Even the earlier Deities submitted their powers to thy supreme divine dominion.  Indra wins wealth and deals it out to other's: men in the strife for booty call on Indra.

7.21.d: कीरिश्चिद धि तवामवसे जुहावेशानमिन्द्र सौभगस्य भूरेः | अवो बभूथ शतमूते अस्मे अभिक्षत्तुस्त्वावतो वरूता ||
7.21.e: The humble hath invoked thee for protection, thee, Lord of great felicity, O Indra.  Thou with a hundred aids hast been our Helper: one who brings gifts like thee hath his defender.

7.21.d: सखायस्त इन्द्र विश्वह सयाम नमोव्र्धासो महिना तरुत्र | वन्वन्तु समा ते.अवसा समीके.अभीतिमर्यो वनुषां शवांसि ||
7.21.e: May we, O Indra, be thy friends for ever, eagerly, Conqueror, yielding greater homage.  May, through thy grace, the strength of us who battle quell in the shock the onset of the foeman.
Place us by food which thou hast given, O Indra, us and the wealthy patrons who command us.  Let thy great power bring good to him who lauds thee. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.22.d: पिबा सोममिन्द्र मन्दतु तवा यं ते सुषाव हर्यश्वाद्रिः | सोतुर्बाहुभ्यां सुयतो नार्वा ||
7.22.e: DRINK Soma, Lord of Bays, and let it cheer thee: Indra, the stone, like a well guided courser,  Directed by the presser's arms hath pressed it.

7.22.d: यस्ते मदो युज्यश्चारुरस्ति येन वर्त्राणि हर्यश्व हंसि | स तवामिन्द्र परभूवसो ममत्तु ||
7.22.e: So let the draught of joy, thy dear companion, by which, O Lord of Bays, thou slayest foemen,  Delight thee, Indra, Lord of princely treasures.

7.22.d: बोधा सु मे मघवन वाचमेमां यां ते वसिष्ठो अर्चतिप्रशस्तिम | इमा बरह्म सधमादे जुषस्व ||
7.22.e: Mark closely, Maghavan, the words I utter, this eulogy recited by Vasiṣṭha:  Accept the prayers I offer at thy banquet.

7.22.d: शरुधी हवं विपिपानस्याद्रेर्बोधा विप्रस्यार्चतो मनीषाम | कर्ष्वा दुवांस्यन्तमा सचेमा ||
7.22.e: Hear thou the call of the juice-drinking press-stone: hear thou the Brahman's hymn who sings and lauds thee.  Take to thine inmost self these adorations.

7.22.d: न ते गिरो अपि मर्ष्ये तुरस्य न सुष्टुतिमसुर्यस्य विद्वान | सदा ते नाम सवयशो विवक्मि ||
7.22.e: I know and ne’er forget the hymns and praises of thee, the Conqueror, and thy strength immortal.  Thy name I ever utter. Self-Refulgent

7.22.d: भूरि हि ते सवना मानुषेषु भूरि मनीषी हवते तवामित | मारे अस्मन मघवञ जयोक कः ||
7.22.e: Among mankind many are thy libations, and many a time the pious sageinvokes thee.  O Maghavan, be not long distant from us.

7.22.d: तुभ्येदिमा सवना शूर विश्वा तुभ्यं बरह्माणि वर्धना कर्णोमि | तवं नर्भिर्हव्यो विश्वधासि ||
7.22.e: All these libations are for thee, O Hero: to thee I offer these my prayers. that strengthen.  Ever, in every place, must men invoke thee.

7.22.d: नू चिन नु ते मन्यमानस्य दस्मोदश्नुवन्ति महिमानमुग्र | न वीर्यमिन्द्र ते न राधः ||
7.22.e: Never do men attain, O Wonder-Worker, thy greatness, Mighty One, who must be lauded,  Nor, Indra, thine heroic power and bounty.

7.22.d: ये च पूर्व रषयो ये च नूत्ना इन्द्र बरह्माणि जनयन्त विप्राः | अस्मे ते सन्तु सख्या शिवानि यूयं पात ... ||
7.22.e: Among all Ṛṣis, Indra, old and recent, who have engendered hymns as sacred singers,  Even with us be thine auspicious friendships. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.23.d: उदु बरह्माण्यैरत शरवस्येन्द्रं समर्ये महया वसिष्ठ | आ यो विश्वानि शवसा ततानोपश्रोता म ईवतो वचांसि ||
7.23.e: PRAYERS have been offered up through love of glory: Vasiṣṭha, honour Indra in the battle.  He who with might extends through all existence hears words which I, his faithful servant, utter.

7.23.d: अयामि घोष इन्द्र देवजामिरिरज्यन्त यच्छुरुधो विवाचि | नहि सवमायुश्चिकिते जनेषु तानीदंहांस्यति पर्ष्यस्मान ||
7.23.e: A cry was raised which reached the Gods, O Indra, a cry to them to send us strength in combat.  None among men knows his own life's duration: bear us in safety over these our troubles.

7.23.d: युजे रथं गवेषणं हरिभ्यामुप बरह्माणि जुजुषाणमस्थुः | वि बाधिष्ट सय रोदसी महित्वेन्द्रो वर्त्राण्यप्रती जघन्वान ||
7.23.e: The Bays, the booty-seeking car I harness: my prayers have reached him who accepts them gladly.  Indra, when he had slain resistless foemen, forced with his might the two world-halves asunder.

7.23.d: आपश्चित पिप्यु सतर्यो न गावो नक्षन्न्र्तं जरितारस्त इन्द्र | याहि वायुर्न नियुतो न अछा तवं हि धीभिर्दयसे वि वाजान ||
7.23.e: Like barren cows, moreover, swelled the waters: the singen sought thy holy rite, O Indra.  Come unto us as with his team comes Vāyu: thou, through our solemn hymns bestowest booty.

7.23.d: ते तवा मदा इन्द्र मादयन्तु शुष्मिणं तुविराधसं जरित्रे | एको देवत्रा दयसे हि मर्तानस्मिञ्छूर सवने मादयस्व ||
7.23.e: So may these gladdening draughts rejoice thee, Indra, the Mighty, very bounteous to the singer.  Alone among the Gods thou pitiest mortals: O Hero, make thee glad at this libation.

7.23.d: एवेदिन्द्रं वर्षणं वज्रबाहुं वसिष्ठासो अभ्यर्चन्त्यर्कैः | स न सतुतो वीरवत पातु गोमद यूयं पात ... ||
7.23.e: Thus the Vasisthas glorify with praises Indra, the Powerful whose arm wields thunder.  Praised, may he guard our wealth in kine and heroes. Ye Gods, preserve us evermore with blessings.

7.24.d: योनिष ट इन्द्र सदने अकारि तमा नर्भिः पुरुहूत पर याहि | असो यथा नो.अविता वर्धे च ददो वसूनि ममदश्च सोमैः ||
7.24.e: A HOME is made for thee to dwell in, Indra: O Much-invoked, go thitherwith the heroes.  That thou, to prosper us, mayst be our Helper, vouchsafe us wealth, rejoice with draughts of Soma.

7.24.d: गर्भीतं ते मन इन्द्र दविबर्हाः सुतः सोमः परिषिक्ता मधूनि | विस्र्ष्टधेना भरते सुव्र्क्तिरियमिन्द्रं जोहुवती मनीषा ||
7.24.e: Indra, thy wish, twice-strong, is comprehended: pressed is the Soma, poured are pleasant juices.  This hymn of praise, from loosened tongue, made perfect, draws Indra to itself with loud invoking.

7.24.d: आ नो दिव आ पर्थिव्या रजीषिन्निदं बर्हिः सोमपेयाय याहि | वहन्तु तवा हरयो मद्र्यञ्चमाङगूषमछा तवसं मदाय ||
7.24.e: Come, thou Impetuous; God, from earth or heaven; come to our holy grass to drink the Soma.  Hither to me let thy Bay Horses bring thee to listen to our hymns and make thee joyful.

7.24.d: आ नो विश्वाभिरूतिभिः सजोषा बरह्म जुषाणो हर्यश्वयाहि | वरीव्र्जत सथविरेभिः सुशिप्रास्मे दधद वर्षणं शुष्ममिन्द्र ||
7.24.e: Come unto us with all thine aids, accordant, Lord of Bay Steeds, accepting our devotions,  Fair-helmeted, o’ercoming with the mighty, and lending us the strength of bulls, O Indra.

7.24.d: एष सतोमो मह उग्राय वाहे धुरीवात्यो न वाजयन्नधायि | इन्द्र तवायमर्क ईट्टे वसूनां दिवीव दयामधि नः शरोमतं धाः ||
7.24.e: As to the chariot pole a vigorous courser, this laud is brought to the great strong Upholder.  This hymn solicits wealth of thee: in heaven, as ’twere above the sky, set thou our glory.

7.24.d: एवा न इन्द्र वार्यस्य पूर्धि पर ते महीं सुमतिं वेविदाम | इषं पिन्व मघवद्भ्यः सुवीरां यूयं पात ... ||
7.24.e: With precious things. O Indra, thus content us: may we attain to thine exalted favour.  Send our chiefs plenteous food with hero children. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.25.d: आ ते मह इन्द्रोतयुग्र समन्यवो यत समरन्त सेनाः | पताति दिद्युन नर्यस्य बाह्वोर्मा ते मनो विष्वद्र्यग वि चारीत ||
7.25.e: WHEN with thy mighty help, O potent Indra, the armies rush together in their fury.  When from the strong man's arm the lightning flieth, let not the mind go forth to side with others.

7.25.d: नि दुर्ग इन्द्र शनथिह्यमित्रानभि ये नो मर्तासो अमन्ति | आरे तं शंसं कर्णुहि निनित्सोरा नो भर सम्भरणं वसूनाम ||
7.25.e: O Indra, where the ground is hard to traverse, smite down our foes, the mortals who assail us,  Keep far from us the curse of the reviler: bring us accumulated store of treasures.

7.25.d: शतं ते शिप्रिन्नूतयः सुदासे सहस्रं शंसा उत रातिरस्तु | जहि वधर्वनुषो मर्त्यस्यास्मे दयुम्नमधि रत्नं च धेहि ||
7.25.e: God of the fair helm, give Sudās a hundred succours, a thousand blessings, and thy bounty.  Strike down the weapon of our mortal foeman: bestow upon us splendid fame and riches.

7.25.d: तवावतो हीन्द्र करत्वे अस्मि तवावतो.अवितुः शूर रातौ | विश्वेदहानि तविषीव उग्रनोकः कर्णुष्व हरिवो न मर्धीः ||
7.25.e: I wait the power of one like thee, O Indra, gifts of a Helper such as thou art, Hero.  Strong, Mighty God, dwell with me now and ever: Lord of Bay Horses, do not thou desert us.

7.25.d: कुत्सा एते हर्यश्वाय शूषमिन्द्रे सहो देवजूतमियानाः | सत्रा कर्धि सुहना शूर वर्त्रा वयं तरुत्राः सनुयाम वाजम ||
7.25.e: Here are the Kutsas supplicating Indra for might, the Lord of Bays for God-sent conquest.  Make our foes ever easy to be vanquished: may we, victorious, win the spoil, O Hero.
With precious things, O Indra, thus content us: may we attain to thine exalted favour.  Send our chiefs plenteous food with hero children. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.26.d: न सोम इन्द्रमसुतो ममाद नाब्रह्माणो मघवानं सुतासः | तस्मा उक्थं जनये यज्जुजोषन नर्वन नवीयः शर्णवद यथा नः ||
7.26.e: SOMA unpressed ne’er gladdened liberal Indra, no juices pressed without a prayer have pleased him.  I generate a laud that shall delight him, new and heroic, so that he may hear us.

7.26.d: उक्थ-उक्थे सोम इन्द्रं ममाद नीथे-नीथे मघवानं सुतासः | यदीं सबाधः पितरं न पुत्राः समानदक्षा अवसे हवन्ते ||
7.26.e: At every laud the Soma gladdens Indra: pressed juices please him as each psalm is chanted,  What time the priests with one united effort call him to aid, as sons invoke their father.

7.26.d: चकार ता कर्णवन नूनमन्या यानि बरुवन्ति वेधसः सुतेषु | जनीरिव पतिरेकः समानो नि माम्र्जे पुर इन्द्रःसु सर्वाः ||
7.26.e: These deeds he did; let him achieve new exploits, such as the priests declare at their libations.  Indra hath taken and possessed all castles, like as one common husband doth his spouses.

7.26.d: एवा तमाहुरुत शर्ण्व इन्द्र एको विभक्ता तरणिर्मघानाम | मिथस्तुर ऊतयो यस्य पूर्वीरस्मे भद्राणि सश्चतप्रियाणि ||
7.26.e: Even thus have they declared him. Famed is Indra as Conqueror, sole distributer of treasures;  Whose many succours come in close succession. May dear delightful benefits attend us.

7.26.d: एवा वसिष्ठ इन्द्रमूतये नॄन कर्ष्टीनां वर्षभं सुते गर्णाति | सहस्रिण उप नो माहि वाजान यूयं पात ... ||
7.26.e: Thus, to bring help to men, Vasiṣṭha laudeth Indra, the peoples' Hero, at libation.  Bestow upon us strength and wealth in thousands. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.27.d: इन्द्रं नरो नेमधिता हवन्ते यत पार्या युनजते धियस्ताः | शूरो नर्षाता शवसश्चकान आ गोमति वरजे भजात्वं नः ||
7.27.e: MEN call on Indra in the armed encounter that he may make the hymns they sing decisive.  Hero, rejoicing in thy might, in combat give us a portion of the stall of cattle,

7.27.d: य इन्द्र शुष्मो मघवन ते अस्ति शिक्षा सखिभ्यः पुरुहूतन्र्भ्यः | तवं हि दर्ळ्हा मघवन विचेता अपा वर्धि परिव्र्तं न राधः ||
7.27.e: Grant, Indra Maghavan, invoked of many, to these my friends the strength which thou possessest.  Thou, Maghavan, hast rent strong places open: unclose for us, Wise God, thy hidden bounty.

7.27.d: इन्द्रो राजा जगतश्चर्षणीनामधि कषमि विषुरूपं यदस्ति | ततो ददाति दाशुषे वसूनि चोदद राध उपस्तुतश्चिदर्वाक ||
7.27.e: King of the living world, of men, is Indra, of all in varied form that earth containeth.  Thence to the worshipper he giveth riches: may he enrich us also when we laud him.

7.27.d: नू चिन न इन्द्रो मघवा सहूती दानो वाजं नि यमते न ऊती | अनूना यस्य दक्षिणा पीपाय वामं नर्भ्यो अभिवीता सखिभ्यः ||
7.27.e: Maghavan Indra, when we all invoke him, bountiful ever sendeth strength to aid us:  Whose perfect guerdon, never failing, bringeth wealth to the men, to friends the thing they covet.

7.27.d: नू इन्द्र राये वरिवस कर्धी न आ ते मनो वव्र्त्याम मघाय | गोमदश्वावद रथवद वयन्तो यूयं पात ... ||
7.27.e: Quick, Indra, give us room and way to riches, and let us bring thy mind to grant us treasures,  That we may win us cars and Steeds and cattle. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.28.d: बरह्मा ण इन्द्रोप याहि विद्वानर्वाञ्चस्ते हरयः सन्तु युक्ताः | विश्वे चिद धि तवा विहवन्त मर्ता अस्माकमिच्छ्र्णुहि विश्वमिन्व ||
7.28.e: COME to our prayers, O Indra, thou who knowest: let thy Bay Steeds be yoked and guided hither.  Though mortal men on every side invoke thee, still give thine ear to us, O All-impeller.

7.28.d: हवं त इन्द्र महिमा वयानड बरह्म यत पासि शवसिन्न्र्षीणाम | आ यद वज्रं दधिषे हस्त उग्र घोरः सन करत्वा जनिष्ठा अषाळः ||
7.28.e: Thy greatness reacheth to our invocation, the sages' prayer which, Potent God, thou guardest.  What time thy hand, O Mighty, holds the thunder, awful in strength thou hast become resistless.

7.28.d: तव परणीतीन्द्र जोहुवानान सं यन नॄन न रोदसी निनेथ | महे कषत्राय शवसे हि जज्ञे.अतूतुजिं चित तूतुजिरशिश्नत ||
7.28.e: What time thou drewest both world-halves together, like heroes led by thee who call each other-  For thou wast born for strength and high dominion-then e’en the active overthrew the sluggish.

7.28.d: एभिर्न इन्द्राहभिर्दशस्य दुर्मित्रासो हि कषितयः पवन्ते | परति यच्चष्टे अन्र्तमनेना अव दविता वरुणो मायीनः सात ||
7.28.e: Honour us in these present days, O Indra, for hostile men are making expiation.  Our sin that sinless Varuṇa discovered, the Wondrous-Wise hath long ago forgiven.

7.28.d: वोचेमेदिन्द्रं मघवानमेनं महो रायो राधसो यद ददन्नः | यो अर्चतो बरह्मक्र्तिमविष्ठो यूयं पात ... ||
7.28.e: We will address this liberal Lord, this Indra, that he may grant us gifts of ample riches,  Best favourer of the singer's prayer and praises. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.29.d: अयं सोम इन्द्र तुभ्यं सुन्व आ तु पर याहि हरिवस्तदोकाः | पिबा तवस्य सुषुतस्य चारोर्ददो मघानि मघवन्नियानः ||
7.29.e: THIS Soma hath been pressed for thee, O Indra: come hither, Lord of Bays, for this thou lovest.  Drink of this fair, this well-effused libation: Maghavan, give us wealth when we implore thee.

7.29.d: बरह्मन वीर बरह्मक्र्तिं जुषाणो.अर्वाचीनो हरिभिर्याहि तूयम | अस्मिन्नू षु सवने मादयस्वोप बरह्माणि शर्णव इमा नः ||
7.29.e: Come to us quickly with thy Bay Steeds, Hero, come to our prayer, accepting our devotion.  Enjoy thyself aright at this libation, and listen thou unto the prayers we offer.

7.29.d: का ते अस्त्यरंक्र्तिः सूक्तैः कदा नूनं ते मघवन दाशेम | विश्वा मतीरा ततने तवायाधा म इन्द्र शर्णवो हवेमा ||
7.29.e: What satisfaction do our hymns afford thee? When, Maghavan? Now let us do thee service.  Hymns, only hymns, with love for thee, I weave thee: then hear, O Indra, these mine invocations.

7.29.d: उतो घा ते पुरुष्या इदासन येषां पूर्वेषामश्र्णोरषीणाम | अधाहं तवा मघवञ जोहवीमि तवं न इन्द्रासि परमतिः पितेव ||
7.29.e: They, verily, were also human beings whom thou wast wont to hear, those earlier sages.  Hence I, O Indra Maghavan, invoke thee: thou art our Providence, even as a Father.
We will address this liberal Lord, this Indra, that he may grant us gifts of ample riches,  Best favourer of the singer's prayer and praises. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.30.d: आ नो देव शवसा याहि शुष्मिन भवा वर्ध इन्द्र रायो अस्य | महे नर्म्णाय नर्पते सुवज्र महि कषत्राय पौंस्याय शूर ||
7.30.e: WITH power and strength, O Mighty God, approach us: be the augmenter, Indra, of these riches;  Strong Thunderer, Lord of men, for potent valour, for manly exploit and for high dominion.

7.30.d: हवन्त उ तवा हव्यं विवाचि तनूषु शूराः सूर्यस्य सातौ | तवं विश्वेषु सेन्यो जनेषु तवं वर्त्राणि रन्धया सुहन्तु ||
7.30.e: Thee, worth invoking, in the din of battle, heroes invoke in fray for life and sunlight.  Among all people thou art foremost fighter: give up our enemies to easy slaughter.

7.30.d: अहा यदिन्द्र सुदिना वयुछान दधो यत केतुमुपमं समत्सु | नयग्निः सीददसुरो न होता हुवानो अत्र सुभगाय देवान ||
7.30.e: When fair bright days shall dawn on us, O Indra, and thou shalt bring thy banner near in battle,  Agni the Asura shall sit as Herald, calling Gods hither for our great good fortune.

7.30.d: वयं ते त इन्द्र ये च देव सतवन्त शूर ददतो मघानि | यछा सूरिभ्य उपमं वरूथं सवाभुवो जरणामश्नवन्त ||
7.30.e: Thine are we, Indra, thine, both these who praise thee, and those who give rich gifts, O God and Hero.  Grant to our princes excellent protection, may they wax old and still be strong and happy.
We will address this liberal Lord, this Indra that he may grant us gifts of ample riches:  Best favourer of the singer's prayer and praises. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.31.d: पर व इन्द्राय मादनं हर्यश्वाय गायत | सखायः सोमपाव्ने ||
7.31.e: SING ye a song, to make him glad, to Indra, Lord of Tawny Steeds,  The Soma-drinker, O my friends.

7.31.d: शंसेदुक्थं सुदानव उत दयुक्षं यथा नरः | चक्र्मा सत्यराधसे ||
7.31.e: To him the Bounteous say the laud, and let us glorify, as men May do, the Giver of true gifts.

7.31.d: तवं न इन्द्र वाजयुस्त्वं गव्युः शतक्रतो | तवं हिरण्ययुर्वसो ||
7.31.e: O Indra, Lord of boundless might, for us thou winnest strength and kine,  Thou winnest gold for us, Good Lord.

7.31.d: वयमिन्द्र तवायवो.अभि पर णोनुमो वर्षन | विद्धी तवस्य नो वसो ||
7.31.e: Faithful to thee we loudly sing, heroic Indra, songs to thee: Mark, O Good Lord, this act of ours.

7.31.d: मा नो निदे च वक्तवे.अर्यो रन्धीरराव्णे | तवे अपि करतुर्मम ||
7.31.e: Give us not up to man's reproach, to foeman's hateful calumny: In thee alone is all my strength.

7.31.d: तवं वर्मासि सप्रथः पुरोयोधश्च वर्त्रहन | तवया परतिब्रुवे युजा ||
7.31.e: Thou art mine ample coat of mail, my Champion, Vṛtra-Slayer, thou:  With thee for Friend I brave the foe.

7.31.d: महानुतासि यस्य ते.अनु सवधावरी सहः | मम्नाते इन्द्ररोदसी ||
7.31.e: Yea, great art thou whose conquering might two independent Powers confess.  The Heaven, O India, and the Earth.

7.31.d: तं तवा मरुत्वती परि भुवद वाणी सयावरी | नक्षमाणा सह दयुभिः ||
7.31.e: So let the voice surround thee, which attends the Maruts on their way,  Reaching thee with the rays of light.

7.31.d: ऊर्ध्वासस्त्वान्विन्दवो भुवन दस्ममुप दयवि | सं ते नमन्त कर्ष्टयः ||
7.31.e: Let the ascending drops attain to thee, the Wondrous God, in heaven:  Let all the folk bow down to thee.

7.31.d: पर वो महे महिव्र्धे भरध्वं परचेतसे पर सुमतिं कर्णुध्वम | विशः पूर्वीः पर चरा चर्षणिप्राः ||
7.31.e: Bring to the Wise, the Great, who waxeth mighty, your offerings, and make ready your devotion;  To many clans he goeth, man's controller.

7.31.d: उरुव्यचसे महिने सुव्र्क्तिमिन्द्राय बरह्म जनयन्त विप्राः | तस्य वरतानि न मिनन्ति धीराः ||
7.31.e: For Indra, the sublime, the far-pervading, have singers generated prayer and praises:  The sages never violate his statutes.

7.31.d: इन्द्रं वाणीरनुत्तमन्युमेव सत्रा राजानं दधिरे सहध्यै | हर्यश्वाय बर्हया समापीन ||
7.31.e: The choirs have stablished Indra King for ever, for victory, him whose anger is resistless:  And, for the Bays' Lord, strengthened those he loveth.

7.32.d: मो षु तवा वाघतश्चनारे अस्मन नि रीरमन | आरात्ताच्चित सधमादं न आ गहीह वा सन्नुप शरुधि ||
7.32.e: LET none, no, not thy worshippers, delay thee far away from us.  Even from far away come thou unto our feast, or listen if already here.

7.32.d: इमे हि ते बरह्मक्र्तः सुते सचा मधौ न मक्ष आसते | इन्द्रे कामं जरितारो वसूयवो रथे न पादमा दधुः ||
7.32.e: For here, like flies on honey, these who pray to thee sit by the juice that they have poured.  Wealth-craving singers have on Indra set their hope, as men set foot upon a car.

7.32.d: रायस्कामो वज्रहस्तं सुदक्षिणं पुत्रो न पितरं हुवे ||
7.32.e: Longing for wealth I call on him, the Thunderer with the strong right hand,  As a son calleth on his sire.

7.32.d: इम इन्द्राय सुन्विरे सोमासो दध्याशिरः | ताना मदाय वज्रहस्त पीतये हरिभ्यां याह्योक आ ||
7.32.e: These Soma juices, mixed with curd, have been expressed for Indra here.  Come with thy Bay Steeds, Thunder-wielder, to our home, to drink them till they make thee glad.

7.32.d: शरवच्छ्रुत्कर्ण ईयते वसूनां नू चिन नो मर्धिषद गिरः | सद्यश्चिद यः सहस्राणि शता ददन नकिर्दित्सन्तमा मिनत ||
7.32.e: May he whose ear is open hear us. He is asked for wealth: will he despise our prayer?  Him who bestows at once a hundred thousand gifts none shall restrain when he would give.

7.32.d: स वीरो अप्रतिष्कुत इन्द्रेण शूशुवे नर्भिः | यस्ते गभीरा सवनानि वर्त्रहन सुनोत्या च धावति ||
7.32.e: The hero never checked by men hath gained his strength through Indra, he  Who presses out and pours his deep libations forth, O Vṛtra-slayer, unto thee.

7.32.d: भवा वरूथं मघवन मघोनां यत समजासि शर्धतः | वि तवाहतस्य वेदनं भजेमह्या दूणाशो भरा गयम ||
7.32.e: When thou dost drive the fighting men together be, thou Mighty One, the mighty's shield.  May we divide the wealth of him whom thou hast slain: bring us, Unreachable, his goods.

7.32.d: सुनोता सोमपाव्ने सोममिन्द्राय वज्रिणे | पचता पक्तीरवसे कर्णुध्वमित पर्णन्नित पर्णते मयः ||
7.32.e: For Indra, Soma-drinker, armed with thunder, press the Soma juice.  Make ready your dressed meats: cause him to favour us. The Giver blesses him who gives.

7.32.d: मा सरेधत सोमिनो दक्षता महे कर्णुध्वं राय आतुजे | तरणिरिज्जयति कषेति पुष्यति न देवासः कवत्नवे ||
7.32.e: Grudge not, ye Soma pourers; stir you, pay the rites, for wealth, to the great Conqueror.  Only the active conquers dwells in peace, and thrives: not for the niggard are the Gods.

7.32.d: नकिः सुदासो रथं पर्यास न रीरमत | इन्द्रो यस्याविता यस्य मरुतो गमत स गोमति वरजे ||
7.32.e: No one hath overturned or stayed the car of him who freely gives.  The man whom Indra and the Marut host defend comes to a stable full of kine.

7.32.d: गमद वाजं वाजयन्निन्द्र मर्त्यो यस्य तवमविता भुवः | अस्माकं बोध्यविता रथानामस्माकं शूर नर्णाम ||
7.32.e: Indra, that man when fighting shall obtain the spoil, whose strong defender thou wilt be.  Be thou the gracious helper, Hero I of our cars, be thou the helper of our men.

7.32.d: उदिन नयस्य रिच्यते.अंशो धनं न जिग्युषः | य इन्द्रोहरिवान न दभन्ति तं रिपो दक्षं दधाति सोमिनि ||
7.32.e: His portion is exceeding great like a victorious soldier's spoil.  Him who is Indra, Lord of Bays, no foes subdue. He gives the Soma-pourer strength.

7.32.d: मन्त्रमखर्वं सुधितं सुपेशसं दधात यज्ञियेष्वा | पूर्वीश्चन परसितयस्तरन्ति तं य इन्द्रे कर्मणा भुवत ||
7.32.e: Make for the Holy Gods a hymn that is not mean, but well-arranged and fair of form.  Even many snares and bonds subdue not him who dwells with Indra through his sacrifice.

7.32.d: कस्तमिन्द्र तवावसुमा मर्त्यो दधर्षति | शरद्धा इत तेमघवन पार्ये दिवि वाजी वाजं सिषासति ||
7.32.e: Indra, what mortal will attack the man who hath his wealth in thee?  The strong will win the spoil on the decisive day through faith in thee, O Maghavan.

7.32.d: मघोनः सम वर्त्रहत्येषु चोदय ये ददति परिया वसु | तवप्रणीती हर्यश्व सूरिभिर्विश्वा तरेम दुरिता ||
7.32.e: In battles with the foe urge on our mighty ones who give the treasures dear to thee,  And may we with our princes, Lord of Tawny Steeds! pass through all peril, led by thee.

7.32.d: तवेदिन्द्रावमं वसु तवं पुष्यसि मध्यमम | सत्रा विश्वस्य परमस्य राजसि नकिष टवा गोषु वर्ण्वते ||
7.32.e: Thine, Indra, is the lowest wealth, thou cherishest the mid-most wealth,  Thou ever rulest all the highest: in the fray for cattle none resisteth thee.

7.32.d: तवं विश्वस्य धनदा असि शरुतो य ईं भवन्त्याजयः | तवायं विश्वः पुरुहूत पार्थिवो.अवस्युर्नाम भिक्षते ||
7.32.e: Thou art renowned as giving wealth to every one in all the battles that are fought.  Craving protection, all these people of the earth, O Much-invoked, implore thy name.

7.32.d: यदिन्द्र यावतस्त्वमेतावदहमीशीय | सतोतारमिद दिधिषेय रदावसो न पापत्वाय रासीय ||
7.32.e: If I, O Indra, were the Lord of riches ample as thine own,  I should support the singer, God. who givest wealth! and not abandon him to woe.

7.32.d: शिक्षेयमिन महयते दिवे-दिवे राय आ कुहचिद्विदे | नहि तवदन्यन मघवन न आप्यं वस्यो अस्ति पिता चन ||
7.32.e: Each day would I enrich the man who sang my praise, in whatsoever place he were.  No kinship is there better, Maghavan, than thine: a father even is no more.

7.32.d: तरणिरित सिषासति वाजं पुरन्ध्या युजा | आ व इन्द्रम्पुरुहूतं नमे गिरा नेमिं तष्टेव सुद्र्वम ||
7.32.e: With Plenty for his true ally the active man will gain the spoil.  Your Indra, Much-invoked, I bend with song, as bends a wright his wheel of solid wood.

7.32.d: न दुष्टुती मर्त्यो विन्दते वसु न सरेधन्तं रयिर्नशत | सुशक्तिरिन मघवन तुभ्यं मावते देष्णं यत पार्ये दिवि ||
7.32.e: A moral wins no riches by unworthy praise: wealth comes not to the niggard churl.  Light is the task to give, O Maghavan, to one like me on the decisive day.

7.32.d: अभि तवा शूर नोनुमो.अदुग्धा इव धेनवः | ईशानमस्य जगतः सवर्द्र्शमीशानमिन्द्र तस्थुषः ||
7.32.e: Like kine unmilked we call aloud, Hero, to thee, and sing thy praise,  Looker on heavenly light, Lord of this moving world, Lord, Indra, of what moveth not.

7.32.d: न तवावानन्यो दिव्यो न पार्थिवो न जातो न जनिष्यते | अश्वायन्तो मघवन्निन्द्र वाजिनो गव्यन्तस्त्वा हवामहे ||
7.32.e: None other like to thee, of earth or of the heavens, hath been or ever will be born.  Desiring horses, Indra Maghavan! and kine, as men of might we call on thee.

7.32.d: अभी षतस्तदा भरेन्द्र जयायः कनीयसः | पुरूवसुर्हि मघवन सनादसि भरे-भरे च हव्यः ||
7.32.e: Bring, Indra, the Victorious Ones; bring, elder thou, the younger host.  For, Maghavan, thou art rich in treasures from of old, and must be called in every fight.

7.32.d: परा णुदस्व मघवन्नमित्रान सुवेदा नो वसू कर्धि | अस्माकं बोध्यविता महाधने भवा वर्धः सखीनाम ||
7.32.e: Drive thou away our enemies, O Maghavan: make riches easy to be won.  Be thou our good Protector in the strife for spoil: Cherisher of our friends be thou.

7.32.d: इन्द्र करतुं न आ भर पिता पुत्रेभ्यो यथा | शिक्षा णोस्मिन पुरुहूत यामनि जीवा जयोतिरशीमहि ||
7.32.e: O Indra, give us wisdom as a sire gives wisdom to his sons.  Guide us, O Much-invoked, in this our way may we still live and look upon the light.

7.32.d: मा नो अज्ञाता वर्जना दुराध्यो माशिवासो अव करमुः | तवया वयं परवतः शश्वतीरपो.अति शूर तरामसि ||
7.32.e: Grant that no mighty foes, unknown, malevolent, unhallowed, tread us to the ground.  With thine assistance, Hero, may we ass through all the waters that are rul`ng down.

7.33.d: शवित्यञ्चो मा दक्षिणतस्कपर्दा धियंजिन्वासो अभि हि परमन्दुः | उत्तिष्ठन वोचे परि बर्हिषो नॄन न मे दूरादवितवे वसिष्ठाः ||
7.33.e: THESE who wear hair-knots on the right, the movers of holy thought, white-robed, have won me over.  I warned the men, when from the grass I raised me, Not from afar can my Vasisthas help you.

7.33.d: दूरादिन्द्रमनयन्ना सुतेन तिरो वैशन्तमति पान्तमुग्रम | पाशद्युम्नस्य वायतस्य सोमात सुतादिन्द्रो.अव्र्णीतावसिष्ठान ||
7.33.e: With  Soma  they brought Indra from a distance, Over Vaisanta, from the strong libation.  Indra preferred Vasisthas to the Soma pressed by the son of Vayata, Pasadyumna.

7.33.d: एवेन नु कं सिन्धुमेभिस्ततारेवेन नु कं भेदमेभिर्जघान | एवेन नु कं दाशराज्ञे सुदासं परावदिन्द्रो बरह्मणा वो वसिष्ठाः ||
7.33.e: So, verily, with these he crossed the river, in company with these he slaughtered Bheda.  So in the fight with the Ten Kings, Vasisthas! did Indra help Sudās through your devotions.

7.33.d: जुष्टी नरो बरह्मणा वः पितॄणामक्षमव्ययं न किला रिषाथ | यच्छक्वरीषु बर्हता रवेणेन्द्रे शुष्ममदधाता वसिष्ठाः ||
7.33.e: I gladly, men I with prayer prayed by our fathers have fixed your axle: ye shall not be injured:  Since, when ye sang aloud the Sakvari verses, Vasisthas! ye invigorated Indra.

7.33.d: उद दयामिवेत तर्ष्णजो नाथितासो.अदीधयुर्दाशराज्ञे वर्तासः | वसिष्ठस्य सतुवत इन्द्रो अश्रोदुरुं तर्त्सुभ्यो अक्र्णोदु लोकम ||
7.33.e: Like thirsty men they looked to heaven, in battle with the Ten Kings, surrounded and imploring.  Then Indra heard Vasiṣṭha as he praised him, and gave the Trtsus ample room and freedom.

7.33.d: दण्डा इवेद गोजनास आसन परिछिन्ना भरता अर्भकासः | अभवच्च पुरेता वसिष्ठ आदित तर्त्सूनां विशो अप्रथन्त ||
7.33.e: Like sticks and staves wherewith they drive the cattle, Stripped bare, the Bharatas were found defenceless:  Vasiṣṭha then became their chief and leader: then widely. were the Trtsus' clans extended.

7.33.d: तरयः कर्ण्वन्ति भुवनेषु रेतस्तिस्रः परजा आर्या जयोतिरग्राः | तरयो घर्मास उषसं सचन्ते सर्वानित ताननुविदुर्वसिष्ठाः ||
7.33.e: Three fertilize the worlds with genial moisture: three noble Creatures cast a light before them.  Three that give warmth to all attend the morning. All these have they discovered, these Vasisthas.

7.33.d: सूर्यस्येव वक्षथो जयोतिरेषां समुद्रस्येव महिमा गभीरः | वातस्येव परजवो नान्येन सतोमो वसिष्ठा अन्वेतवे वः ||
7.33.e: Like the Sun's growing glory is their splendour, and like the sea's is their unflathomed greatness.  Their course is like the wind's. Your laud, Vasisthas, can never be attained by any other.

7.33.d: त इन निण्यं हर्दयस्य परकेतैः सहस्रवल्शमभि संचरन्ति | यमेन ततं परिधिं वयन्तो.अप्सरस उप सेदुर्वसिष्ठाः ||
7.33.e: They with perceptions of the heart in secret resort to that which spreads a thousand branches.  The Apsaras brought hither the Vasisthas wearing the vesture spun for them by Yama.

7.33.d: विद्युतो जयोतिः परि संजिहानं मित्रावरुणा यदपश्यतां तवा | तत ते जन्मोतैकं वसिष्ठागस्त्यो यत तवा विशाजभार ||
7.33.e: A form of lustre springing from the lightning wast thou, when Varuṇa and Mitra saw thee.  Tliy one and only birth was then, Vasiṣṭha, when from thy stock Agastya brought thee hither.

7.33.d: उतासि मैत्रावरुणो वसिष्ठोर्वश्या बरह्मन मनसो.अधि जातः | दरप्सं सकन्नं बरह्मणा दैव्येन विश्वे देवाः पुष्करे तवाददन्त ||
7.33.e: Born of their love for Urvasi, Vasiṣṭha thou, priest, art son of Varuṇa and Mitra;  And as a fallen drop, in heavenly fervour, all the Gods laid thee on a lotus-blossorn.

7.33.d: स परकेत उभयस्य परविद्वान सहस्रदान उत वा सदानः | यमेन ततं परिधिं वयिष्यन्नप्सरसः परि जज्ञे वसिष्ठः ||
7.33.e: He thinker, knower both of earth and heaven, endowed with many a gift, bestowing thousands,  Destined to wear the vesture spun by Yama, sprang from the Apsaras to life, Vasiṣṭha.

7.33.d: सत्रे ह जाताविषिता नमोभिः कुम्भे रेतः सिषिचतुः समानम | ततो ह मान उदियाय मध्यात ततो जातं रषिमाहुर्वसिष्ठम ||
7.33.e: Born at the sacrifice, urged by adorations, both with a common flow bedewed the pitcher.  Then from the midst thereof there rose up Māna, and thence they say was born the sage Vasiṣṭha.

7.33.d: उक्थभ्र्तं सामभ्र्तं बिभर्ति गरावाणं बिभ्रत पर वदात्यग्रे | उपैनमाध्वं सुमनस्यमाना आ वो गछाति परत्र्दो वसिष्ठः ||
7.33.e: He brings the bearer of the laud and Sāman: first shall he speak bringing the stone for pressing.  With grateful hearts in reverence approach him: to you, O Pratrdas, Vasiṣṭha cometh.

7.34.d: पर शुक्रैतु देवी मनीषा अस्मत सुतष्टो रथो न वाजी ||
7.34.e: MAY our divine and brilliant hymn go forth, like a swift chariot wrought and fashioned well.

7.34.d: विदुः पर्थिव्या दिवो जनित्रं शर्ण्वन्त्यापो अध कषरन्तीः ||
7.34.e: The waters listen as they flow along: they know the origin of heaven and earth.

7.34.d: आपश्चिदस्मै पिन्वन्त पर्थ्वीर्व्र्त्रेषु शूरा मंसन्त उग्राः ||
7.34.e: Yea, the broad waters swell their flood ior him: of him strong heroes think amid their foes.

7.34.d: आ धूर्ष्वस्मै दधाताश्वानिन्द्रो न वज्री हिरण्यबाहुः ||
7.34.e: Set ye for him the coursers to the pole: like Indra Thunderer is the Golden-armed.

7.34.d: अभि पर सथाताहेव यज्ञं यातेव पत्मन तमना हिनोत ||
7.34.e: Arouse you, like the days, to sacrifice speed gladly like a traveller on the way.

7.34.d: तमना समत्सु हिनोत यज्ञं दधात केतुं जनाय वीरम ||
7.34.e: Go swift to battles, to the sacrifice: set up a flag, a hero for the folk.

7.34.d: उदस्य शुष्माद भानुर्नार्त बिभर्ति भारं पर्थिवी नभूम ||
7.34.e: Up from his strength hath risen as ’twere a light: it bears the load as earth bears living things.

7.34.d: हवयामि देवानयातुरग्ने साधन्न्र्तेन धियं दधामि ||
7.34.e: Agni, no demon I invoke the Gods: by law completing it, I form a hymn.

7.34.d: अभि वो देवीं धियं दधिध्वं पर वो देवत्रा वाचं कर्णुध्वम ||
7.34.e: Closely albout you lay your heavenly song, and send your voice to where the Gods abide.

7.34.d: आ चष्ट आसां पाथो नदीनां वरुण उग्रः सहस्रचक्षाः ||
7.34.e: Varuṇa, Mighty, with a thousand eyes, beholds the paths wherein these rivers run.

7.34.d: राजा राष्ट्रानां पेशो नदीनामनुत्तमस्मै कषत्रं विश्वायु ||
7.34.e: He, King of kings, the glory of the floods, o’er all that liveth hath resistless sway.

7.34.d: अविष्टो अस्मान विश्वासु विक्ष्वद्युं कर्णोत शंसं निनित्सोः ||
7.34.e: May he assist us among all the tribes, and make the envier's praise devoid of light.

7.34.d: वयेतु दिद्युद दविषामशेवा युयोत विष्वग रपस्तनूनाम ||
7.34.e: May the foes' threatening arrow pass us by: may he put far from us our bodies' sin.

7.34.d: अवीन नो अग्निर्हव्यान नमोभिः परेष्ठो अस्मा अधायि सतोमः ||
7.34.e: Agni, oblation-cater, through our prayers aid us: to him our dearest laud is brought.

7.34.d: सजूर्देवेभिरपां नपातं सखायं कर्ध्वं शिवो नो अस्तु ||
7.34.e: Accordant with the Gods choose for our Friend the Waters’ Child: may he be good to us.

7.34.d: अब्जामुक्थैरहिं गर्णीषे बुध्ने नदीनां रजस्सु षीदन ||
7.34.e: With lauds I sing the Dragon born of floods: he sits beneath the streams in middle air.

7.34.d: मा नो.अहिर्बुध्न्यो रिषे धान मा यज्ञो अस्य सरिधद रतायोः ||
7.34.e: Ne’er may the Dragon of the Deep harm us: ne’er fail this faithful servant's sacrifice.

7.34.d: उत न एषु नर्षु शरवो धुः पर राये यन्तु शर्धन्तो अर्यः ||
7.34.e: To these our heroes may they grant renown: may pious men march boldly on to wealth.

7.34.d: तपन्ति शत्रुं सवर्ण भूमा महासेनासो अमेभिरेषाम ||
7.34.e: Leading great hosts, with fierce attacks of these, they burn their foes as the Sun burns the earth.

7.34.d: आ यन नः पत्नीर्गमन्त्यछा तवष्टा सुपाणिर्दधातुवीरान ||
7.34.e: What time our wives draw near to us, may he, left-handed Tvaṣṭar, give us hero sons.

7.34.d: परति न सतोमं तवष्टा जुषेत सयादस्मे अरमतिर्वसूयुः ||
7.34.e: May Tvaṣṭar find our hymn acceptable, and may Aramati, seeking wealth, be ours.

7.34.d: ता नो रासन रातिषाचो वसून्या रोदसी वरुणानी शर्णोतु | वरूत्रीभिः सुशरणो नो अस्तु तवष्टा सुदत्रो वि दधातु रायः ||
7.34.e: May they who lavish gifts bestow those treasures: may Rodasī and Varuṇānī listen.  May he, with the Varūtrīs, be our refuge, may bountiful Tvaṣṭar give us store of riches.

7.34.d: तन नो रायः पर्वतास्तन न आपस्तद रातिषाच ओषधीरुत दयौः | वनस्पतिभिः पर्थिवी सजोषा उभे रोदसी परि पासतो नः ||
7.34.e: So may rich Mountains and the liberal Waters, so may all Herbs that grow on ground, and Heaven,  And Earth accordant with the Forest-Sovrans, and both the World-halves round about protect us.

7.34.d: अनु तदुर्वी रोदसी जिहातामनु दयुक्षो वरुण इन्द्रसखा | अनु विश्वे मरुतो ये सहासो रायः सयाम धरुणं धियध्यै ||
7.34.e: To this may both the wide Worlds lend approval, and Varuṇa in heaven, whose Friend is Indra.  May all the Maruts give consent, the Victors, that we may hold great wealth in firm possession.

7.34.d: तन न इन्द्रो वरुणो मित्रो अग्निराप ओषधीर्वनिनो जुषन्त | शर्मन सयाम मरुतामुपस्थे यूयं पात ... ||
7.34.e: May Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni, Waters, Herbs, Trees accept the praise we offer.  May we find refuge in the Marut's bosom. Protect us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.35.d: शं न इन्द्राग्नी भवतामवोभिः शं न इन्द्रावरुणा रातहव्या | शमिन्द्रासोमा सुविताय शं योः शं न इन्द्रापूषणा वाजसातौ ||
7.35.e: BEFRIEND us with their aids Indra and Agni, Indra and Varuṇa who receive oblations!  Indra and Soma give health, strength and comfort, Indra and Pūṣan be our help in battle.

7.35.d: शं नो भगः शमु नः शंसो अस्तु शं नः पुरन्धिःशमु सन्तु रायः | शं नः सत्यस्य सुयमस्य शंसःशं नो अर्यमा पुरुजातो अस्तु ||
7.35.e: Auspicious Friends to us be Bhaga, Sathsa, auspicious be Purandhi aid all Riches;  The blessing of the true and well-conducted, and Aryaman in many forms apparent.

7.35.d: शं नो धाता शमु धर्ता नो अस्तु शं न उरूची भवतुस्वधाभिः | शं रोदसी बर्हती शं नो अद्रिः शं नोदेवानां सुहवानि सन्तु ||
7.35.e: Kind unto us he Maker and Sustainer, and the far-reaching Pair with God-like natures.  Auspicious unto us be Earth and Heaven, the Mountain, and the Gods’ fair invocations.

7.35.d: शं नो अग्निर्ज्योतिरनीको अस्तु शं नो मित्रावरुणावश्विना शम | शं नः सुक्र्तां सुक्र्तानि सन्तु शं न इषिरोभि वातु वातः ||
7.35.e: Favour us Agni with his face of splendour, and Varuva and Mitra and the Aśvins.  Favour us noble actions of the pious, impetuous vita blow on us with favour.

7.35.d: शं नो दयावाप्र्थिवी पूर्वहूतौ शमन्तरिक्षं दर्शयेनो अस्तु | शं न ओषधीर्वनिनो भवन्तु शं नो रजसस पतिरस्तु जिष्णुः ||
7.35.e: Early invoked, may Heaven and Earth be friendly, and Air's mid-region good for us to look on.  To us may Herbs and Forest-Trees be gracious, gracious the Lord Victorious of the region.

7.35.d: शं न इन्द्रो वसुभिर्देवो अस्तु शमादित्येभिर्वरुणः सुशंसः | शं नो रुद्रो रुद्रेभिर्जलाषः शं नस्त्वष्टा गनाभिरिह शर्णोतु ||
7.35.e: Be the God Indra with the Vasus friendly, and, with Ādityas, Varuṇa who blesseth.  Kind, with the Rudras, be the Healer Rudra, and, with the Dames, may Tvaṣṭar kindly listen.

7.35.d: शं नः सोमो भवतु बरह्म शं नः शं नो गरावाणःशमु सन्तु यज्ञाः | शं नः सवरूणां मितयो भवन्तु शं नः परस्वः शं वस्तु वेदिः ||
7.35.e: Blest unto us be Soma, and devotions, blest be the Sacrifice, the Stones for pressing.  Blest be the fixing of the sacred Pillars, blest be the tender Grass and blest the Altar.

7.35.d: शं नः सूर्य उरुचक्षा उदेतु शं नश्चतस्रः परदिशो भवन्तु | शं नः पर्वता धरुवयो भवन्तु शं नः सिन्धवः शमु सन्त्वापः ||
7.35.e: May the far-seeing Sun rise up to bless us: be the four Quarters of the sky auspicious.  Auspicious be the firmly-seated Mountains, auspicious be the Rivers and the Waters.

7.35.d: शं नो अदितिर्भवतु वरतेभिः शं नो भवन्तु मरुतः सवर्काः | शं नो विष्णुः शं उ पूषा नो अस्तु शं नो भवित्रं शं वस्तु वायुः ||
7.35.e: May Adid through holy works be gracioas, and may the Maruts, loud in song, be friendly.  May Viṣṇu give felicity, and Pūṣan, the Air that cherisheth our life, and Vāyu.

7.35.d: शं नो देवः सविता तरायमाणः शं नो भवन्तूषसो विभातीः | शं नः पर्जन्यो भवतु परजाभ्यः शं नःक्षेत्रस्य पतिरस्तु शम्भुः ||
7.35.e: Prosper us Savitar, the God who rescues, and let the radiant Mornings be propitious.  Auspicious to all creatures be Parjanya, auspicious be the field's benign Protector.

7.35.d: शं नो देवा विश्वदेवा भवन्तु शं सरस्वती सह धीभिरस्तु | शमभिषाचः शमु रातिषाचः शं नो दिव्याः पार्थिवाः शं नो अप्याः ||
7.35.e: May all the fellowship of Gods befriend us, Sarasvatī, with Holy Thoughts, be gracious.  Friendly be they, the Liberal Ones who seek us, yea, those who dwell in heaven, on earth, in waters.

7.35.d: शं नः सत्यस्य पतयो भवन्तु शं नो अर्वन्तः शमु सन्तु गावः | शं न रभवः सुक्र्तः सुहस्ताः शं नो भवन्तु पितरो हवेषु ||
7.35.e: May the great Lords of Truth protect and aid us: blest to us be our horses and our cattle.  Kind be the pious skilful-handed Ṛbhus, kind be the Fathers at our invocations.

7.35.d: शं नो अज एकपाद देवो अस्तु शं नो.अहिर्बुध्न्यः शं समुद्रः | शं नो अपां नपात पेरुरस्तु शं नः पर्श्निर्भवतु देवगोपा ||
7.35.e: May Aja-Ekapād, the God, be gracious, gracious the Dragon of the Deep, and Ocean.  Gracious be he the swelling Child of Waters, gracious be Pṛśni who hath Gods to guard her.

7.35.d: आदित्या रुद्रा वसवो जुषन्तेदं बरह्म करियमाणं नवीयः | शर्ण्वन्तु नि दिव्याः पार्थिवासो गोजाता उत ये यज्ञियासः ||
7.35.e: So may the Rudras, Vasus, and Ādityas accept the new hymn which we now are making.  May all the Holy Ones of earth and heaven, and the Cow's offipring hear our invocation.

7.35.d: ये देवानां यज्ञिया यज्ञियानां मनोर्यजत्रा अम्र्ता रतज्ञाः | ते नो रासन्तामुरुगायमद्य यूयं पात ... ||
7.35.e: They who of Holy Gods are very holy, Immortal, knowing Law, whom man must worship,—  May these to-day give us broad paths to travel. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.36.d: पर बरह्मैतु सदनाद रतस्य वि रश्मिभिः सस्र्जे सूर्यो गाः | वि सानुना पर्थिवी सस्र उर्वी पर्थु परतीकमध्येधे अग्निः ||
7.36.e: LET the prayer issue from the seat of Order, for Sūrya with his beams hath loosed the cattle.  With lofty ridges earth is far extended, and Agni's flame hath lit the spacious surface.

7.36.d: इमां वां मित्रावरुणा सुव्र्क्तिमिषं न कर्ण्वे असुरा नवीयः | इनो वामन्यः पदवीरदब्धो जनं च मित्रो यतति बरुवाणः ||
7.36.e: O Asuras, O Varuṇa and Mitra, this hymn to you, like food, anew I offer.  One of you is a strong unerring Leader, and Mitra, speaking, stirreth men to labour.

7.36.d: आ वातस्य धरजतो रन्त इत्या अपीपयन्त धेनवो न सूदाः | महो दिवः सदने जायमानो.अचिक्रदद वर्षभः सस्मिन्नूधन ||
7.36.e: The movements of the gliding wind come hither: like cows, the springs are filled to overflowing.  Born in the station e’en of lofty heaven the Bull hath loudly bellowed in this region.

7.36.d: गिरा य एता युनजद धरी त इन्द्र परिया सुरथा शूर धायू | पर यो मन्युं रिरिक्षतो मिनात्या सुक्रतुमर्यमणं वव्र्त्याम ||
7.36.e: May I bring hither with my song, O Indra, wise Aryaman who yokes thy dear Bay Horses,  Voracious, with thy noble car, O Hero, him who defeats the wrath of the malicious.

7.36.d: यजन्ते अस्य सख्यं वयश्च नमस्विनः सव रतस्य धामन | वि पर्क्षो बाबधे नर्भि सतवान इदं नमो रुद्राय परेष्ठम ||
7.36.e: In their own place of sacrifice adorers worship to gain long life and win his friendship.  He hath poured food on men when they have praised him; be this, the dearest reverence, paid to Rudra.

7.36.d: आ यत साकं यशसो वावशानाः सरस्वती सप्तथी सिन्धुमाता | याः सुष्वयन्त सुदुघाः सुधारा अभि सवेन पयसा पीप्यानाः ||
7.36.e: Coming together, glorious, loudly roaring - Sarasvatī, Mother of Floods, the seventh-  With copious milk, with fair streams, strongly flowing, full swelling with the volume of their water;

7.36.d: उत तये नो मरुतो मन्दसाना धियं तोकं च वाजिनो.अवन्तु | मा नः परि खयदक्षरा चरन्त्यवीव्र्धन युज्यं ते रयिं नः ||
7.36.e: And may the mighty Maruts, too, rejoicing, aid our devotion and protect our offspring.  Let not swift-moving Aksara neglect us: they have increased our own appropriate riches,

7.36.d: पर वो महीमरमतिं कर्णुध्वं पर पूषणं विदथ्यं न वीरम | भगं धियो.अवितारं नो अस्याः सातौ वाजं रातिषाचं पुरन्धिम ||
7.36.e: Bring ye the great Aramati before you, and Pūṣan as the Hero of the synod,  Bhaga who looks upon this hymn with favour, and, as our strength, the bountiful Purandbi.

7.36.d: अछायं वो मरुतः शलोक एत्वछा विष्णुं निषिक्तपामवोभिः | उत परजायै गर्णते वयो धुर्यूयं पात ... ||
7.36.e: May this our song of praise reach you, O Maruts, and Viṣṇu guardian of the future infant.  May they vouchsafe the singer strength for offspring. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.37.d: आ वो वाहिष्ठो वहतु सतवध्यै रथो वाजा रभुक्षणो अम्र्क्तः | अभि तरिप्र्ष्ठैः सवनेषु सोमैर्मदे सुशिप्रा महभिः पर्णध्वम ||
7.37.e: LET your best-bearing car that must be lauded, ne’er injured, bring you Vājas and Ṛbhukṣans.  Fill you, fair-helmeted! with mighty Soma, thrice-mixed, at our libations to delight you.

7.37.d: यूयं ह रत्नं मघवत्सु धत्थ सवर्द्र्श रभुक्षणो अम्र्क्तम | सं यज्ञेषु सवधावन्तः पिबध्वं वि नो राधांसि मतिभिर्दयध्वम ||
7.37.e: Ye who behold the light of heaven, Ṛbhukṣans, give our rich patrons unmolested riches.  Drink, heavenly-natured. at our sacrifices, and give us bounties for the hymns we sing you.

7.37.d: उवोचिथ हि मघवन देष्णं महो अर्भस्य वसुनो विभागे | उभा ते पूर्णा वसुना गभस्ती न सून्र्ता नि यमते वसव्या ||
7.37.e: For thou, O Bounteous One, art used to giving, at parting treasure whether small or ample.  Filled full are both thine arms with great possessions: thy goodness keeps thee not from granting riches.

7.37.d: तवमिन्द्र सवयशा रभुक्षा वाजो न साधुरस्तमेष्य रक्वा | वयं नु ते दाश्वांसः सयाम बरह्म कर्ण्वन्तो हरिवो वसिष्ठाः ||
7.37.e: Indra, high-famed, as Vāja and Ṛbhukṣans, thou goest working, singing to the dwelling.  Lord of Bay Steeds, this day may we Vasisthas offer our prayers to thee and bring oblations.

7.37.d: सनितासि परवतो दाशुषे चिद याभिर्विवेषो हर्यश्व धीभिः | ववन्मा नु ते युज्याभिरूती कदा न इन्द्र राय आ दशस्येः ||
7.37.e: Thou winnest swift advancement for thy servant, through hymns, Lord of Bay Steeds, which thou hast favoured.  For thee with friendly succour have we battled, and when, O Indra, wilt thou grant us riches?

7.37.d: वासयसीव वेधसस्त्वं नः कदा न इन्द्र वचसो बुबोधः | अस्तं तात्या धिया रयिं सुवीरं पर्क्षो नो अर्वा नयुहीत वाजी ||
7.37.e: To us thy priests a home, as ’twere, thou givest: when, Indra wilt thou recognize our praises?  May thy strong Steed, through our ancestral worship, bring food and wealth with heroes to our dwelling.

7.37.d: अभि यं देवी निरतिश्चिदीशे नक्षन्त इन्द्रं शरदःसुप्र्क्षः | उप तरिबन्धुर्जरदष्टिमेत्यस्ववेशं यं कर्णवन्त मर्ताः ||
7.37.e: Though Nirrti the Goddess reigneth round him, Autumns with food in plenty come to Indra.  With three close Friends to length of days he cometh, he whom men let not rest at home in quiet.

7.37.d: आ नो राधांसि सवितः सतवध्या आ रायो यन्तु पर्वतस्यरातौ | सदा नो दिव्यः पायुः सिषक्तु यूयं पात ... ||
7.37.e: Promise us gifts, O Savitar: may riches come unto us in Parvata's full bounty.  May the Celestial Guardian still attend us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.38.d: उदु षय देवः सविता ययाम हिरण्ययीममतिं यामशिश्रेत | नूनं भगो हव्यो मानुषेभिर्वि यो रत्ना पुरूवसुर्दधाति ||
7.38.e: ON high hath Savitar, this God, extended the golden lustre which he spreads around him.  Now, now must Bhaga be invoked by mortals, Lord of great riches who distributes treasures.

7.38.d: उदु तिष्ठ सवितः शरुध्यस्य हिरण्यपाणे परभ्र्ताव रतस्य | वयुर्वीं पर्थ्वीममतिं सर्जान आ नर्भ्यो मर्तभोजनं सुवानः ||
7.38.e: Rise up, O Savitar whose hands are golden, and hear this man while sacrifice is offered,  Spreading afar thy broad and wide effulgence, and bringing mortal men the food that feeds them.

7.38.d: अपि षटुतः सविता देवो अस्तु यमा चिद विश्वे वसवो गर्णन्ति | स न सतोमान नमस्यश्चनो धाद विश्वेभिः पातु पायुभिर्नि सूरीन ||
7.38.e: Let Savitar the God he hymned with praises, to whom the Vasus, even, all sing glory.  Sweet be our lauds to him whose due is worship: may he with all protection guard our princes.

7.38.d: अभि यं देव्यदितिर्ग्र्णाति सवं देवस्य सवितुर्जुषाणा | अभि सम्राजो वरुणो गर्णन्त्यभि मित्रासो अर्यमा सजोषाः ||
7.38.e: Even he whom Aditi the Goddess praises, rejoicing in God Savitar's incitement:  Even he who praise the high imperial Rulers, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, sing in concert.

7.38.d: अभि ये मिथो वनुषः सपन्ते रातिं दिवो रातिषाचः पर्थिव्याः | अहिर्बुध्न्य उत नः शर्णोतु वरूत्र्येकधेनुभिर्नि पातु ||
7.38.e: They who come emulous to our oblation, dispensing bounty, from the earth and heaven.  May they and Ahibudhnya hear our calling: guard us Varūtrī with the Ekadhenus.

7.38.d: अनु तन नो जास्पतिर्मंसीष्ट रत्नं देवस्य सवितुरियानः | भगमुग्रो.अवसे जोहवीति भगमनुग्रो अध याति रत्नम ||
7.38.e: This may the Lord of Life, entreated, grant us,—the wealth which Savitar the God possesses.  The mighty calls on Bhaga for protection, on Bhaga calls the weak to give him riches.

7.38.d: शं नो भवन्तु वाजिनो हवेषु देवताता मितद्रवः सवर्काः | जम्भयन्तो.अहिं वर्कं रक्षांसि सनेम्यस्मद युयवन्नमीवाः ||
7.38.e: Bless us the Vajins when we call, while slowly they move, strong Singers, to the Gods’ assembly.  Crushing the wolf, the serpent, and the demons, may they completely banish all affliction.

7.38.d: वाजे-वाजे.अवत वाजिनो नो धनेषु विप्रा अम्र्ता रतज्ञाः | अस्य मध्वः पिबत मादयध्वं तर्प्ता यात पथिभिर्देवयानैः ||
7.38.e: Deep-skilled in Law eternal, deathless, Singers, O Vajins, help us in each fray for booty.  Drink of this meath, he satisfied, be joyful: then go on paths which Gods are wont to travel.
