7.39.d: ऊर्ध्वो अग्निः सुमतिं वस्वो अश्रेत परतीची जूर्णिर्देवतातिमेति | भेजाते अद्री रथ्येव पन्थां रतं होता न इषितो यजाति ||
7.39.e: AGNI, erect, hath shown enriching favour: the flame goes forward to the Gods’ assembly.  Like car-borne men the stones their path have chosen: let the priest, quickened, celebrate our worship.

7.39.d: पर वाव्र्जे सुप्रया बर्हिरेषामा विश्पतीव बीरिट इयाते | विशामक्तोरुषसः पूर्वहूतौ वायुः पूषा सवस्तये नियुत्वान ||
7.39.e: Soft to the tread, their sacred grass is scattered: these go like Kings amid the band around them,  At the folks early call on Night and Morning,—Vāyu, and Pūṣan with his team, to bless us.

7.39.d: जमया अत्र वसवो रन्त देवा उरावन्तरिक्षे मर्जयन्त शुभ्राः | अर्वाक पथ उरुज्रयः कर्णुध्वं शरोता दूतस्य जग्मुषो नो अस्य ||
7.39.e: Here on their path the noble Gods proceeded: in the wide firmament the Beauteous decked them.  Bend your way hither, ye who travel widely: hear this our envoy who hath gone to meet you.

7.39.d: ते हि यज्ञेषु यज्ञियास ऊमाः सधस्थं विश्वे अभि सन्ति देवाः | तानध्वर उशतो यक्ष्यग्ने शरुष्टी भगं नासत्या पुरन्धिम ||
7.39.e: For they are holy aids at sacrifices: all Gods approach the place of congregation.  Bring these, desirous, to our worship, Agni, swift the Nisatyas, Bhaga, and Purandhi.

7.39.d: आग्ने गिरो दिव आ पर्थिव्या मित्रं वह वरुणमिन्द्रमग्निम | आर्यमणमदितिं विष्णुमेषां सरस्वती मरुतो मादयन्ताम ||
7.39.e: Agni, to these men's hymns, from earth, from heaven, bring Mitra, Varuṇa, Indra, and Agni,  And Aryaman, and Aditi, and Viṣṇu. Sarasvatī be joyful, and the Maruts.

7.39.d: ररे हव्यं मतिभिर्यज्ञियानां नक्षत कामं मर्त्यानामसिन्वन | धाता रयिमविदस्यं सदासां सक्षीमहि युज्येभिर्नु देवैः ||
7.39.e: Even as the holy wish, the gift is offered: may he, unsated, come when men desire him.  Give never-failing ever-conquering riches: with Gods for our allies may we be victors.

7.39.d: नू रोदसी अभिष्टुते वसिष्ठैरतावानो वरुणो मित्रो अग्निः | यछन्तु चन्द्रा उपमं नो अर्कं यूयं पात ... ||
7.39.e: Now have both worlds been praised by the Vasisthas; and holy Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni.  May they, bright Deities, make our song supremest. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.40.d: ओ शरुष्टिर्विदथ्या समेतु परति सतोमं दधीमहि तुराणाम | यदद्य देवः सविता सुवाति सयामास्य रत्निनो विभागे ||
7.40.e: BE gathered all the audience of the synod: let us begin their praise whose course is rapid.  Whate’er God Savitar this day produces, may we be where the Wealthy One distributes.

7.40.d: मित्रस्तन नो वरुणो रोदसी च दयुभक्तमिन्द्रो अर्यमा ददातु | दिदेष्टु देव्यदिती रेक्णो वायुश्च यन नियुवैते भगश्च ||
7.40.e: This, dealt from heaven ' may both the Worlds vouchsafe us, and Varuṇa, Indra, Aryaman, and Mitra.  May Goddess Aditi assign us riches, Vāyu and Bhaga make them ours for ever.

7.40.d: सेदुग्रो अस्तु मरुतः स शुष्मी यं मर्त्यं पर्षदश्वा अवाथ | उतेमग्निः सरस्वती जुनन्ति न तस्य रायः पर्येतास्ति ||
7.40.e: Strong be the man and full of power, O Maruts, whom ye, borne on by spotted coursers, favour.  Him, too, Sarasvatī and Agni further, and there is none to rob him of his riches.

7.40.d: अयं हि नेता वरुण रतस्य मित्रो राजानो अर्यमापो धुः | सुहवा देव्यदितिरनर्वा ते नो अंहो अति पर्षन्नरिष्टान ||
7.40.e: This Varuṇa is guide of Law, he, Mitra, and Aryaman, the Kings, our work have finished.  Divine and foeless Aditi quickly listens. May these deliver us unharmed from trouble.

7.40.d: अस्य देवस्य मीळ्हुषो वया विष्णोरेषस्य परभ्र्थे हविर्भिः | विदे हि रुद्रो रुद्रियं महित्वं यासिष्टं वर्तिरश्विनाविरावत ||
7.40.e: With offerings I propitiate the branches of this swift-moving God, the bounteous Viṣṇu.  Hence Rudra gained his Rudra-strength: O Aśvins, ye sought the house that hath celestial viands.

7.40.d: मात्र पूषन्नाघ्र्ण इरस्यो वरूत्री यद रातिषाचश्च रासन | मयोभुवो नो अर्वन्तो नि पान्तु वर्ष्टिं परिज्मा वातो ददातु ||
7.40.e: Be not thou angry here, O glowing Pūṣan, for what Varūtrī and the Bounteous gave us.  May the swift-moving Gods protect and bless us, and Vāta send us rain, wha wanders round us.
Now have both worlds been praised by the Vasisthas, and holy Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni.  May they, bright Deities, make our song supremest. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.41.d: परातरग्निं परातरिन्द्रं हवामहे परातर्मित्रावरुणाप्रातरश्विना | परातर्भगं पूषणं बरह्मणस पतिं परातः सोममुत रुद्रं हुवेम ||
7.41.e: AGNI at dawn, and Indra we invoke at dawn, and Varuṇa and Mitra, and the Aśvins twain.  Bhaga at dawn, Pūṣan, and Brahmaṇaspati, Soma at dawn, Rudra we will invoke at dawn.

7.41.d: परातर्जितं भगमुग्रं हुवेम वयं पुत्रमदितेर्यो विधर्ता | आध्रश्चिद यं मन्यमानस्तुरश्चिद राजा चिद यं भगं भक्षीत्याह ||
7.41.e: We will invoke strong, early-conquering Bhaga, the Son of Aditi, the great supporter:  Thinking of whom, the poor, yea, even the mighty, even the King himself says, Give me Bhaga.

7.41.d: भग परणेतर्भग सत्यराधो भगेमां धियमुदवा ददन नः | भग पर णो जनय गोभिरश्वैर्भग पर नर्भिर्न्र्वन्तः सयाम ||
7.41.e: Bhaga our guide, Bhaga whose gifts are faithful, favour this song, and give us wealth, O Bhaga.  Bhaga, augment our store of kine and horses, Bhaga, may we be rich in men and heroes.

7.41.d: उतेदानीं भगवन्तः सयामोत परपित्व उत मध्ये अह्नाम | उतोदिता मघवन सूर्यस्य वयं देवानां सुमतौ सयाम ||
7.41.e: So may felicity be ours at present, and when the day approaches, and at noontide;  And may we still, O Bounteous One, at sunset be happy in the Deities' loving-kindness.

7.41.d: भग एव भगवानस्तु देवास्तेन वयं भगवन्तः सयाम | तं तवा भग सर्व इज्जोहवीति स नो भग पुरेता भवेह ||
7.41.e: May Bhaga verily be bliss-bestower, and through him, Gods! may happiness attend us.  As such, O Bhaga, all with might invoke thee: as such be thou our Champion here, O Bhaga.

7.41.d: समध्वरायोषसो नमन्त दधिक्रावेव शुचये पदाय | अर्वाचीनं वसुविदं भगं नो रथमिवाश्वा वाजिन आ वहन्तु ||
7.41.e: To this our worship may all Dawns incline them, and come to the pure place like Dadhikrāvan.  As strong steeds draw a chariot may they bring us hitherward Bhaga who discovers treasure.

7.41.d: अश्वावतीर्गोमतीर्न उषासो वीरवतीः सदमुछन्तु भद्राः | घर्तं दुहाना विश्वतः परपीता यूयं पात ... ||
7.41.e: May blessed Mornings dawn on us for ever, with wealth of kine, of horses, and of heroes,  Streaming with all abundance, pouring fatness. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.42.d: पर बरह्माणो अङगिरसो नक्षन्त पर करन्दनुर्नभन्यस्य वेतु | पर धेनव उदप्रुतो नवन्त युज्यातामद्री अध्वरस्य पेशः ||
7.42.e: LET Brahmans and Aṅgirases come forward, and let the roar of cloudy heaven surround us.  Loud low the Milch-kine swimming in the waters: set be the stones that grace our holy service.

7.42.d: सुगस्ते अग्ने सनवित्तो अध्वा युक्ष्वा सुते हरितो रोहितश्च | ये वा सद्मन्नरुषा वीरवाहो हुवे देवानां जनिमानिसत्तः ||
7.42.e: Fair, Agni, is thy long-known path to travel: yoke for the juice tfiy bay, thy ruddy horses,  Or red steeds, Hero-bearing, for the chamber. Seated, I call the Deities' generations.

7.42.d: समु वो यज्ञं महयन नमोभिः पर होता मन्द्रो रिरिच उपाके | यजस्व सु पुर्वणीक देवाना यज्ञियामरमतिं वव्र्त्याः ||
7.42.e: They glorify your sacrifice with worship, yet the glad Priest near them is left unequalled.  Bring the Gods hither, thou of many aspects: turn hitherward Aramati the Holy.

7.42.d: यदा वीरस्य रेवतो दुरोणे सयोनशीरतिथिराचिकेतत | सुप्रीतो अग्निः सुधितो दम आ स विशे दाति वार्यमियत्यै ||
7.42.e: What time the Guest hath made himself apparent, at ease reclining in the rich man's dwelling,  Agni, well-pleased, well-placed within the chamber gives to a house like this wealth worth the choosing.

7.42.d: इमं नो अग्ने अध्वरं जुषस्व मरुत्स्विन्द्रे यशसं कर्धी नः | आ नक्ता बर्हिः सदतामुषासोशन्ता मित्रावरुणायजेह ||
7.42.e: Accept this sacrifice of ours, O Agni; glorify it with Indra and the Maruts.  Here on our grass let Night and Dawn be seated: bring longing Varuṇa and Mitra hither.

7.42.d: एवाग्निं सहस्यं वसिष्ठो रायस्कामो विश्वप्स्न्यस्य सतौत | इषं रयिं पप्रथद वाजमस्मे यूयं पात ... ||
7.42.e: Thus hath Vasiṣṭha praised victorious Agni, yearning for wealth that giveth all subsistence.  May he bestow on us food, strength, and riches. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.43.d: पर वो यज्ञेषु देवयन्तो अर्चन दयावा नमोभिः परिथिवी इषध्यै | येषां बरह्माण्यसमानि विप्रा विष्वग वियन्ति वनिनो न शाखाः ||
7.43.e: SING out the pious at your sacrifices to move with adorations Earth and Heaven-  The Holy Singers, whose unmatched devotions, like a tree's branches, part in all directions.

7.43.d: पर यज्ञ एतु हेत्वो न सप्तिरुद यछध्वं समनसो घर्ताचीः | सत्र्णीत बर्हिरध्वराय साधूर्ध्वा शोचींषि देवयून्यस्थुः ||
7.43.e: Let sacrifice proceed like some fleet courser: with one accord lift ye on high the ladles.  Strew sacred grass meet for the solenm service: bright flames that love the Gods have mounted upward.

7.43.d: आ पुत्रासो न मातरं विभ्र्त्राः सानौ देवासो बर्हिषःसदन्तु | आ विश्वाची विदथ्यामनक्त्वग्ने मा नो देवताता मर्धस कः ||
7.43.e: Like babes in arms reposing on their mother, let the Gods sit upon the grass's summit.  Let general fire make bright the flame of worship: scorn us not, Agni, in the Gods’ assembly.

7.43.d: ते सीषपन्त जोषमा यजत्रा रतस्य धाराः सुदुघा दुहानाः | जयेष्ठं वो अद्य मह आ वसूनामा गन्तन समनसो यति षठ ||
7.43.e: Gladly the Gods have let themselves be honoured, milking the copious streams of holy Order.  The highest might to-day is yours, the Vasits': come ye, as many as ye are, one-minded.

7.43.d: एवा नो अग्ने विक्ष्वा दशस्य तवया वयं सहसावन्नास्क्राः | राया युजा सधमादो अरिष्टा यूयं पात ... ||
7.43.e: So, Agni, send us wealth among the people: may we be closely knit to thee, O Victor,  Unharmed, and rich, and taking joy together. Preserve us evermore, ye ods, with blessings.

7.44.d: दधिक्रां वः परथममश्विनोषसमग्निं समिद्धं भगमूतये हुवे | इन्द्रं विष्णुं पूषणं बरह्मणस पतिमादित्यान दयावाप्र्थिवी अपः सवः ||
7.44.e: I CALL on Dadhikrās, the first, to give you aid, the Aśvins, Bhaga, Dawn, and Agni kindled well,  Indra, and Viṣṇu, Pūṣan, Brahmaṇaspati, Ādityas, Heaven and Earth, the Waters, and the Light.

7.44.d: दधिक्रामु नमसा बोधयन्त उदीराणा यज्ञमुपप्रयन्तः | इळां देवीं बर्हिषि सादयन्तो.अश्विना विप्रा सुहवाहुवेम ||
7.44.e: When, rising, to the sacrifice we hasten, awaking Dadhikrās with adorations.  Seating on sacred grass the Goddess Iḷā. let us invoke the sage swift-hearing Aśvins.

7.44.d: दधिक्रावाणं बुबुधानो अग्निमुप बरुव उषसं सूर्यं गाम | बरध्नं मांश्चतोर्वरुणस्य बभ्रुं ते विश्वास्मद दुरिता यावयन्तु ||
7.44.e: While I am thus arousing Dadhikrāvan I speak to Agni, Earth, and Dawn, and Sūrya,  The red, the brown of Varuṇa ever mindful: may they ward off from us all grief and trouble.

7.44.d: दधिक्रावा परथमो वाज्यर्वाग्रे रथानां भवति परजानन | संविदान उषसा सूर्येणादित्येभिर्वसुभिरङगिरोभिः ||
7.44.e: Foremost is Dadhikrāvan, vigorous courser; in forefront of the cars, his way he knoweth,  Closely allied with Sūrya and with Morning, Ādityas, and Aṅgirases, and Vasus.

7.44.d: आ नो दधिक्राः पथ्यामनक्त्व रतस्य पन्थामन्वेतवा उ | शर्णोतु नो दैव्यं शर्धो अग्निः शर्ण्वन्तु विश्वे महिषामूराः ||
7.44.e: May Dadhikrās prepare the way we travel that we may pass along the path of Order.  May Agni bear us, and the Heavenly Army: hear us all Mighty Ones whom none deceiveth.

7.45.d: आ देवो यातु सविता सुरत्नो.अन्तरिक्षप्रा वहमानो अश्वैः | हस्ते दधानो नर्या पुरूणि निवेशयञ्च परसुवञ्च भूम ||
7.45.e: MAY the God Savitar, rich in goodly treasures, filling the region, borne by steeds, come hither,  In his hand holding much that makes men happy, lulling to slumber and arousing creatures.

7.45.d: उदस्य बाहू शिथिरा बर्हन्ता हिरण्यया दिवो अन्ताननष्टाम | नूनं सो अस्य महिमा पनिष्ट सूरश्चिदस्मा अनु दादपस्याम ||
7.45.e: Golden, sublime, and easy in their motion, his arms extend unto the bounds of heaven.  Now shall that mightiness of his he lauded: even Sūrya yields to him in active vigour.

7.45.d: स घा नो देवः सविता सहावा साविषद वसुपतिर्वसूनि | विश्रयमाणो अमतिमुरूचीं मर्तभोजनमध रासते नः ||
7.45.e: May this God Savitar, the Strong and Mighty, the Lord of precious wealth, vouchsafe us treasures.  May he, advancing his far-spreading lustre, bestow on us the food that feedeth mortals.

7.45.d: इमा गिरः सवितारं सुजिह्वं पूर्णगभस्तिमीळते सुपाणिम | चित्रं वयो बर्हदस्मे दधातु यूयं पात ... ||
7.45.e: These songs praise Savitar whose tongue is pleasant, praise him whose arms are full, whose hands are lovely.  High vital strength, and manifold, may he grant us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.46.d: इमा रुद्राय सथिरधन्वने गिरः कषिप्रेषवे देवाय सवधाव्ने | अषाळ्हाय सहमानाय वेधसे तिग्मायुधाय भरता शर्णोतु नः ||
7.46.e: To Rudra bring these songs, whose bow is firm and strong, the self-dependent God with swiftly-flying shafts,  The Wise, the Conqueror whom none may overcome, armed with sharp-pointed weapons: may he hear our call.

7.46.d: स हि कषयेण कषम्यस्य जन्मनः साम्राज्येन दिव्यस्य चेतति | अवन्नवन्तीरुप नो दुरश्चरानमीवो रुद्र जासु नो भव ||
7.46.e: He through his lordship thinks on beings of the earth, on heavenly beings through his high imperial sway.  Come willingly to our doors that gladly welcome thee, and heal all sickness, Rudra., in our families.

7.46.d: या ते दिद्युदवस्र्ष्टा दिवस परि कष्मया चरति परि साव्र्णक्तु नः | सहस्रं ते सवपिवात भेषजा मा नस्तोकेषुतनयेषु रीरिषह ||
7.46.e: May thy bright arrow which, shot down by thee from heaven, flieth upon the earth, pass us uninjured by.  Thou, very gracious God, hast thousand medicines: inflict no evil on our sons or progeny.

7.46.d: मा नो वधी रुद्र मा परा दा मा ते भूम परसितौ हीळितस्य | आ नो भज बर्हिषि जीवशंसे यूयं पात ... ||
7.46.e: Slay us not, nor abandon us, O Rudra let not thy noose, when thou art angry, seize us.  Give us trimmed grass and fame among the living. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.47.d: आपो यं वः परथमं देवयन्त इन्द्रपानमूर्मिमक्र्ण्वतेळः | तं वो वयं शुचिमरिप्रमद्य घर्तप्रुषं मधुमन्तं वनेम ||
7.47.e: MAY we obtain this day from you, O Waters, that wave of pure refreshment, which the pious  Made erst the special beverage of Indra, bright, stainless, rich in sweets and dropping fatness.

7.47.d: तमूर्मिमापो मधुमत्तमं वो.अपां नपादवत्वाशुहेमा | यस्मिन्निन्द्रो वसुभिर्मादयाते तमश्याम देवयन्तो वो अद्य ||
7.47.e: May the Floods' Offspring, he whose course is rapid, protect that wave most rich in sweets, O Waters,  That shall make Indra and the Vasus joyful. This may we gain from you to-day, we pious.

7.47.d: शतपवित्राः सवधया मदन्तीर्देवीर्देवानामपि यन्ति पाथः | ता इन्द्रस्य न मिनन्ति वरतानि सिन्धुभ्यो हव्यं घर्तवज्जुहोत ||
7.47.e: All-purifying, joying in their nature, to paths of Gods the Goddesses move onward.  They never violate the laws of Indra. Present the oil-rich offering to the Rivers.

7.47.d: याः सूर्यो रश्मिभिराततान याभ्य इन्द्रो अरदद गातुमूर्मिम | ते सिन्धवो वरिवो धातना नो यूयं पात ... ||
7.47.e: Whom Sūrya with his bright beams hath attracted, and Indra dug the path for them to travel,  May these Streams give us ample room and freedom. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.48.d: रभुक्षणो वाजा मादयध्वमस्मे नरो मघवानः सुतस्य | आ वो.अर्वाचः करतवो न यातां विभ्वो रथं नर्यं वर्तयन्तु ||
7.48.e: YE liberal Heroes, Vājas and Ṛbhukṣans, come and delight you with our flowing Soma.  May your strength, Vibhus, as ye come to meet us, turn hitherward your car that brings men profit.

7.48.d: रभुरभुभिरभि वः सयाम विभ्वो विभुभिः शवसा शवांसि | वाजो अस्मानवतु वाजसाताविन्द्रेण युजा तरुषेमव्र्त्रम ||
7.48.e: May we as Ṛbhu with your Ṛbhus conquer strength with our strength, as Vibhus with the Vibhus.  May Vāja aid us in the fight for booty, and helped by Indra may we quell the foeman.

7.48.d: ते चिद धि पूर्वीरभि सन्ति शासा विश्वानर्य उपरताति वन्वन | इन्द्रो विभ्वान रभुक्षा वाजो अर्यः शत्रोर्मिथत्या कर्णवन वि नर्म्णम ||
7.48.e: For they rule many tribes with high dominion, and conquer all their foes in close encounter.  May Indra, Vibhvan, Vāja, and Ṛbhukṣan destroy by turns the wicked foeman's valour.

7.48.d: नू देवासो वरिवः कर्तना नो भूत नो विश्वे.अवसे सजोषाः | समस्मे इषं वसवो ददीरन यूयं पात ... ||
7.48.e: Now, Deities, give us ample room and freedom: be all of you, one-minded, our protection.  So let the Vasus grant us strength and vigour. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.49.d: समुद्रज्येष्ठाः सलिलस्य मध्यात पुनाना यन्त्यनिविशमानाः | इन्द्रो या वज्री वर्षभो रराद ता आपो देवीरिहमामवन्तु ||
7.49.e: FORTH from the middle of the flood the Waters-their chief the Sea-flow cleansing, never sleeping.  Indra, the Bull, the Thunderer, dug their channels: here let those Waters, Goddesses, protect me.

7.49.d: या आपो दिव्या उत वा सरवन्ति खनित्रिमा उत वा याः सवयंजाः | समुद्रार्था याः शुचयः पावकास्ता आपो .. . ||
7.49.e: Waters which come from heaven, or those that wander dug from the earth, or flowing free by nature,  Bright, purifying, speeding to the Ocean, here let those Waters. Goddesses, protect me.

7.49.d: यासां राजा वरुणो याति मध्ये सत्यान्र्ते अवपश्यञ जनानाम | मधुश्चुतः शुचयो याः पावकास्ता आपो ... ||
7.49.e: Those amid whom goes Varuṇa the Sovran, he who discriminates men's truth and falsehood-  Distilling meath, the bright, the purifying, here let those Waters, Goddesses, protect me.

7.49.d: यासु राजा वरुणो यासु सोमो विश्वे देवा यासूर्जं मदन्ति | वैश्वानरो यास्वग्निः परविष्टस्ता आपो ... ||
7.49.e: They from whom Varuṇa the King, and Soma, and all the Deities drink strength and vigour,  They into whom Vaiśvānara Agni entered, here let those Waters, Goddesses, protect Me.

7.50.d: आ मां मित्रावरुणेह रक्षतं कुलाययद विश्वयन मा न आ गन | अजकावं दुर्द्र्शीकं तिरो दधे मा मां पद्येन रपसा विदत तसरुः ||
7.50.e: O MITRA-VARUNA, guard and protect me here: let not that come to me which nests within and swells.  I drive afar the scorpion hateful to the sight: let not the winding worm touch me and wound my foot.

7.50.d: यद विजामन परुषि वन्दनं भुवदष्ठीवन्तौ परि कुल्फौ च देहत | अग्निष टच्छोचन्नप बाधतामितो मा माम्पद्येन ... ||
7.50.e: Eruption that appears upon the twofold joints, and that which overspreads the ankles and the knees,  May the refulgent Agni banish far away let not the winding worm touch me and wound my foot.

7.50.d: यच्छल्मलौ भवति यन नदीषु यदोषधीभ्यः परि जायते विषम | विश्वे देवा निरितस्तत सुवन्तु मा मां पद्येन ... ||
7.50.e: The poison that is formed upon the Salmali, that which is found in streams, that which the plants produce,  All this may all the Gods banish and drive away: let not the winding worm touch me and wound my foot.

7.50.d: याः परवतो निवत उद्वत उदन्वतीरनुदकाश्च याः | ता अस्मभ्यं पयसा पिन्वमानाः शिवा देवीरशिपदा भवन्तु सर्वा नद्यो अशिमिदा भवन्तु ||
7.50.e: The steep declivities, the valleys, and the heights, the channels full of water, and the waterless-  May those who swell with water, gracious Goddesses, never afflict us with the Sipada disease, may all the rivers keep us free from Simida.

7.51.d: आदित्यानामवसा नूतनेन सक्षीमहि शर्मणा शन्तमेन | अनागास्त्वे अदितित्वे तुरास इमं यज्ञं दधतु शरोषमाणाः ||
7.51.e: THROUGH the Ādityas’ most auspicious shelter, through their most recent succour may we conquer.  May they, the Mighty, giving ear, establish this sacrifice, to make us free and sinless.

7.51.d: आदित्यासो अदितिर्मादयन्तां मित्रो अर्यमा वरुणो रजिष्ठाः | अस्माकं सन्तु भुवनस्य गोपाः पिबन्तु सोममवसे नो अद्य ||
7.51.e: Let Aditi rejoice and the Ādityas, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, most righteous.  May they, the Guardians of the world, protect us, and, to show favour, drink this day our Soma.

7.51.d: आदित्या विश्वे मरुतश्च विश्वे देवाश्च विश्व रभवश्च विश्वे | इन्द्रो अग्निरश्विना तुष्टुवाना यूयं पात ... ||
7.51.e: All Universal Deities, the Maruts, all the Ādityas, yea, and all the Ṛbhus,  Indra, and Agni, and the Aśvins, lauded. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.52.d: आदित्यासो अदितयः सयाम पूर्देवत्रा वसवो मर्त्यत्रा | सनेम मित्रावरुणा सनन्तो भवेम दयावाप्र्थिवी भवन्तः ||
7.52.e: MAY we be free from every bond, Ādityas! a castle among Gods and men, ye Vasus.  Winning, may we win Varuṇa and Mitra, and, being, may we be, O Earth and Heaven.

7.52.d: मित्रस्तन नो वरुणो मामहन्त शर्म तोकाय तनयाय गोपाः | मा वो भुजेमान्यजातमेनो मा तत कर्म वसवो यच्चयध्वे ||
7.52.e: May Varuṇa and Mitra grant this blessing, our Guardians, shelter to our seed and offspring.  Let us not suffer for another's trespass. nor do the thing that ye, O Vasus, punish.

7.52.d: तुरण्यवो.अङगिरसो नक्षन्त रत्नं देवस्य सवितुरियानाः | पिता च तन नो महान यजत्रो विश्वे देवाः समनसो जुषन्त ||
7.52.e: The ever-prompt Aṅgirases, imploring riches from Savitar the God, obtained them.  So may our Father who is great and holy, and all the Gods, accordant, grant this favour.

7.53.d: पर दयावा यज्ञैः पर्थिवी नमोभिः सबाध ईळे बर्हतीयजत्रे | ते चिद धि पूर्वे कवयो गर्णन्तः पुरो मही दधिरे देवपुत्रे ||
7.53.e: AS priest with solemn rites and adorations I worship Heaven and Earth, the High and Holy.  To them, great Parents of the Gods, have sages of ancient time, singing, assigned precedence.

7.53.d: पर पूर्वजे पितरा नव्यसीभिर्गीर्भिः कर्णुध्वं सदने रतस्य | आ नो दयावाप्र्थिवी दैव्येन जनेन यातं महि वां वरूथम ||
7.53.e: With newest hymns set in the seat of Order, those the Two Parents, born before all others,  Come, Heaven and Earth, with the Celestial People, hither to us, for strong is your protection.

7.53.d: उतो हि वां रत्नधेयानि सन्ति पुरूणि दयावाप्र्थिवी सुदासे | अस्मे धत्तं यदसदस्क्र्धोयु यूयं पात ... ||
7.53.e: Yea, Heaven and Earth, ye hold in your possession full many a treasure for the liberal giver.  Grant us that wealth which comes in free abundance. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.54.d: वास्तोष पते परति जानीह्यस्मान सवावेशो अनमीवो भवा नः | यत तवेमहे परति तन नो जुषस्व शं नो भव दविपदे शं चतुष्पदे ||
7.54.e: ACKNOWLEDGE us, O Guardian of the Homestead: bring no disease, and give us happy entrance.  Whate’er we ask of thee, be pleased to grant it, and prosper thou quadrupeds and bipeds.

7.54.d: वास्तोष पते परतरणो न एधि गयस्फानो गोभिरश्वेभिरिन्दो | अजरासस्ते सख्ये सयाम पितेव पुत्रान परति नो जुषस्व ||
7.54.e: Protector of the Home, be our promoter: increase our wealth in kine and steeds, O Indu.  May we be ever-youthful in thy friendship: be pleased in us as in his sons a father.

7.54.d: वास्तोष पते शग्मया संसदा ते सक्षीमहि रण्वया गातुमत्या | पाहि कषेम उत योगे वरं नो यूयं पात ... ||
7.54.e: Through thy dear fellowship that bringeth welfare, may we be victors, Guardian of the Dwelling!  Protect our happiness in rest and labour. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.55.d: अमीवहा वास्तोष पते विश्वा रूपाण्याविशन | सखा सुशेव एधि नः ||
7.55.e: VASTOSPATI, who killest all disease and wearest every form,  Be an auspicious Friend to us.

7.55.d: यदर्जुन सारमेय दतः पिशङग यछसे | वीव भराजन्त रष्टय उप सरक्वेषु बप्सतो नि षु सवप ||
7.55.e: When, O bright Son of Saramā, thou showest, tawny-hued! thy teeth,  They gleam like lances' points within thy mouth when thou wouldst bite; go thou to steep.

7.55.d: सतेनं राय सारमेय तस्करं वा पुनःसर | सतोतॄनिन्द्रस्य रायसि किमस्मान दुछुनायसे नि षु सवप ||
7.55.e: Saramā's Son, retrace thy way: bark at the robber and the thief.  At Indra's singers barkest thou? Why dust thou seek to terrify us? Go to sleep.

7.55.d: तवं सूकरस्य दर्द्र्हि तव दर्दर्तु सूकरः | सतोतॄनिन्द्रस्य ... ||
7.55.e: Be on thy guard against the boar, and let the boar beware of thee.  At Indra's singers barkest thou? Why dost thou seek to terrify us? Go to sleep.

7.55.d: सस्तु माता सस्तु पिता सस्तु शवा सस्तु विश्पतिः | ससन्तु सर्वे जञातयः सस्त्वयमभितो जनः ||
7.55.e: Sleep mother, let the father sleep, sleep dog and master of the house.  Let all the kinsmen sleep, sleep all the people who are round about.

7.55.d: य आस्ते यश्च चरति यश्च पश्यति नो जनः | तेषांसं हन्मो अक्षाणि यथेदं हर्म्यं तथा ||
7.55.e: The man who sits, the man who walks, and whosoever looks on us,  Of these we closely shut the eyes, even as we closely shut this house.

7.55.d: सहस्रश्र्ङगो वर्षभो यः समुद्रादुदाचरत | तेना सहस्येना वयं नि जनान सवापयामसि ||
7.55.e: The Bull who hath a thousand horns, who rises up from out the sea,—  By him the Strong and Mighty One we lull and make the people sleep.

7.55.d: परोष्ठशया वह्येशया नारीर्यास्तल्पशीवरीः | सत्रियो याः पुण्यगन्धास्ताः सर्वाः सवापयामसि ||
7.55.e: The women sleeping in the court, lying without, or stretched on beds,  The matrons with their odorous sweetsthese, one and all, we lull to sleep.

7.56.d: क ईं वयक्ता नरः सनीळा रुद्रस्य मर्या अध सवश्वाः ||
7.56.e: Wno are these radiant men in serried rank, Rudra's young heroes borne by noble steeds?

7.56.d: नकिर्ह्येषां जनूंषि वेद ते अङग विद्रे मिथो जनित्रम ||
7.56.e: Verily no one knoweth whence they sprang: they, and they only, know each other's birth.

7.56.d: अभि सवपूभिर्मिथो वपन्त वातस्वनसः शयेना अस्प्र्ध्रन ||
7.56.e: They strew each other with their blasts, these Hawks: they strove together, roaring like the wind.

7.56.d: एतानि धीरो निण्या चिकेत पर्श्निर्यदूधो मही जभार ||
7.56.e: A sage was he who knew these mysteries, what in her udder mighty Pṛśni bore.

7.56.d: सा विट सुवीरा मरुद्भिरस्तु सनात सहन्ती पुष्यन्ती नर्म्णम ||
7.56.e: Ever victorious, through the Maruts, be this band of Heroes, nursing manly strength,

7.56.d: यामं येष्ठाः शुभा शोभिष्ठाः शरिया सम्मिश्ला ओजोभिरुग्राः ||
7.56.e: Most bright in splendour, flectest on their way, close-knit to glory, strong with varied power.

7.56.d: उग्रं व ओज सथिरा शवांस्यधा मरुद्भिर्गणस्तुविष्मान ||
7.56.e: Yea, mighty is your power and firm your strength: so, potent, with the Maruts, be the band.

7.56.d: शुभ्रो वः शुष्मः करुध्मी मनांसि धुनिर्मुनिरिव शर्धस्य धर्ष्णोः ||
7.56.e: Bright is your spirit, wrathful are your minds: your bold troop's minstrel is like one inspired.

7.56.d: सनेम्यस्मद युयोत दिद्युं मा वो दुर्मतिरिह परणं नः ||
7.56.e: Ever avert your blazing shaft from us, and let not your displeasure reach us here

7.56.d: परिया वो नाम हुवे तुराणामा यत तर्पन मरुतो वावशानाः ||
7.56.e: Your dear names, conquering Maruts, we invoke, calling aloud till we are satisfied.

7.56.d: सवायुधास इष्मिणः सुनिष्का उत सवयं तन्वः शुम्भमानाः ||
7.56.e: Well-armed, impetuous in their haste, they deck themselves, their forms, with oblations: to you, the pure, ornaments made of gold.

7.56.d: शुची वो हव्या मरुतः शुचीनां शुचिं हिनोम्यध्वरं शुचिभ्यः | रतेन सत्यं रतसाप आयञ्छुचिजन्मानः शुचयः पावकाः ||
7.56.e: Pure, Maruts, pure yourselves, are your oblations: to you, the pure, pure sacrifice I offer.  By Law they came to truth, the Law's observers, bright by their birth, and pure, and sanctifying.

7.56.d: अंसेष्वा मरुतः खादयो वो वक्षस्सु रुक्मा उपशिश्रियाणाः | वि विद्युतो न वर्ष्टिभी रुचाना अनु सवधामायुधैर्यछमानाः ||
7.56.e: Your rings, O Maruts, rest upon your shoulders, and chains of gold are twined upon your bosoms.  Gleaming with drops of rain, like lightning-flashes, after your wont ye whirl about your weapons.

7.56.d: पर बुध्न्या व ईरते महांसि पर नामानि परयज्यवस्तिरध्वम | सहस्रियं दम्यं भागमेतं गर्हमेधीयं मरुतो जुषध्वम ||
7.56.e: Wide in the depth of air spread forth your glories, far, most adorable, ye bear your titles.  Maruts, accept this thousandfold allotment of household sacrifice and household treasure.

7.56.d: यदि सतुतस्य मरुतो अधीथेत्था विप्रस्य वाजिनो हवीमन | मक्षू रायः सुवीर्यस्य दात नू चिद यमन्य आदभदरावा ||
7.56.e: If, Maruts, ye regard the praise recited here at this mighty singer invocation,  Vouchsafe us quickly wealth with noble heroes, wealth which no man uho hateth us may injure.

7.56.d: अत्यासो न ये मरुतः सवञ्चो यक्षद्र्शो न शुभयन्त मर्याः | ते हर्म्येष्ठाः शिशवो न शुभ्रा वत्सासो न परक्रीळिनः पयोधाः ||
7.56.e: The Maruts, fleet as coursers, while they deck them like youths spectators of a festal meeting,  Linger, like beauteous colts, about the dwelling, like frisking calves, these who pour down the water.

7.56.d: दशस्यन्तो नो मरुतो मर्ळन्तु वरिवस्यन्तो रोदसी सुमेके | आरे गोहा नर्हा वधो वो अस्तु सुम्नेभिरस्मे वसवो नमध्वम ||
7.56.e: So may the Maruts help us and be gracious, bringing free room to lovely Earth and Heaven.  Far be your bolt that slayeth men and cattle. Ye Vasus, turn yourselves to us with blessings.

7.56.d: आ वो होता जोहवीति सत्तः सत्राचीं रातिं मरुतो गर्णानः | य ईवतो वर्षणो अस्ति गोपाः सो अद्वयावी हवते व उक्थैः ||
7.56.e: The priest, when seated, loudly calls you, Maruts, praising in song your universal bounty.  He, Bulls! who hath so much in his possession, free from duplicity, with hymns invokes you.

7.56.d: इमे तुरं मरुतो रामयन्तीमे सहः सहस आ नमन्ति | इमेशंसं वनुष्यतो नि पान्ति गुरु दवेषो अररुषे दधन्ति ||
7.56.e: These Maruts bring the swift man to a stand-still, and strength with mightier strength they break and humble  These guard the singer from the man who hates him and lay their sore displeasure on the wicked.

7.56.d: इमे रध्रं चिन मरुतो जुनन्ति भर्मिं चिद यथा वसवो जुषन्त | अप बाधध्वं वर्षणस्तमांसि धत्त विश्वं तनय ||
7.56.e: These Maruts rouse even the poor and needy: the Vasus love him as an active champion.  Drive to a distance, O ye Bulls, the darkness: give us full store of children and descendants.

7.56.d: ं तोकमस्मे ||
7.56.e: Never, O Maruts, may we lose your bounty, nor, car-borne Lords! be hitidmost when ye deal it.  Give us a share in that delightful treasure, the genuine wealth that, Bulls! is your possession.

7.56.d: मा वो दात्रान मरुतो निरराम मा पश्चाद दघ्म रथ्यो विभागे | आ न सपार्हे भजतना वसव्ये यदीं सुजातं वर्षणो वो अस्ति ||
7.56.e: What time the men in fury rush together for running streams, for pastures, and for houses.  Then, O ye Maruts, ye who spring from Rudra, be our protectors in the strife with foemen.

7.56.d: सं यद धनन्त मन्युभिर्जनासः शूरा यह्वीष्वोषधीषु विक्षु | अध समा नो मरुतो रुद्रियासस्त्रातारो भूत पर्तनास्वर्यः ||
7.56.e: Full many a deed ye did for our forefathers worthy of lauds which, even of old, they sang you.  lle strong man, with the Maruts, wins in battle, the charger, with the Maruts, gains the booty.

7.56.d: भूरि चक्र मरुतः पित्र्याण्युक्थानि या वः शस्यन्ते पुरा चित | मरुद्भिरुग्रः पर्तनासु साळ्हा मरुद्भिरित सनिता वाजमर्वा ||
7.56.e: Ours, O ye Maruts, be the vigorous Hero, the Lord Divine of men, the strong Sustainer,  With whom to fair lands we may cross the waters, and dwell in our own home with you beside us.

7.56.d: अस्मे वीरो मरुतः शुष्म्यस्तु जनानां यो असुरो विधर्ता | अपो येन सुक्षितये तरेमाध सवमोको अभि वः सयाम ||
7.56.e: May Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni, Waters, and Plants, and Trees accept our praises.  May we find shelter in the Marut's bosom. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.56.d: तन न इन्द्रो वरुणो मित्रो अग्निर... ||
7.56.e: Missing line from Griffith.

7.57.d: मध्वो वो नाम मारुतं यजत्राः पर यज्ञेषु शवसा मदन्ति | ये रेजयन्ति रोदसी चिदुर्वी पिन्वन्त्युत्सं यदयासुरुग्राः ||
7.57.e: YEA, through the power of your sweet juice, ye Holy! the Marut host is glad at sacrifices.  They cause even spacious heaven and earth to tremble, they make the spring flow when they come, the Mighty.

7.57.d: निचेतारो हि मरुतो गर्णन्तं परणेतारो यजमानस्य मन्म | अस्माकमद्य विदथेषु बर्हिरा वीतये सदत पिप्रियाणाः ||
7.57.e: The Maruts watch the man who sings their praises, promoters of the thought of him who worships.  Seat you on sacred grass in our assembly, this day, with friendly minds, to share the banquet.

7.57.d: नैतावदन्ये मरुतो यथेमे भराजन्ते रुक्मैरायुधैस्तनूभिः | आ रोदसी विश्वपिशः पिशानाः समानमञ्ज्यञ्जते शुभे कम ||
7.57.e: No others gleam so brightly as these Maruts with their own forms, their golden gauds, their weapons.  With all adornments, decking earth and heaven, they heighten, for bright show, their common splendour.

7.57.d: रधक सा वो मरुतो दिद्युदस्तु यद व आगः पुरुषता कराम | मा वस्तस्यामपि भूमा यजत्रा अस्मे वो अस्तु सुमतिश्चनिष्ठा ||
7.57.e: Far from us be your blazing dart, O Maruts, when we, through human frailty, sin against you.  Let us not he exposed to that, ye Holy! May your most loving favour still attend us.

7.57.d: कर्ते चिदत्र मरुतो रणन्तानवद्यासः शुचयः पावकाः | पर णो.अवत सुमतिभिर्यजत्राः पर वाजेभिस्तिरत पुष्यसे नः ||
7.57.e: May even what we have done delight the Maruts, the blameless Ones, the bright, the purifying.  Further us, O ye Holy, with your kindness: advance us mightily that we may prosper.

7.57.d: उत सतुतासो मरुतो वयन्तु विश्वेभिर्नामभिर्नरो हवींषि | ददात नो अम्र्तस्य परजायै जिग्र्त रायः सून्र्ता मघानि ||
7.57.e: And may the Maruts, praised by all their titles, Heroes, enjoy the taste of our oblations.  Give us of Amṛta for the sake of offspring: awake the excellent fair stores of riches.

7.57.d: आ सतुतासो मरुतो विश्व ऊती अछा सूरीन सर्वताता जिगात | ये नस्त्मना शतिनो वर्धयन्ति यूयं पात ... ||
7.57.e: Hither, ye Maruts, praised, with all your succours, with all felicity come to our princes,  Who, of themselves, a hundredfold increase us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.58.d: पर साकमुक्षे अर्चता गणाय यो दैव्यस्य धाम्नस्तुविष्मान | उत कषोदन्ति रोदसी महित्वा नक्षन्ते नाकं निरतेरवंशात ||
7.58.e: SING to the troop that pours down rain in common, the Mighty Company of celestial nature.  They make the world-halves tremble with their greatness: from depths of earth and sky they reach to heaven.

7.58.d: जनूश्चिद वो मरुतस्त्वेष्येण भीमासस्तुविमन्यवो.अयासः | पर ये महोभिरोजसोत सन्ति विश्वो वो यामन भयते सवर्द्र्क ||
7.58.e: Yea, your birth, Maruts, was with wild commotion, ye who move swiftly, fierce in wrath, terrific.  Ye all-surpassing in your might and vigour, each looker on the light fears at your coming.

7.58.d: बर्हद वयो मघवद्भ्यो दधात जुजोषन्निन मरुतः सुष्टुतिं नः | गतो नाध्वा वि तिराति जन्तुं पर ण सपार्हाभिरूतिभिस्तिरेत ||
7.58.e: Give ample vital power unto our princes let our fair praises gratify the Maruts.  As the way travelled helpeth people onward, so further us with your delightful succours.

7.58.d: युष्मोतो विप्रो मरुतः शतस्वी युष्मोतो अर्वा सहुरिः सहस्री | युष्मोतः सम्राळ उत हन्ति वर्त्रं पर तद वो अस्तु धूतयो देष्णम ||
7.58.e: Your favoured singer counts his wealth by hundreds: the strong steed whom ye favour wins a thousand.  The Sovran whom ye aid destroys the foeman. May this your gift, ye Shakers, be distinguished.

7.58.d: ताना रुद्रस्य मीळ्हुषो विवासे कुविन नंसन्ते मरुतः पुनर्नः | यत सस्वर्ता जिहीळिरे यदाविरव तदेन ईमहे तुराणाम ||
7.58.e: I call, as such, the Sons of bounteous Rudra: will not the Maruts turn again to us-ward?  What secret sin or open stirs their anger, that we implore the Swift Ones to forgive us.

7.58.d: परा सा वाचि सुष्टुतिर्मघोनामिदं सूक्तं मरुतो जुषन्त | आराच्चिद दवेषो वर्षणो युयोत यूयं पात ... ||
7.58.e: This eulogy of the Bounteous hath been spoken: accept, ye Maruts, this our hymn of praises.  Ye Bulls, keep those who hate us at a distance. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.59.d: यं तरायध्व इदम-इदं देवासो यं च नयथ | तस्मा अग्ने वरुण मित्रार्यमन मरुतः शर्म यछत ||
7.59.e: WHOMSO ye rescue here and there, whomso ye guide, O Deities,  To him give shelter, Agni, Mitra, Varuṇa, ye Maruts, and thou Aryaman.

7.59.d: युष्माकं देवा अवसाहनि परिय ईजानस्तरति दविषः | पर स कषयं तिरते वि महीरिषो यो वो वराय दाशति ||
7.59.e: Through your kind favour, Gods, on some auspicious day, the worshipper subdues his foes.  That man increases home and strengthening ample food who brings you offerings as ye list.

7.59.d: नहि वश्चरमं चन वसिष्ठः परिमंसते | अस्माकमद्य मरुतः सुते सचा विश्वे पिबत कामिनः ||
7.59.e: Vasiṣṭha will not overlook the lowliest one among you all.  O Maruts, of our Soma juice effused to-day drink all of you with eager haste.

7.59.d: नहि व ऊतिः पर्तनासु मर्धति यस्मा अराध्वं नरः | अभि व आवर्त सुमतिर्नवीयसी तूयं यात पिपीषवः ||
7.59.e: Your succour in the battle injures not the man to whom ye, Heroes, grant your gifts.  May your most recent favour turn to us again. Come quickly, ye who fain would drink.

7.59.d: ओ षु घर्ष्विराधसो यातनान्धांसि पीतये | इमा वो हव्या मरुतो ररे हि कं मो षवन्यत्र गन्तन ||
7.59.e: Come hitherward to drink the juice, O ye whose bounties give you joy.  These offerings are for you, these, Maruts, I present. Go not to any place but this.

7.59.d: आ च नो बर्हिः सदताविता च न सपार्हाणि दातवे वसु | अस्रेधन्तो मरुतः सोम्ये मधौ सवाहेह मादयाध्वै ||
7.59.e: Sit on our sacred grass, be graciously inclined to give the wealth for which we long,  To take delight, ye Maruts, Friends of all, with Svāhā, in sweet Soma juice.

7.59.d: सस्वश्चिद धि तन्वः शुम्भमाना आ हंसासो नीलप्र्ष्ठा अपप्तन | विश्वं शर्धो अभितो मा नि षेद नरो न रण्वाः सवने मदन्तः ||
7.59.e: Decking the beauty of their forms in secret the Swans with purple backs have flown down hither.  Around me all the Company hath settled, like joyous Heroes glad in our libation.

7.59.d: यो नो मरुतो अभि दुर्ह्र्णायुस्तिरश्चित्तानि वसवो जिघांसति | दरुहः पाशान परति स मुचीष्ट तपिष्ठेन हन्मनाहन्तना तम ||
7.59.e: Maruts, the man whose wrath is hard to master, he who would slay us ere we think, O Vasus,  May he be tangled in the toils of mischief; smite ye him down with your most flaming weapon.
O Maruts, ye consuming Gods, enjoy this offering brought for you,  To help us, ye who slay the foe.

7.59.d: गर्हमेधास आ गत मरुतो माप भूतन | युष्माकोती सुदानवः ||
7.59.e: Sharers of household sacrifice, come, Maruts, stay not far away,  That ye may help us, Bounteous Ones.

7.59.d: इहेह वः सवतवसः कवयः सूर्यत्वचः | यज्ञं मरुत आव्र्णे ||
7.59.e: Here, Self-strong Maruts, yea, even here. ye Sages with your sunbright skins  I dedicate your sacrifice.

7.59.d: तर्यम्बकं यजामहे सुगन्धिं पुष्टिवर्धनम | उर्वारुकमिवबन्धनान मर्त्योर्मुक्षीय माम्र्तात ||
7.59.e: Tryambaka we worship, sweet augmenter of prosperity.  As from its stem the cucumber, so may I be released from death, not reft of immortality.

7.60.d: यदद्य सूर्य बरवो.अनागा उद्यन मित्राय वरुणाय सत्यम | वयं देवत्रादिते सयाम तव परियासो अर्यमन गर्णन्तः ||
7.60.e: WHEN thou, O Sun, this day, arising sinless, shalt speak the truth to Varuṇa and Mitra,  O Aditi, may all the Deities love us, and thou, O Aryaman, while we are singing.

7.60.d: एष सय मित्रावरुणा नर्चक्षा उभे उदेति सूर्यो अभि जमन | विश्वस्य सथातुर्जगतश्च गोपा रजु मर्तेषु वर्जिना चपश्यन ||
7.60.e: Looking on man, O Varuṇa and Mitra, this Sun ascendeth up by both the pathways,  Guardian of all things fixt, of all that moveth, beholding good and evil acts of mortals.

7.60.d: अयुक्त सप्त हरितः सधस्थाद या ईं वहन्ति सूर्यं घर्ताचीः | धामानि मित्रावरुणा युवाकुः सं यो यूथेव जनिमानि चष्टे ||
7.60.e: He from their home hath yoked the Seven gold Coursers who, dropping oil and fatness, carry Sūrya.  Yours, Varuṇa and Mitra, he surveyeth the worlds and living creatures like a herdsman.

7.60.d: उद वां पर्क्षासो मधुमन्तो अस्थुरा सूर्यो अरुहच्छुक्रमर्णः | यस्मा आदित्या अध्वनो रदन्ति मित्रो अर्यमा वरुणःसजोषाः ||
7.60.e: Your coursers rich in store of sweets have mounted: to the bright ocean Sūrya hath ascended,  For whom the Ādityas make his pathway ready, Aryaman, Mitra, Varuṇa, accordant.

7.60.d: इमे चेतारो अन्र्तस्य भूरेर्मित्रो अर्यमा वरुणो हि सन्ति | इम रतस्य वाव्र्धुर्दुरोणे शग्मासः पुत्रा अदितेरदब्धाः ||
7.60.e: For these, even Aryaman, Varuṇa and Mitra, are the chastisers of all guile and falsehood.  These, Aditi's Sons, infallible and mighty, have waxen in the home of law Eternal.

7.60.d: इमे मित्रो वरुणो दूळभासो.अचेतसं चिच्चितयन्ति दक्षैः | अपि करतुं सुचेतसं वतन्तस्तिरश्चिदंहः सुपथानयन्ति ||
7.60.e: These, Mitra, Varuṇa whom none deceiveth, with great power quicken even the fool to wisdom,  And, wakening, moreover, thoughtful insight, lead it by easy paths o’er grief and trouble.

7.60.d: इमे दिवो अनिमिषा पर्थिव्याश्चिकित्वांसो अचेतसं नयन्ति | परव्राजे चिन नद्यो गाधमस्ति पारं नो अस्य विष्पितस्य पर्षन ||
7.60.e: They ever vigilant, with eyes that close not, caring for heaven and earth, lead on the thoughtless.  Even in the river's bed there is a shallow. across this broad expanse may they conduct us.

7.60.d: यद गोपावददितिः शर्म भद्रं मित्रो यछन्ति वरुणः सुदासे | तस्मिन्ना तोकं तनयं दधाना मा कर्म देवहेळनं तुरासः ||
7.60.e: When Aditi and Varuṇa and Mitra, like guardians, give Sudās their friendly shelter,  Granting him sons and lineal succession, let us not, bold ones! move the Gods to anger.

7.60.d: अव वेदिं होत्राभिर्यजेत रिपः काश्चिद वरुणध्रुतः सः | परि दवेषोभिरर्यमा वर्णक्तूरुं सुदासे वर्षणा उ लोकम ||
7.60.e: May he with ofierings purify the altar from any stains of Varuṇa's reviler.  Aryaman save us us all those who hate us: give room and freedom to Sudās, ye Mighty.

7.60.d: सस्वश्चिद धि सम्र्तिस्त्वेष्येषामपीच्येन सहसा सहन्ते | युष्मद भिया वर्षणो रेजमाना दक्षस्य चिन महिना मर्ळता नः ||
7.60.e: Hid from our eyes is their resplendent meeting: by their mysterious might they hold dominion.  Heroes! we cry trembling in fear before you, even in the greatness of your power have mercy.

7.60.d: यो बरह्मणे सुमतिमायजाते वाजस्य सातौ परमस्य रायः | सीक्षन्त मन्युं मघवानो अर्य उरु कषयाय चक्रिरे सुधातु ||
7.60.e: He who wins favour for his prayer by worship, that he may gain him strength and highest riches,  That good man's mind the Mighty Ones will follow: they have brought comfort to his spacious dwelling.

7.60.d: इयं देव पुरोहितिर्युवभ्यां यज्ञेषु मित्रावरुणावकारि | विश्वानि दुर्गा पिप्र्तं तिरो नो यूयं पात ... ||
7.60.e: This priestly task, Gods! Varuṇa and Mitra! hath been performed for you at sacrifices.  Convey us safely over every peril. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.61.d: उद वां चक्षुर्वरुण सुप्रतीकं देवयोरेति सूर्यस्ततन्वान | अभि यो विश्वा भुवनानि चष्टे स मन्युं मर्त्येष्वा चिकेत ||
7.61.e: O VARUNA and Mitra, Sūrya spreading the beauteous light of you Twain Gods ariseth.  He who beholdetb all existing creatures observetb well the zeal that is in mortals.

7.61.d: पर वां स मित्रावरुणाव रतावा विप्रो मन्मानि दीर्घश्रुदियर्ति | यस्य बरह्माणि सुक्रतू अवाथ आ यत करत्वा न शरदः पर्णैथे ||
7.61.e: The holy sage, renowned afar, directeth his hymns to you, O Varuṇa and Mitra,—  He whose devotions, sapient Gods, ye favour so that ye fill, as ’twere, with power his autumns.

7.61.d: परोरोर्मित्रावरुणा पर्थिव्याः पर दिव रष्वाद बर्हतः सुदानू | सपशो दधाथे ओषधीषु विक्ष्व रधग यतो अनिमिषंरक्षमाणा ||
7.61.e: From the wide earth, O Varuṇa and Mitra from the great lofty heaven, ye, Bounteous Givers, -  Have in the fields and houses set your warder-, who visit every spot and watch unceasing.

7.61.d: शंसा मित्रस्य वरुणस्य धाम शुष्मो रोदसी बद्बधे महित्वा | अयन मासा अयज्वनामवीराः पर यज्ञमन्मा वर्जनं तिराते ||
7.61.e: I praise the strength of Varuṇa and Mitra that strength, by mightiness, keeps both worlds asunder.  Heroless pass the months of the ungodly he who loves sacrifice makes his home enduring.

7.61.d: अमूरा विश्वा वर्षणाविमा वां न यासु चित्रं दद्र्शेन यक्षम | दरुहः सचन्ते अन्र्ता जनानां न वां निण्यान्यचिते अभूवन ||
7.61.e: Steers, all infallible are these your people in whom no wondrous thing is seen, no worship.  Guile follows close the men who are untruthful: no secrets may be hidden from your knowledge.

7.61.d: समु वां यज्ञं महयं नमोभिर्हुवे वां मित्रावरुणा सबाधः | पर वां मन्मान्य रचसे नवानि कर्तानि बरह्म जुजुषन्निमानि ||
7.61.e: I will exalt your sacrifice with homage: as priest, I, Mitra-Varuṇa, invoke you.  May these new hymns and prayers that I have fashioned delight you to the profit of the singer.
This priestly task, Gods! Varuṇa and Mitra! hath been performed for you at sacrifices.  Convey us safely over every peril. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.62.d: उत सूर्यो बर्हदर्चींष्यश्रेत पुरु विश्वा जनिम मानुषाणाम | समो दिवा दद्र्शे रोचमानः करत्वा कर्तः सुक्र्तःकर्त्र्भिर्भूत ||
7.62.e: SURYA hath sent aloft his beams of splendour o’er all the tribes of men in countless places.  Together with the heaven he shines apparent, formed by his Makers well with power and wisdom.

7.62.d: स सूर्य परति पुरो न उद गा एभिः सतोमेभिरेतशेभिरेवैः | पर नो मित्राय वरुणाय वोचो.अनागसो अर्यम्णे अग्नये च ||
7.62.e: So hast thou mounted up before us, Sūrya, through these our praises, with fleet dappled horses.  Declare us free from all offence to Mitra, and Varuṇa, and Aryaman, and Agni.

7.62.d: वि नः सहस्रं शुरुधो रदन्त्व रतावानो वरुणो मित्रो अग्निः | यछन्तु चन्द्रा उपमं नो अर्कमा नः कामं पूपुरन्तुस्तवानाः ||
7.62.e: May holy Agni, Varuṇa, and Mitra send down their riches upon us in thousands.  May they, the Bright Ones, make our praise-song perfect, and, when we laud them, grant us all our wishes.

7.62.d: दयावाभूमी अदिते तरासीथां नो ये वां जज्ञुः सुजनिमान रष्वे | मा हेळे भूम वरुणस्य वायोर्मा मित्रस्य परियतमस्य नर्णाम ||
7.62.e: O undivided Heaven and Earth, preserve us, us, Lofty Ones! your nobIy-born descendants.  Let us not anger Varuṇa, nor Vāyu, nor him, the dearest Friend of mortals, Mitra.

7.62.d: पर बाहवा सिस्र्तं जीवसे न आ नो गव्यूतिमुक्षतं घर्तेन | आ नो जने शरवयतं युवाना शरुतं मे मित्रावरुणा हवेमा ||
7.62.e: Stretch forth your arms and let our lives be lengthened: with fatness dew the pastures of our cattle.  Ye Youthful, make us famed among the people: hear, Mitra-Varuṇa, these mine invocations.

7.62.d: नू मित्रो वरुणो अर्यमा नस्त्मने तोकाय वरिवो दधन्तु | सुगा नो विश्वा सुपथानि सन्तु यूयं पात ... ||
7.62.e: Now Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman vouchsafe us freedom and room, for us and for our children.  May we find paths all fair and good to travel. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.63.d: उद वेति सुभगो विश्वचक्षाः साधारणः सूर्यो मानुषाणाम | चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्य देवश्चर्मेव यः समविव्यक तमांसि ||
7.63.e: COMMON to all mankind, auspicious Sūrya, he who beholdeth all, is mounting upward;  The God, the eye of Varuṇa and Mitra, who rolled up darkness like a piece of leather.

7.63.d: उद वेति परसवीता जनानां महान केतुरर्णवः सूर्यस्य | समानं चक्रं पर्याविव्र्त्सन यदेतशो वहति धूर्षु युक्तः ||
7.63.e: Sūrya's great ensign, restless as the billow, that urgeth men to action, is advancing:  Onward he still would roll the wheel well-rounded, which Etaśa, harnessed to the car-pole, moveth.

7.63.d: विभ्राजमान उषसामुपस्थाद रेभैरुदेत्यनुमद्यमानः | एष मे देवः सविता चछन्द यः समानं न परमिनातिधाम ||
7.63.e: Refulgent from the bosom of the Mornings, he in Whom singers take delight ascendeth.  This Savitar, God, is my chief joy and pleasure, who breaketh not the universal statute.

7.63.d: दिवो रुक्म उरुचक्षा उदेति दूरेर्थस्तरणिर्भ्राजमानः | नूनं जनाः सूर्येण परसूता अयन्नर्थानि कर्णवन्नपांसि ||
7.63.e: Golden, far-seeing, from the heaven he riseth: far is his goal, he hasteth on resplendent.  Men, verily, inspirited by Sūrya speed to their aims and do the work assigned them.

7.63.d: यत्रा चक्रुरम्र्ता गातुमस्मै शयेनो न दीयन्नन्वेति पाथः | परति वां सूर उदिते विधेम नमोभिर्मित्रावरुणोत हव्यैः ||
7.63.e: Where the irrunortals have prepared his pathway he flieth through the region like a falcon.  With homage and oblations will we serve you, O Mitra-Varuṇa, when the Sun hath risen.
Now Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman vouchsafe us freedom and room, for us and for our children.  May we find paths all fair and good to travel. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.64.d: दिवि कषयन्ता रजसः पर्थिव्यां पर वां घर्तस्य निर्णिजोददीरन | हव्यं नो मित्रो अर्यमा सुजातो राजा सुक्षत्रो वरुणो जुषन्त ||
7.64.e: YE Twain who rule, in heaven and earth, the region, clothed be your clouds in robes of oil and fatness.  May the imperial Varuṇa, and Mitra, and high-born Aryaman accept our presents.

7.64.d: आ राजाना मह रतस्य गोपा सिन्धुपती कषत्रिया यातमर्वाक | इळां नो मित्रावरुणोत वर्ष्टिमव दिव इन्वतं जीरदानू ||
7.64.e: Kings, guards of rrtighty everlasting Order, come hitherward, ye Princes, Lords of Rivers.  Send us from heaven, O Varuṇa and Mitra, rain and sweet food, ye who pour down your bounties.

7.64.d: मित्रस्तन नो वरुणो देवो अर्यः पर साधिष्ठेभिः पथिभिर्नयन्तु | बरवद यथा न आदरिः सुदास इषा मदेम सह देवगोपाः ||
7.64.e: May the dear God, and Varuṇa and Mitra conduct us by the most effective pathways,  That foes may say unto Sudās our chieftain, May, we, too, joy in food with Gods to guard us.

7.64.d: यो वां गर्तं मनसा तक्षदेतमूर्ध्वां धीतिं कर्णवद धारयच्च | उक्षेथां मित्रावरुणा घर्तेन ता राजानासुक्षितीस्तर्पयेथाम ||
7.64.e: Him who hath wrought for you this car in spirit, who makes the song rise upward and sustains it,  Bedew with fatness, Varuṇa nd Mitra ye Kings, make glad the pleasant dwelling-places.

7.64.d: एष सतोमो वरुण मित्र तुभ्यं सोमः शुक्रो न वायवे.अयामि | अविष्टं धियो जिग्र्तं पुरम्धीर्यूयं पात ||
7.64.e: To you this laud, O Varuṇa and Mitra is offered like bright Soma juice to Vāyu.  Favour our songs of praise, wake thought and spirit. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.65.d: परति वां सूर उदिते सूक्तैर्मित्रं हुवे वरुणं पूतदक्षम | ययोरसुर्यमक्षितं जयेष्ठं विश्वस्य यामन्नाचिता जिगत्नु ||
7.65.e: WITH hymns I call you, when the Sun hath risen, Mitra, and Varuṇa whose thoughts are holy,  Whose Power Divine, supreme and everlasting, comes with good heed at each man's supplication.

7.65.d: ता हि देवानामसुरा तावर्या ता नः कषितीः करतमूर्जयन्तीः | अश्याम मित्रावरुणा वयं वां दयावा च यत्र पीपयन्नहा च ||
7.65.e: For they are Asuras of Gods, the friendly make, both of you, our lands exceeding fruitful.  May we obtain you, Varuṇa and Mitra, wherever Heaven and Earth and days may bless us.

7.65.d: ता भूरिपाशावन्र्तस्य सेतू दुरत्येतू रिपवे मर्त्याय | रतस्य मित्रावरुणा पथा वामपो न नावा दुरिता तरेम ||
7.65.e: Bonds of the sinner, they bear many nooses: the wicked mortal hardly may escape them.  Varuṇa-Mitra, may your path of Order bear us o’er trouble as a boat o’er waters.

7.65.d: आ नो मित्रावरुणा हव्यजुष्टिं घर्तैर्गव्यूतिमुक्षतमिळाभिः | परति वामत्र वरमा जनाय पर्णीतमुद्नो दिव्यस्य चारोः ||
7.65.e: Come, taste our offering, Varuṇa and Mitra: bedew our pasture wil sweet food and fatness.  Pour down in plenty here upon the people the choicest of your fair celestial water.
To you this laud, O Varuṇa and Mitra, is offered, like bright Soma juice to Vāyu.  Favour our songs of praise, wake thought and spirit. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.66.d: पर मित्रयोर्वरुणयोः सतोमो न एतु शूष्यः | नमस्वान तुविजातयोः ||
7.66.e: LET our strong hymn of praise go forth, the laud of Mitra-Varuṇa,  With homage to that high-born Pair;

7.66.d: या धारयन्त देवाः सुदक्षा दक्षपितरा | असुर्याय परमहसा ||
7.66.e: The Two exceeding wise, the Sons of Dakṣa, whom the gods ordained  For lordship, excellently great.

7.66.d: ता न सतिपा तनूपा वरुण जरितॄणाम | मित्र साधयतं धियः ||
7.66.e: Such, Guardians of our homes and us, O Mitra-Varuṇa, fulfil  The thoughts of those who sing your praise.

7.66.d: यदद्य सूर उदिते.अनागा मित्रो अर्यमा | सुवाति सविताभगः ||
7.66.e: So when the Sun hath risen to-day, may sinless Mitra, Aryaman,  Bhaga, and Savitar sendus forth.

7.66.d: सुप्रावीरस्तु स कषयः पर नु यामन सुदानवः | ये नो अंहो.अतिपिप्रति ||
7.66.e: May this our home be guarded well forward, ye Bounteous, on the way,  Who bear us safely o’er distress.

7.66.d: उत सवराजो अदितिरदब्धस्य वरतस्य ये | महो राजान ईशते ||
7.66.e: And those Self-reigning, Aditi, whose statute is inviolate,  The Kings who rule a vast domain.

7.66.d: परति वां सूर उदिते मित्रं गर्णीषे वरुणम | अर्यमणंरिशादसम ||
7.66.e: Soon as the Sun hath risen, to you, to Mitra-Varuṇa, I sing,  And Aryarnan who slays the foe.

7.66.d: राया हिरण्यया मतिरियमव्र्काय शवसे | इयं विप्रामेधसातये ||
7.66.e: With wealth of gold may this my song bring unmolested power and might,  And, Brahmans, gain the sacrifice.

7.66.d: ते सयाम देव वरुण ते मित्र सूरिभिः सह | इषं सवश्च धीमहि ||
7.66.e: May we be thine, God Varuṇa, and with our princes, Mitra, thine.  Food and Heaven's light will we obtain.

7.66.d: बहवः सूरचक्षसो.अग्निजिह्वा रताव्र्धः | तरीणि ये येमुर्विदथानि धीतिभिर्विश्वानि परिभूतिभिः ||
7.66.e: Many are they who strengthen Law, Sun-eyed, with Agni for their tongue,  They who direct the three great gatherings with their thoughts, yea, all things with surpassing might.

7.66.d: वि ये दधुः शरदं मासमादहर्यज्ञमक्तुं चाद रचम | अनाप्यं वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा कषत्रं राजान आशत ||
7.66.e: They who have stablished year and month and then the day, night, sacrifice and holy verse,  Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryarnan, the Kings, have won dominion which none else may gain.

7.66.d: तद वो अद्य मनामहे सूक्तैः सूर उदिते | यदोहते वरुणो मित्रो अर्यमा यूयं रतस्य रथ्यः ||
7.66.e: So at the rising of the Sun we think of you with hymns to-day,  Even as Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman deserve: ye are the charioteers of Law.

7.66.d: रतावान रतजाता रताव्र्धो घोरासो अन्र्तद्विषः | तेषांवः सुम्ने सुछर्दिष्टमे नरः सयाम ये च सूरयः ||
7.66.e: True to Law, born in Law the strengtheners of Law, terrible, haters of the false,  In their felicity which gives the best defence may we men and our princes dwell.

7.66.d: उदु तयद दर्शतं वपुर्दिव एति परतिह्वरे | यदीमाशुर्वहति देव एतशो विश्वस्मै चक्षसे अरम ||
7.66.e: Uprises, on the slope of heaven, that marvel that attracts die sight  As swift celestial Etaśa bears it away, prepared for every eye to see.

7.66.d: शीर्ष्णः-शीर्ष्णो जगतस्तस्थुषस पतिं समया विश्वमा रजः | सप्त सवसारः सुविताय सूर्यं वहन्ति हरितो रथे ||
7.66.e: Lord of each single head, of fixt and moving things, equally through the whole expanse,  The Seven sister Bays bear Sūrya on his car, to bring us wealth and happiness.

7.66.d: तच्चक्षुर्देवहितं शुक्रमुच्चरत | पश्येम शरदः शतं जीवेम शरदः शतम ||
7.66.e: A hundred autumns may we see that bright Eye, God-ordained, arise  A hundred autumns may we live.

7.66.d: काव्येभिरदाभ्या यातं वरुण दयुमत | मित्रश्च सोमपीतये ||
7.66.e: Infallible through your wisdom, come hither, resplendent Varuṇa,  And Mitra, to the Soma draught.

7.66.d: दिवो धामभिर्वरुण मित्रश्चा यातमद्रुहा | पिबतं सोममातुजी ||
7.66.e: Come as the laws of Heaven ordain, Varuṇa, Mitra, void of guile:  Press near and drink the Soma juice.

7.66.d: आ यातं मित्रावरुणा जुषाणावाहुतिं नरा | पातं सोमं रताव्र्धा ||
7.66.e: Come, Mitra, Varuṇa, accept, Heroes, our sacrificial gift:  Drink Soma, ye who strengthen Law.

7.67.d: परति वां रथं नर्पती जरध्यै हविष्मता मनसा यज्ञियेन | यो वां दूतो न धिष्ण्यावजीगरछा सूनुर्न पितरा विवक्मि ||
7.67.e: I WITH a holy heart that brings oblation will sing forth praise to meet your car, ye Princes,  Which, Much-desired! hath wakened as your envoy. I call you hither as a son his parents.

7.67.d: अशोच्यग्निः समिधानो अस्मे उपो अद्र्श्रन तमसश्चिदन्ताः | अचेति केतुरुषसः पुरस्ताच्छ्रिये दिवो दुहितुर्जायमानः ||
7.67.e: Brightly hath Agni shone by us enkindled: the limits even of darkness were apparent.  Eastward is seen the Banner of the Morning, the Banner born to give Heaven's Daughter glory.

7.67.d: अभि वां नूनमश्विना सुहोता सतोमैः सिषक्ति नासत्या विवक्वान | पूर्वीभिर्यातं पथ्याभिरर्वाक सवर्विदा वसुमता रथेन ||
7.67.e: With hymns the deft priest is about you, Aśvins, the eloquent priest attends you now, Nāsatyas.  Come by the paths that ye are wont to travel, on car that finds the light, laden with treasure.

7.67.d: अवोर्वां नूनमश्विना युवाकुर्हुवे यद वां सुते माध्वीवसूयुः | आ वां वहन्तु सथविरासो अश्वाः पिबाथो अस्मेसुषुता मधूनि ||
7.67.e: When, suppliant for your help, Lovers of Sweetness! I seeking wealth call you to our libation,  Hitherward let your vigorous horses bear you: drink ye with us the well-pressed Soma juices.

7.67.d: पराचीमु देवाश्विना धियं मे.अम्र्ध्रां सातये कर्तं वसूयुम | विश्वा अविष्टं वाज आ पुरन्धीस्ता नः शक्तं शचीपती शचीभिः ||
7.67.e: Bring forward, Aśvins, Gods, to its fulfilment my never-wearied prayer that asks for riches.  Vouchsafe us all high spirit in the combat, and with your powers, O Lords of Power, assist us.

7.67.d: अविष्टं धीष्वश्विना न आसु परजावद रेतो अह्रयं नो अस्तु | आ वां तोके तनये तूतुजानाः सुरत्नासो देववीतिंगमेम ||
7.67.e: Favour us in these prayers of ours, O Aśvins. May we have genial vigour, ne’er to fail us.  So may we, strong in children and descendants, go, wealthy, to the banquet that awaits you.

7.67.d: एष सय वां पूर्वगत्वेव सख्ये निधिर्हितो माध्वी रातो अस्मे | अहेळता मनसा यातमर्वागश्नन्ता हव्यं मानुषीषु विक्षु ||
7.67.e: Lovers of Sweetness, we have brought this treasure to you as ’twere an envoy sent for friendship.  Come unto us with spirits free from anger, in homes of men enjoying our oblation.

7.67.d: एकस्मिन योगे भुरणा समाने परि वां सप्त सरवतो रथो गात | न वायन्ति सुभ्वो देवयुक्ता ये वां धूर्षु तरणयोवहन्ति ||
7.67.e: With one, the same, intention, ye swift movers, o’er the Seven Rivers hath your chariot travelled.  Yoked by the Gods, your strong steeds never weary while speeding forward at the pole they bear you.

7.67.d: असश्चता मघवद्भ्यो हि भूतं ये राया मघदेयं जुनन्ति | पर ये बन्धुं सून्र्ताभिस्तिरन्ते गव्या पर्ञ्चन्तो अश्व्या मघानि ||
7.67.e: Exhaustless be your bounty to our princes who with their wealth incite the gift of riches,  Who further friendship with their noble natures, combining wealth in kine with wealth in herses.

7.67.d: नू मे हवमा शर्णुतं युवाना यासिष्टं वर्तिरश्विनाविरावत | धत्तं रत्नानि जरतं च सूरीन यूयं पात .. . ||
7.67.e: Now hear, O Youthful Twain, mine invocation: come, Aśvins, to the home where food aboundeth.  Vouchsafe us wealth, do honour to our nobles. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.68.d: आ शुभ्रा यातमश्विना सवश्वा गिरो दस्रा जुजुषाणा युवाकोः | हव्यानि च परतिभ्र्ता वीतं नः ||
7.68.e: COME, radiant Aśvins, with your noble horses: accept your servant's hymns, ye Wonder-Workers:  Enjoy oblations which we bring to greet you.

7.68.d: पर वामन्धांसि मद्यान्यस्थुररं गन्तं हविषो वीतये मे | तिरो अर्यो हवनानि शरुतं नः ||
7.68.e: The gladdening juices stand prepared before you: come quickly and partake of mine oblation.  Pass by the calling of our foe and bear us.

7.68.d: पर वां रथो मनोजवा इयर्ति तिरो रजांस्यश्विना शतोतिः | अस्मभ्यं सूर्यावसू इयानः ||
7.68.e: Your chariot with a hundred aids, O Aśvins, beareth you swift as thought across the regions,  Speeding to us, O ye whose wealth is Sūrya.

7.68.d: अयं ह यद वां देवया उ अद्रिरूर्ध्वो विवक्ति सोमसुद युवभ्याम | आ वल्गू विप्रो वव्र्तीत हव्यैः ||
7.68.e: What time this stone of yours, the Gods’ adorer, upraised, sounds forth for you as Soma-presser,  Let the priest bring you, Fair Ones, through oblations.

7.68.d: चित्रं ह यद वां भोजनं नवस्ति नयत्रये महिष्वन्तं युयोतम | यो वामोमानं दधते परियः सन ||
7.68.e: The nourishment ye have is, truly, wondrous: ye gave thereof a quickening store to Atri,  Who being dear to you, receives your favour.

7.68.d: उत तयद वां जुरते अश्विना भूच्च्यवानाय परतीत्यं हविर्दे | अधि यद वर्प इतूति धत्थः ||
7.68.e: That gift, which all may gain, ye gave Cyavāna, when he grew old, who offered you oblations,  When ye bestowed on him enduring beauty.

7.68.d: उत तयं भुज्युमश्विना सखायो मध्ये जहुर्दुरेवासः समुद्रे | निरीं पर्षदरावा यो युवाकुः ||
7.68.e: What time his wicked friends abandoned Bhujyu, O Aśvins, in the middle of the ocean,  Your horse delivered him, your faithful servant.

7.68.d: वर्काय चिज्जसमानाय शक्तमुत शरुतं शयवे हूयमाना | यावघ्न्यामपिन्वतमपो न सतर्यं चिच्छक्त्यश्विनाशचीभिः ||
7.68.e: Ye lent your aid to Vrka when exhausted, and listened when invoked to Śayu's calling.  Ye made the cow pour forth her milk like water, and, Aśvins, strengthened with your strength the barren.

7.68.d: एष सय कारुर्जरते सूक्तैरग्रे बुधान उषसां सुमन्मा | इषा तं वर्धदघ्न्या पयोभिर्यूयं पात ... ||
7.68.e: With his fair hymns this singer, too, extols you, waking with glad thoughts at the break of morning.  May the cow nourish him with milk to feed llim. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.69.d: आ वां रथो रोदसी बद्बधानो हिरण्ययो वर्षभिर्यात्वश्वैः | घर्तवर्तनिः पविभी रुचान इषां वोळ्हा नर्पतिर्वाजिनीवान ||
7.69.e: MAY your gold chariot, drawn by vigorous horses, come to us, blocking up the earth  and heaven,  Bright with its fellies while its way drops fatness, food-laden, rich in coursers, man's protector.

7.69.d: स पप्रथानो अभि पञ्च भूमा तरिवन्धुरो मनसा यातु युक्तः | विशो येन गछथो देवयन्तीः कुत्रा चिद याममश्विना दधाना ||
7.69.e: Let it approach, yoked by thewill, three-seated, extending far and wide o’er fivefold beings,  Whereon ye visit God-adoring races, bending your course whither ye will, O Aśvins.

7.69.d: सवश्वा यशसा यातमर्वाग दस्रा निधिं मधुमन्तं पिबाथः | वि वां रथो वध्वा यादमानो.अन्तान दिवो बाधते वर्तनिभ्याम ||
7.69.e: Renowned, with noble horses, come ye hither: drink, Wondrous Pair, the cup that holds sweet juices.  Your car whereon your Spouse is wont to travel marks with its track the farthest ends of heaven.

7.69.d: युवोः शरियं परि योषाव्र्णीत सूरो दुहिता परितक्म्यायाम | यद देवयन्तमवथः शचीभिः परि घरंसमोमना वां वयो गात ||
7.69.e: When night was turning to the grey of morning the Maiden, Sūrya's Daughter, chose your splendour.  When with your power and might ye aid the pious he comes through heat to life by your assistance.

7.69.d: यो ह सय वां रथिरा वस्त उस्रा रथो युजानः परियातिवर्तिः | तेन नः शं योरुषसो वयुष्टौ नयश्विना वहतं यज्ञे अस्मिन ||
7.69.e: O Chariot-borne, this car of yours invested with rays of light comes harnessed to our dwelling.  Herewith, O Aśvins, while the dawn is breaking, to this our sacrifice bring peace and blessing.

7.69.d: नरा गौरेव विद्युतं तर्षाणास्माकमद्य सवनोप यातम | पुरुत्रा हि वां मतिभिर्हवन्ते मा वामन्ये नि यमन देवयन्तः ||
7.69.e: Like the wild cattle thirsty for the lightning, Heroes, come nigh this day to our libations.  Men call on you with hymns in many places, but let not other worshippers detain you.

7.69.d: युवं भुज्युमवविद्धं समुद्र उदूहथुरर्णसो अस्रिधानैः | पतत्रिभिरश्रमैरव्यथिभिर्दंसनाभिरश्विना पारयन्ता ||
7.69.e: Bhujyu, abandoned in the midst of ocean, ye raised from out the water with your horses,  Uninjured, winged, flagging not, undaunted, with deeds of wonder saving him, O Aśvins.
Now hear, O Youthful Twain, mine invocation: come, Aśvins, to the home where food aboundeth.  Vouchsafe us wealth, do honour to our nobles. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.70.d: आ विश्ववाराश्विना गतं नः पर तत सथानमवाचि वां पर्थिव्याम | अश्वो न वाजी शुनप्र्ष्ठो अस्थादा यत सेदथुर्ध्रुवसे न योनिम ||
7.70.e: RICH in all blessings, Aśvins come ye hither: this place on earth is called your own possession,  Like a strong horse with a fair back it standeth, whereon, as in a lap, ye seat you firmly.

7.70.d: सिषक्ति सा वां सुमतिश्चनिष्ठातापि घर्मो मनुषो दुरोणे | यो वां समुद्रान सरितः पिपर्त्येतग्वा चिन न सुयुजा युजानः ||
7.70.e: This most delightful eulogy awaits you in the man's house drink-offering hath been heated,  Which bringeth you over the seas and rivers, yoking as’twere two well-matched shining horses.

7.70.d: यानि सथानान्यश्विना दधाथे दिवो यह्वीष्वोषधीषु विक्षु | नि पर्वतस्य मूर्धनि सदन्तेषं जनाय दाशुषेवहन्ता ||
7.70.e: Whatever dwellings ye possess, O Aśvins, in fields of men or in the streams of heaven,  Resting upon the summit of the mountain, or bringing food to him who gives oblation,

7.70.d: चनिष्टं देवा ओषधीष्वप्सु यद योग्या अश्नवैथे रषीणाम | पुरूणि रत्ना दधतौ नयस्मे अनु पूर्वाणि चख्यथुर्युगानि ||
7.70.e: Delight yourselves, ye Gods, in plants and waters when Ṛṣis give them and ye find they suit You.  Enriching us with treasures in abundance ye have looked back to former generations.

7.70.d: शुश्रुवांसा चिदश्विना पुरूण्यभि बरह्माणि चक्षाथे रषीणाम | परति पर यातं वरमा जनायास्मे वामस्तु सुमतिश्चनिष्ठा ||
7.70.e: Aśvins, though ye have heard them oft aforetime, regard the many prayers which Ṛṣis offer.  Come to the man even as his heart desireth: may we enjoy your most delightful favour.

7.70.d: यो वां यज्ञो नासत्या हविष्मान कर्तब्रह्मा समर्यो भवाति | उप पर यातं वरमा वसिष्ठमिमा बरह्माण्य रच्यन्ते युवभ्याम ||
7.70.e: Come to the sacrifice offered you, Nāsatyas, with men, oblations, and prayer duly uttered.  Come to Vasiṣṭha as his heart desireth, for unto you these holy hymns are chanted.

7.70.d: इयं मनीषा इयमश्विना गीरिमां सुव्र्क्तिं वर्षणा जुषेथाम | इमा बरह्माणि युवयून्यग्मन यूयं पात ... ||
7.70.e: This is the thought, this is the song, O Aśvins: accept this hymn of ours, ye Steers, with favour.  May these our prayers addressed to you come nigh you. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.71.d: अप सवसुरुषसो नग जिहीते रिणक्ति कर्ष्णीररुषाय पन्थाम | अश्वामघा गोमघा वां हुवेम दिवा नक्तं शरुमस्मद युयोतम ||
7.71.e: THE Night retireth from the Dawn her Sister; the Dark one yieldeth to the Red her pathway.  Let us invoke you rich in steeds and cattle - by day and night keep far from us the arrow.

7.71.d: उपायातं दाशुषे मर्त्याय रथेन वाममश्विना वहन्ता | युयुतमस्मदनिराममीवां दिवा नक्तं माध्वी तरासिथां नः ||
7.71.e: Bearing rich treasure in your car, O Aśvins, come to the mortal who presents oblation.  Keep at a distance penury and sickness; Lovers of Sweetness, day and night preserve us.

7.71.d: आ वां रथमवमस्यां वयुष्टौ सुम्नायवो वर्षणो वर्तयन्तु | सयूमगभस्तिं रतयुग्भिरश्वैराश्विना वसुमन्तं वहेथाम ||
7.71.e: May your strong horses, seeking bliss, bring hither your chariot at the earliest flush of morning.  With coursers yoked by Law drive hither, Aśvins, your car whose reins are light, laden with treasure.

7.71.d: यो वां रथो नर्पती अस्ति वोळ्हा तरिवन्धुरो वसुमानुस्रयामा | आ न एना नासत्योप यातमभि यद वां विश्वप्स्न्यो जिगाति ||
7.71.e: The chariot, Princes, that conveys you, moving at daylight, triple-seated, fraught with riches,  Even with this come unto us, Nāsatyas, that laden with all food it may approach us.

7.71.d: युवं चयवानं जरसो.अमुमुक्तं नि पेदव ऊहथुराशुमश्वम | निरंहसस्तमस सपर्तमत्रिं नि जाहुषं शिथिरे धातमन्तः ||
7.71.e: Ye freed Cyavāna from old age and weakness: ye brought the courser fleet of food to Pedu.  Ye rescued Atri from distress and darkness, and loosed for Jāhuṣa the bonds that bound him.

This is the thought, this is the song, O Aśvins: accept this hymn of ours, ye Steers, With favour.  May these our prayers addressed to you come nigh you. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.72.d: आ गोमता नासत्या रथेनाश्वावता पुरुश्चन्द्रेण यातम | अभि वां विश्वा नियुतः सचन्ते सपार्हया शरिया तन्वा शुभाना ||
7.72.e: COME, O Nāsatyas, on your car resplendent, rich in abundant wealth of kine and horses.  As harnessed steeds, all our laudations follow you whose forms shine with most delightful beauty.

7.72.d: आ नो देवेभिरुप यातमर्वाक सजोषसा नासत्या रथेन | युवोर्हि नः सख्या पित्र्याणि समानो बन्धुरुत तस्य वित्तम ||
7.72.e: Come with the Gods associate, come ye hither to us, Nāsatyas, with your car accordant.  'Twixt you and us there is ancestral friendship and common kin: remember and regard it.

7.72.d: उदु सतोमासो अश्विनोरबुध्रञ जामि बरह्माण्युषसश्च देवीः | आविवासन रोदसी धिष्ण्येमे अछा विप्रो नासत्या विवक्ति ||
7.72.e: Awakened are the songs that praise the Aśvins, the kindred prayers and the Celestial Mornings.  Inviting those we long for, Earth and Heaven, the singer calleth these Nāsatyas hither.

7.72.d: वि चेदुछन्त्यश्विना उषासः पर वां बरह्माणि कारवो भरन्ते | ऊर्ध्वं भानुं सविता देवो अश्रेद बर्हदग्नयः समिधा जरन्ते ||
7.72.e: What time the Dawns break forth in light, O Aśvins, to you the poets offer their devotions.  God Savitar hath sent aloft his splendour, and fires sing praises with the kindled fuel.

7.72.d: आ पश्चातान नासत्या पुरस्तादाश्विना यातमधरादुदक्तात | आ विश्वतः पाञ्चजन्येन राया यूयं पात ... ||
7.72.e: Come from the west, come from the cast, Nāsatyas, come, Aśvins, from below and from above us.  Bring wealth from all sides for the Fivefold People. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.73.d: अतारिष्म तमसस पारमस्य परति सतोमं देवयन्तो दधानाः | पुरुदंसा पुरुतमा पुराजामर्त्या हवते अश्विना गीः ||
7.73.e: WE have o’erpassed the limit of this darkness while, worshipping the Gods, we sang their praises.  The song invoketh both Immortal Aśvins far-reaching, born of old, great WonderWorkers.

7.73.d: नयु परियो मनुषः सादि होता नासत्या यो यजते वन्दते च | अश्नीतं मध्वो अश्विना उपाक आ वां वोचे विदथेषु परयस्वान ||
7.73.e: And, O Nāsatyas, man's dear Priest is seated, who brings to sacrifice and offers worship,  Be near and taste the pleasant juice, O Aśvins: with food, I call you to the sacrifices.

7.73.d: अहेम यज्ञं पथामुराणा इमां सुव्र्क्तिं वर्षणा जुषेथाम | शरुष्टीवेव परेषितो वामबोधि परति सतोमैर्जरमाणो वसिष्ठः ||
7.73.e: We choosing you, have let our worship follow its course: ye Steers, accept this hymn with favour.  Obeying you as your appointed servant, Vasiṣṭha singing hath with lauds aroused you.

7.73.d: उप तया वह्नी गमतो विशं नो रक्षोहणा सम्भ्र्ता वीळुपाणी | समन्धांस्यग्मत मत्सराणि मा नो मर्धिष्टमा गतं शिवेन ||
7.73.e: And these Two Priests come nigh unto our people, united, demon-slayers, mighty-handed.  The juices that exhilarate are mingled. Injure us not, but come with happy fortune.
Come from the west, come from the cast, Nāsatyas, come, Aśvins, from below and from above us.  Bring wealth from all sides for the Fivefold People. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.74.d: इमा उ वां दिविष्टय उस्रा हवन्ते अश्विना | अयं वामह्वे.अवसे शचीवसू विशं-विशं हि गछथः ||
7.74.e: THESE morning sacrifices call you, Aśvins, at the break of day.  For help have I invoked you rich in power and might: for, house by house ye visit all.

7.74.d: युवं चित्रं ददथुर्भोजनं नरा चोदेथां सून्र्तावते | अर्वाग रथं समनसा नि यछतं पिबतं सोम्यं मधु ||
7.74.e: O Heroes, ye bestow wonderful nourishment. send it to him whose songs are sweet  Accordant, both of you, drive your car down to us, and drink the savoury Soma juice.

7.74.d: आ यातमुप भूषतं मध्वः पिबतमश्विना | दुग्धं पयोव्र्षणा जेन्यावसू मा नो मर्धिष्टमा गतम ||
7.74.e: Approach ye and be near to us. drink, O ye Aśvins, of the meath.  Draw forth the milk, ye Mighty, rich in genuine wealth: injure us not, and come to us.

7.74.d: अश्वासो ये वामुप दाशुषो गर्हं युवां दीयन्ति बिभ्रतः | मक्षूयुभिर्नरा हयेभिरश्विना देवा यातमस्मयू ||
7.74.e: The horses that convey you in their rapid flight down to the worshipper's abode,  With these your speedy coursers, Heroes, Aśvins, come, ye Gods, come well-inclined to us.

7.74.d: अधा ह यन्तो अश्विना पर्क्षः सचन्त सूरयः | ता यंसतो मघवद्भ्यो धरुवं यशश्छर्दिरस्मभ्यं नासत्या ||
7.74.e: Yea, verily, our princes seek the Aśvins in pursuit of food.  These shall give lasting glory to our liberal lords, and, both Nāsatyas, shelter us.

7.74.d: पर ये ययुरव्र्कासो रथा इव नर्पातारो जनानाम | उत सवेन शवसा शूशुवुर्नर उत कषियन्ति सुक्षितिम ||
7.74.e: Those who have led the way, like cars, offending none, those who are guardians of the men-  Also through their own might the heroes have grown strong, and dwell in safe and happy homes.

7.75.d: वयुषा आवो दिविजा रतेनाविष्क्र्ण्वाना महिमानमागात | अप दरुहस्तम आवरजुष्टमङगिरस्तमा पथ्या अजीगः ||
7.75.e: BORN in the heavens the Dawn hath flushed, and showing her majesty is come as Law ordaineth.  She hath uncovered fiends and hateful darkness; best of Aṅgirases, hath waked the pathways.

7.75.d: महे नो अद्य सुविताय बोध्युषो महे सौभगाय पर यन्धि | चित्रं रयिं यशसं धेह्यस्मे देवि मर्तेषु मानुषि शरवस्युम ||
7.75.e: Rouse us this day to high and happy fortune: to great felicity, O Dawn, promote us.  Vouchsafe us manifold and splendid riches, famed among mortals, man-befriending Goddess!

7.75.d: एते तये भानवो दर्शतायाश्चित्रा उषसो अम्र्तास आगुः | जनयन्तो दैव्यानि वरतान्याप्र्णन्तो अन्तरिक्षा वयस्थुः ||
7.75.e: See, lovely Morning's everlasting splendours, bright with their varied colours, have approached us.  Filling the region of mid-air, producing the rites of holy worship, they have mounted.

7.75.d: एषा सया युजाना पराकात पञ्च कषितीः परि सद्यो जिगाति | अभिपश्यन्ती वयुना जनानां दिवो दुहिता भुवनस्यपत्नी ||
7.75.e: She yokes her chariot far away, and swiftly visits the lands where the Five Tribes are settled,  Looking upon the works and ways of mortals, Daughter of Heaven, the world's Imperial Lady.

7.75.d: वाजिनीवती सूर्यस्य योषा चित्रामघा राय ईशे वसूनाम | रषिष्टुता जरयन्ती मघोन्युषा उछति वह्निभिर्ग्र्णाना ||
7.75.e: She who is rich in spoil, the Spouse of Sūrya, wondrously opulent, rules all wealth and treasures.  Consumer of our youth, the seers extol her: lauded by priests rich Dawn shines out refulgent.

7.75.d: परति दयुतानामरुषासो अश्वाश्चित्रा अद्र्श्रन्नुषसं वहन्तः | याति शुभ्रा विश्वपिशा रथेन दधाति रत्नंविधते जनाय ||
7.75.e: Apparent are the steeds of varied colour, the red steeds carrying resplendent Morning.  On her all-lovely car she comes, the Fair One, and brings rich treasure for her faithful servant.

7.75.d: सत्या सत्येभिर्महती महद्भिर्देवी देवेभिर्यजता यजत्रैः | रुजद दर्ळ्हानि दददुस्रियाणां परति गाव उषसं वावशन्त ||
7.75.e: True with the True and Mighty with the Mighty, with Gods a Goddess, Holy with the Holy,  She brake strong fences down and gave the cattle: the kine were lowing as they greeted Morning.

7.75.d: नू नो गोमद वीरवद धेहि रत्नमुषो अश्वावद पुरुभोजो अस्मे | मा नो बर्हिः पुरुषता निदे कर्यूयं पात ... ||
7.75.e: O Dawn, now give us wealth in kine and heroes, and horses, fraught with manifold enjoyment.  Protect our sacred grass from man's reproaches. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.76.d: उदु जयोतिरम्र्तं विश्वजन्यं विश्वानरः सविता देवो अश्रेत | करत्वा देवानामजनिष्ट चक्षुराविरकर्भुवनंविश्वमुषाः ||
7.76.e: SAVITAR God of all men hath sent upward his light, designed for all mankind, immortal.  Through the Gods’ power that Eye was first created. Dawn hath made all the universe apparent.

7.76.d: पर मे पन्था देवयाना अद्र्श्रन्नमर्धन्तो वसुभिरिष्क्र्तासः | अभूदु केतुरुषसः पुरस्तात परतीच्यागादधि हर्म्येभ्यः ||
7.76.e: I see the paths which Gods are wont to travel, innocuous paths made ready by the Vasus.  Eastward the flag of Dawn hath been uplifted; she hath come hither o’er the tops of houses.

7.76.d: तानीदहानि बहुलान्यासन या पराचीनमुदिता सूर्यस्य | यतः परि जार इवाचरन्त्युषो दद्र्क्षे न पुनर्यतीव ||
7.76.e: Great is, in truth, the number of the Mornings which were aforetime at the Sun's uprising.  Since thou, O Dawn, hast been beheld repairing as to thy love, as one no more to leave him.

7.76.d: त इद देवानां सधमाद आसन्न्र्तावानः कवयः पूर्व्यासः | गूळ्हं जयोतिः पितरो अन्वविन्दन सत्यमन्त्रा अजनयन्नुषासम ||
7.76.e: They were the Gods’ companions at the banquet, the ancient sages true to Law Eternal.  The Fathers found the light that lay in darkness, and with effectual words begat the Morning.

7.76.d: समान ऊर्वे अधि संगतासः सं जानते न यतन्ते मिथस्ते | ते देवानां न मिनन्ति वरतान्यमर्धन्तो वसुभिर्यादमानाः ||
7.76.e: Meeting together in the same enclosure, they strive not, ofone mind, one with another.  They never break the Gods’ eternal statutes, and injure none, in rivalry with Vasus.

7.76.d: परति तवा सतोमैरीळते वसिष्ठा उषर्बुधः सुभगे तुष्टुवांसः | गवां नेत्री वाजपत्नी न उछोषः सुजाते परथमा जरस्व ||
7.76.e: Extolling thee, Blest Goddess, the Vasisthas, awake at early mom, with lauds implore thee.  Leader of kine and Queen of all that strengthens, shine, come as first to us, O high-born Morning.

7.76.d: एषा नेत्री राधसः सून्र्तानामुषा उछन्ती रिभ्यते वसिष्ठैः | दीर्घश्रुतं रयिमस्मे दधाना यूयं पात . .. ||
7.76.e: She bringeth bounty and sweet charm of voices. The flushing Dawn is sung by the Vasisthas,  Giving us riches famed to distant places. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.77.d: उपो रुरुचे युवतिर्न योषा विश्वं जीवं परसुवन्ती चरायै | अभूदग्निः समिधे मानुषाणामकर्ज्योतिर्बाधमाना तमांसि ||
7.77.e: SHE hath shone brightly like a youthful woman, stirring to motion every living creature.  Agni hath come to feed on mortal? fuel. She hath made light and chased away the darkness.

7.77.d: विश्वं परतीची सप्रथा उदस्थाद रुशद वासो बिभ्रतीशुक्रमश्वैत | हिरण्यवर्णा सुद्र्शीकसन्द्र्ग गवां मातानेत्र्यह्नामरोचि ||
7.77.e: Turned to this All, far-spreading, she hath risen and shone in brightness with white robes about her.  She hath beamed forth lovely with golden colours, Mother of kine, Guide of the days she bringeth.

7.77.d: देवानां चक्षुः सुभगा वहन्ती शवेतं नयन्ती सुद्र्शीकमश्वम | उषा अदर्शि रश्मिभिर्व्यक्ता चित्रामघा विश्वमनु परभूता ||
7.77.e: Bearing the Gods’ own Eye, auspicious Lady, leading her Courser white and fair to look on,  Distinguished by her bean-is Dawn shines apparent, come forth to all the world with wondrous treasure.

7.77.d: अन्तिवामा दूरे अमित्रमुछोर्वीं गव्यूतिमभयं कर्धी नः | यावय दवेष आ भरा वसूनि चोदय राधो गर्णते मघोनि ||
7.77.e: Draw nigh with wealth and dawn away the foeman: prepare for us wide pasture free from danger.  Drive away those who hate us, bring us riches: pour bounty, opulent Lady, on the singer.

7.77.d: अस्मे शरेष्ठेभिर्भानुभिर्वि भाह्युषो देवि परतिरन्ती न आयुः | इषं च नो दधती विश्ववारे गोमदश्वावद रथवच्च राधः ||
7.77.e: Send thy most excellent beams to shine and light us, giving us lengthened days, O Dawn, O Goddess,  Granting us food, thou who hast all things precious, and bounty rich in chariots, kine, and horses.

7.77.d: यां तवा दिवो दुहितर्वर्धयन्त्युषः सुजाते मतिभिर्वसिष्ठाः | सास्मासु धा रयिं रष्वं बर्हन्तं यूयं पात .. . ||
7.77.e: O Uṣas, nobly-born, Daughter of Heaven, whom the Vasisthas with their hymns make mighty,  Bestow thou on us vast and glorious riches. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.78.d: परति केतवः परथमा अद्र्श्रन्नूर्ध्वा अस्या अञ्जयो वि शरयन्ते | उषो अर्वाचा बर्हता रथेन जयोतिष्मता वाममस्मभ्यं वक्षि ||
7.78.e: WE have beheld her earliest lights approaching: her many glories part, on high, asunder.  On car sublime, refulgent, wending hither, O Uṣas, bring the Wealth that makes us happy.

7.78.d: परति षीमग्निर्जरते समिद्धः परति विप्रासो मतिभिर्ग्र्णन्तः | उषा याति जयोतिषा बाधमाना विश्वा तमांसि दुरिताप देवी ||
7.78.e: The fire well-kindIed sings aloud to greet her, and with their hymns the priests are chaming welcome.  Uṣas approaches in her splendour, driving all evil darkness far away, the Goddess.

7.78.d: एता उ तयाः परत्यद्र्श्रन पुरस्ताज्ज्योतिर्यछन्तीरुषसोविभातीः | अजीजनन सूर्यं यज्ञमग्निमपाचीनं तमो अगादजुष्टम ||
7.78.e: Apparent eastward are those lights of Morning, sending out lustre, as they rise, around them.  She hath brought forth Sun, sacrifice, and Agni, and far away hath fled detested darkness.

7.78.d: अचेति दिवो दुहिता मघोनी विश्वे पश्यन्त्युषसं विभातीम | आस्थाद रथं सवधया युज्यमानमा यमश्वासः सुयुजो वहन्ति ||
7.78.e: Rich Daughter of the Sky, we all behold her, yea, all men look on Dawn as she is breaking.  fler car that moves self-harnessed hath she mounted, the car drawn onward by her well-yoked horses.

7.78.d: परति तवाद्य सुमनसो बुधन्तास्माकासो मघवानो वयं च | तिल्विलायध्वमुषसो विभातीर्यूयं पात ... ||
7.78.e: Inspired with loving thoughts this day to greet thee, we and our wealthy nobles have awakened.  Show yourselves fruitful, Dawns, as ye are rising. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.79.d: वयुषा आवः पथ्या जनानां पञ्च कषितीर्मानुषीर्बोधयन्ती | सुसन्द्र्ग्भिरुक्षभिर्भानुमश्रेद वि सूर्यो रोदसी चक्षसावः ||
7.79.e: ROUSING the lands where men's Five Tribes are settled, Dawn hath disclosed the pathways of the people.  She hath sent out her sheen with beauteous oxen. The Sun with light hath opened earth and heaven.

7.79.d: वयञ्जते दिवो अन्तेष्वक्तून विशो न युक्ता उषसो यतन्ते | सं ते गावस्तम आ वर्तयन्ति जयोतिर्यछन्ति सवितेव बाहू ||
7.79.e: They paint their bright rays on the sky's far limits. the Dawns come on like tribes arrayed for battle.  Thy cattle, closely shutting up the darkness, as Savitar spreads his arms, give forth their lustre.

7.79.d: अभूदुषा इन्द्रतमा मघोन्यजीजनत सुविताय शरवांसि | वि दिवो देवी दुहिता दधात्यङगिरस्तमा सुक्र्ते वसूनि ||
7.79.e: Wealthy, most like to Indra, Dawn hath risen, and brought forth lauds that shall promote our welfare.  Daughter of Heaven, a Goddess, she distributes, best of Aṅgirases, treasures to the pious.

7.79.d: तावदुषो राधो अस्मभ्यं रास्व यावत सतोत्र्भ्यो अरदो गर्णाना | यां तवा जज्ञुर्व्र्षभस्या रवेण वि दर्ळ्हस्य दुरो अद्रेरौर्णोः ||
7.79.e: Bestow on us, O Dawn, that ample bounty which thou didst send to those who sang thy praises;  Thou whom with bellowings of a bull they quickened: thou didst unbar the firm-set mountain's portals.

7.79.d: देवं-देवं राधसे चोदयन्त्यस्मद्र्यक सून्र्ता ईरयन्ती | वयुछन्ती नः सनये धियो धा यूयं पात ... ||
7.79.e: Impelling every God to grant his bounty sending to us the charm of pleasant voices,  Vouchsafe us thoughts, for profit, as thou breakest. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.

7.80.d: परति सतोमेभिरुषसं वसिष्ठा गीर्भिर्विप्रासः परथमा अबुध्रन | विवर्तयन्तीं रजसी समन्ते आविष्क्र्ण्वतीं भुवनानि विश्वा ||
7.80.e: THE priests, Vasisthas, are the first awakened to welcome Uṣas with their songs and praises,  Who makes surrounding regions part asunder,and shows apparent all existing creatures.
